definition_zh: 有氧的（运动）；需氧的（生物）；靠氧气供能的
definition_en: using oxygen to produce energy over a sustained period; of organisms, requiring oxygen to live; of exercise, strengthening the heart and lungs
core_image: 一边呼吸一边持续燃烧，氧气始终供得上
scene: 跑道上的呼吸声很稳，脚步没有停下来的意思。 Aerobic training keeps the heart working for a long time.
sceneCN: 这里 aerobic 是「有氧的」（第 1 个义项：靠氧气持续供能、能长时间维持的运动）；句意为有氧训练让心脏长时间持续工作。核心画面是氧气始终供得上的持续燃烧。

pos.zh: 有氧的；需氧的

derivatives.zh: 加 -ally 构成，义为「以有氧方式」
加 -s 构成，义为「有氧健身操；有氧运动」
加否定前缀 an- 构成，义为「无氧的；厌氧的」

senses.title: Of exercise, sustained by oxygen
senses.definition: of physical activity that is steady enough for the body to supply oxygen continuously, strengthening heart and lungs
senses.definitionCN: 指强度平稳、身体能持续供氧的体育活动，可增强心肺功能
senses.example: Swimming is one of the best aerobic activities.
senses.exampleCN: 游泳是最好的有氧活动之一。
senses.why: Aer means air and bios means life, so aerobic literally describes life kept going by air: effort you can sustain because breathing keeps up.
senses.whyCN: aer 意为「空气」，bios 意为「生命」，所以 aerobic 字面就是「靠空气维持的生命」：因为呼吸跟得上，这份用力才能持续。

senses.title: Of organisms, needing oxygen to live
senses.definition: of bacteria or other organisms that can live and grow only in the presence of oxygen
senses.definitionCN: 指只有在有氧环境中才能生存繁殖的细菌或其他生物
senses.example: Aerobic bacteria break down the waste in the tank.
senses.exampleCN: 需氧菌分解池中的废物。
senses.why: This is the older scientific sense from Pasteur: the same air-plus-life image applied to a microbe rather than to a runner.
senses.whyCN: 这是来自巴斯德的更早的科学义项：同一个「空气加生命」的意象用在微生物身上，而不是跑者身上。

intro.en: Aerobic was coined for microbiology before it ever reached the gym: air plus life, written in Greek.
intro.cn: aerobic 先为微生物学而造，之后才走进健身房：空气加生命，用希腊语写成。

items.en: Greek aer meant air, the first half of the compound.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 意为「空气」，是复合词的前半。

items.en: Greek bios meant life, and it also gives biology, biography and biosphere.
items.cn: 希腊语 bios 意为「生命」，它也给出 biology、biography 与 biosphere。

items.en: Pasteur used French aérobie in the eighteen sixties for microbes that need free oxygen.
items.cn: 巴斯德在十九世纪六十年代用法语 aérobie 指需要游离氧的微生物。

items.en: English aerobic appeared in the eighteen seventies as the adjective of aerobe, first in biology.
items.cn: 英语 aerobic 于十九世纪七十年代作为 aerobe 的形容词出现，最初用于生物学。

items.en: In the nineteen sixties the word moved into exercise science, naming effort that oxygen can sustain.
items.cn: 二十世纪六十年代该词进入运动科学，指氧气能够支撑的运动强度。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the aero- family and its opposite; the near-meaning group lists words used for the same kind of training.
note.cn: 形近组收 aero- 词族及其反面；近义组收描述同类训练的词语。

entries.definition: Without oxygen; the an- prefix negates aer-.
entries.definitionCN: 无氧的；an- 前缀否定 aer-。

entries.definition: A class or system of aerobic exercise.
entries.definitionCN: 有氧健身操课程或有氧运动体系。

entries.definition: In the air; sharing aer- but not bios.
entries.definitionCN: 在空中的；共享 aer- 但不含 bios。

entries.definition: Relating to heart and blood vessels, often used of the same training.
entries.definitionCN: 与心脏和血管有关的，常指同一类训练。

entries.definition: The ability to keep going for a long time.
entries.definitionCN: 长时间持续下去的能力。

entries.definition: Energetic and forceful, though not necessarily oxygen-sustained.
entries.definitionCN: 精力充沛而有力的，但不一定靠氧气维持。

normalIntro.en: Split aerobic into aer, air, and bic from bios, life: life that runs on air.
normalIntro.cn: 把 aerobic 拆成 aer「空气」与来自 bios「生命」的 bic：靠空气运转的生命。

normal.en: Aer plus bios plus -ic: the adjective of air-life.
normal.cn: aer 加 bios 加 -ic：空气生命的形容词。

normal.en: If you can talk while doing it, it is probably aerobic.
normal.cn: 如果做的时候还能说话，那多半是有氧的。

normal.en: Add an- and you flip it: anaerobic means the oxygen has run out.
normal.cn: 加上 an- 就翻转：anaerobic 表示氧气已跟不上。

normal.en: Aerobic bacteria need air; aerobic exercise gives you more air.
normal.cn: 需氧菌需要空气；有氧运动给你更多空气。

normal.en: The noun aerobics is just this adjective wearing an -s.
normal.cn: 名词 aerobics 就是这个形容词戴上 -s。

abstract.en: Picture a candle burning steadily because the window is open.
abstract.cn: 想象一支蜡烛因窗户开着而稳定燃烧。

abstract.en: Imagine a fire that never smokes because air arrives as fast as it is used.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆从不冒烟的火，因为空气抵达的速度与消耗一样快。

abstract.en: Think of a runner and a microbe sharing one rule: no air, no life.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者与微生物共享一条规则：没有空气，就没有生命。

examples.en: Doctors recommend thirty minutes of aerobic exercise most days.
examples.cn: 医生建议大多数日子进行三十分钟有氧运动。

examples.en: The test measures aerobic capacity on a treadmill.
examples.cn: 该测试在跑步机上测量有氧能力。

examples.en: Aerobic organisms cannot survive in the sealed layer of mud.
examples.cn: 需氧生物无法在密封的泥层中存活。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱肉比克」——爱（ae）肉（ro）比（bi）克（c），爱跑步的肉体靠氧气比拼耐力，就是有氧的。

root: 希腊语 aer「空气」加 bios「生命」构成 aerobic，字面为「靠空气而活的」；十九世纪先用于微生物学，二十世纪转入运动科学，指氧气能持续支撑的强度。

sensesIntro.en: One image covers both senses: life kept going by a steady supply of air, whether in a working muscle or in a bacterium.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个意象覆盖两个义项：靠稳定供气维持的生命，无论是在工作的肌肉里，还是在细菌里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: life sustained by a steady supply of air
core.cn: 核心意象：靠稳定供气维持的生命

branches.en: Muscle burning fuel with enough oxygen.
branches.cn: 肌肉在氧气充足下燃烧燃料。

branches.en: A microbe that lives only with oxygen.
branches.cn: 只有在有氧时才存活的微生物。

branches.en: Both stop when the air stops.
branches.cn: 两者都在断气时停下。

branches.en: Effort paced so breathing keeps up.
branches.cn: 把强度控制在呼吸跟得上的节奏。

branches.en: The opposite is named by adding an-.
branches.cn: 反面由加 an- 来命名。

intro.en: Aerobic is a two-root Greek compound, so its relatives are built by swapping either root or by adding a negating prefix.
intro.cn: aerobic 是双词根的希腊语复合词，因此其亲属词通过替换任一词根或加否定前缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Greek aer and bios travelled through French aérobie into English; Latin had no part in this compound.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 aer 与 bios 经法语 aérobie 进入英语；这个复合词与拉丁语无关。

definition_zh: 机器人学；机器人技术；机器人产业
definition_en: the branch of technology that designs, builds and operates robots
core_image: 车间里几台不同形状的机械臂按同一套程序协同工作，一旁的工程师在平板上调整抓取角度
scene: 比赛场上，学生给四足机器狗输入路线，它自己避开障碍，把小球送到终点。 Modern robotics combines mechanics, electronics and software.
sceneCN: 这里指设计、制造与操控机器人的技术领域（第 1 个义项：机器人技术）；句意：现代机器人技术结合了机械、电子与软件。

pos.zh: 机器人学；机器人技术；机器人产业

derivatives.zh: 源自捷克语「苦役」，义为「机器人」
由「机器人」加形容词尾构成，义为「机器人的、机械的」
由「机器人的」加副词词尾构成，义为「以机械方式」
由「机器人」加动词词尾构成，义为「使机器人化」
由该动词加动作名词尾构成，义为「机器人化」

senses.title: The field of robot technology
senses.definition: the engineering field that studies how robots are designed, controlled and used
senses.definitionCN: 研究机器人如何设计、控制与使用的工程领域
senses.example: Robotics draws on mechanics, electronics and software.
senses.exampleCN: 机器人技术融合机械、电子与软件。
senses.why: The subject ending turns the noun for a robot into the name of the discipline that studies it.
senses.whyCN: 表示学科的结尾把「机器人」这一名词变成研究它的学科名称。

senses.title: The robot industry
senses.definition: the companies, factories and market that produce and sell robots
senses.definitionCN: 生产与销售机器人的公司、工厂与市场
senses.example: Robotics has become a major employer in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 机器人产业已成为该地区的重要雇主。
senses.why: A discipline with commercial products is also named by its field term, so the word can mean the industry.
senses.whyCN: 拥有商业产品的学科也以领域名称指称，因此这个词可以指产业。

senses.title: Designing and building robots
senses.definition: the practical work of creating robot bodies, joints and drives
senses.definitionCN: 创造机器人本体、关节与驱动的实际工作
senses.example: Robotics begins with a frame that can carry its own motors.
senses.exampleCN: 机器人技术从一副能承载自身电机的框架开始。
senses.why: The field is not only theory, so the same word covers the hands-on making of machines.
senses.whyCN: 这一领域不只是理论，因此同一个词也涵盖亲手制造机器的工作。

senses.title: Industrial robot technology
senses.definition: the branch concerned with arms, grippers and production lines
senses.definitionCN: 关注机械臂、夹爪与生产线的分支
senses.example: Industrial robotics changed car assembly more than any other sector.
senses.exampleCN: 工业机器人技术对汽车装配的改变超过任何其他行业。
senses.why: Factories were the first large market, so the branch that serves them is named with a qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 工厂是最早的大市场，因此服务工厂的分支前面加上限定词。

senses.title: Autonomous robot research
senses.definition: the branch that gives robots sensing, planning and independent movement
senses.definitionCN: 赋予机器人感知、规划与自主移动能力的分支
senses.example: Robotics labs now test machines that explore without a map.
senses.exampleCN: 机器人实验室如今在测试没有地图也能探索的机器。
senses.why: Autonomy adds perception and decision, so it forms a distinct research branch within the field.
senses.whyCN: 自主性加入感知与决策，因此在该领域内形成独立的研究分支。

senses.title: Robot control systems
senses.definition: the branch that keeps joints stable and follows planned paths
senses.definitionCN: 保持关节稳定并沿规划路径运动的控制分支
senses.example: Robotics relies on control theory to keep the arm steady.
senses.exampleCN: 机器人技术依靠控制理论让机械臂保持稳定。
senses.why: A machine that moves must be governed, and that governing work is a core part of the field.
senses.whyCN: 会动的机器必须被支配，这一支配工作构成领域的核心部分。

senses.title: Service and medical robotics
senses.titleCN: 服务与医疗机器人技术
senses.definition: the branch that builds robots to assist people in care, surgery or daily tasks
senses.definitionCN: 制造在护理、手术或日常事务中协助人的机器人的分支
senses.example: Medical robotics lets a surgeon work through a tiny opening.
senses.exampleCN: 医疗机器人技术让外科医生通过很小的开口操作。
senses.why: When robots leave the factory floor, the field is named by the service it performs.
senses.whyCN: 当机器人走出车间，领域便以它所提供的服务命名。

senses.title: Robotics in education and competition
senses.titleCN: 教育与竞赛中的机器人技术
senses.definition: the use of robot building as a teaching method and a contest
senses.definitionCN: 把机器人制作用作教学方法与竞赛活动
senses.example: School robotics gives students a reason to learn physics.
senses.exampleCN: 学校机器人活动给学生学习物理的理由。
senses.why: A field that is easy to demonstrate becomes a teaching subject, and the word takes on that role.
senses.whyCN: 易于演示的领域会成为教学科目，这个词也承担起这一角色。

intro.en: Robotics is robot plus the Greek subject ending -ics; robot itself came to English from a Czech play in 1920, built on a word for forced labour.
intro.cn: 这个词由「机器人」加希腊语学科词尾构成；「机器人」本身来自 1920 年一部捷克戏剧，词根源自「苦役」。

items.en: Robota meant forced labour or drudgery, a word tied to the historical system of unpaid service.
items.cn: 这个词意为苦役或繁重劳动，与历史上无偿服役的制度相关。

items.en: A play about manufactured workers used robot for the artificial people, and the word spread quickly in translation.
items.cn: 一部关于人造工人的戏剧用这个词指人造人，该词随译本迅速传播。

items.en: English adopted robot in the 1920s for a machine that performs work, often shaped like a person.
items.cn: 英语在二十世纪二十年代采用这个词，指执行工作、常具人形的机器。

items.en: Writers on machines added the Greek subject ending to robot, producing a name for the field of building and using them.
items.cn: 机器领域的写作者在「机器人」后加希腊语学科词尾，造出研究制造与使用机器人的领域名称。

items.en: Assembly-line arms gave the field its first industry, and later medical and household machines widened it.
items.cn: 装配线机械臂给了这个领域第一个产业，后来的医疗与家用机器又拓宽了它。

items.en: The suggestion of the word robot is generally credited to the playwright's brother, but the attribution rests on later recollection rather than a contemporary record.
items.cn: 「机器人」一词的提议一般归功于剧作家的兄弟，但这一归属依据的是后来的回忆，而非当时的记录。

note.en: The first group shares the robot stem; the second group names neighbouring automation fields.
note.cn: 第一组共享「机器人」词干；第二组是相邻的自动化领域。

entries.definition: A single machine; robotics is the field that designs and uses such machines.
entries.definitionCN: 单台机器；机器人技术是设计与使用这类机器的领域。

entries.definition: Relating to robots, or stiff like one; it describes rather than names the field.
entries.definitionCN: 与机器人有关的，或像机器人一样僵硬；描述而非命名领域。

entries.definition: In a mechanical way; it modifies an action.
entries.definitionCN: 以机械的方式；修饰动作。

entries.definition: To convert a process to robot operation.
entries.definitionCN: 把流程改为机器人操作。

entries.definition: Replacing human work with machines of any kind; robots are one branch of it.
entries.definitionCN: 用任何机器替代人工；机器人只是其中一个分支。

entries.definition: The union of mechanics, electronics and control; it supplies much of the engineering inside robotics.
entries.definitionCN: 机械、电子与控制的结合；为机器人技术提供大量内部工程基础。

entries.definition: The study of control and communication in machines and living things, a theoretical ancestor.
entries.definitionCN: 研究机器与生物中的控制与通信，是理论上的祖先。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Czech labour root, the play and the real branch names.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：捷克语「苦役」词根、那部戏剧与真实分支名称。

normal.en: Robot came from a word for forced labour, and the subject ending makes it a field.
normal.cn: 「机器人」来自表示苦役的词，加上学科词尾就成了一个领域。

normal.en: The family runs robot, robotic, robotically, robotize and robotics.
normal.cn: 同族词有机器人、机器人的、以机械方式、使机器人化与机器人技术。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the sectors: industrial, service and medical robotics.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出行业：工业、服务与医疗机器人技术。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the people: robotics engineer, robotics company, robotics research.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出人与机构：机器人工程师、机器人公司、机器人研究。

normal.en: A 1920 play gave the machine its name, and the factory gave the field its first market.
normal.cn: 1920 年的一部戏剧给了机器名字，工厂给了这个领域第一个市场。

abstract.en: Picture a workforce made of metal that never asks for a break.
abstract.cn: 想象一支金属做的劳动队伍，从不要求休息。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that can be lent to someone across the world.
abstract.cn: 想象一只可以借给世界另一端某人的手。

abstract.en: Picture a body assembled from parts that each know their own job.
abstract.cn: 想象一具由各司其职的部件组装起来的身体。

examples.en: Robotics is one of the fastest-growing engineering fields.
examples.cn: 机器人技术是发展最快的工程领域之一。

examples.en: The lab opened a robotics programme for local schools.
examples.cn: 实验室为当地学校开设了机器人项目。

examples.en: Service robotics now includes machines that deliver medicine.
examples.cn: 服务机器人技术如今包括送药的机器。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「机器人」+「学科」——研究怎么造、怎么用机器人的学问

root: 捷克语「苦役」，1920 年经戏剧进入英语；再加希腊语学科词尾构成机器人技术。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the discipline to the industry, the making, the industrial branch, autonomy, control, service uses and education.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从学科出发，依次到产业、制造、工业分支、自主性、控制、服务用途与教育。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: metal workers assembled from parts, each part given a job by a shared program.
core.cn: 核心意象：由部件组装起来的金属劳动者，每个部件都由同一套程序分派任务。

branches.en: THE FIELD AND THE MAKING: the discipline, and the practical work of building bodies and drives.
branches.cn: 领域与制造：学科，以及建造本体与驱动的实际工作。

branches.en: THE MARKET: companies and factories that make robots a business.
branches.cn: 市场：把机器人变成商业的公司与工厂。

branches.en: THE FACTORY BRANCH: arms, grippers and assembly lines.
branches.cn: 工厂分支：机械臂、夹爪与装配线。

branches.en: SENSE AND GOVERN: autonomy through perception and planning, and the control that keeps motion stable.
branches.cn: 感知与支配：通过感知与规划获得的自主，以及保持运动稳定的控制。

branches.en: PEOPLE OUTSIDE THE FACTORY: care and surgery, and the classroom where the field is taught.
branches.cn: 工厂之外的人：护理与手术，以及讲授这一领域的课堂。

intro.en: Robotics is a Czech-derived noun with a Greek subject ending; the two halves come from very different places.
intro.cn: 这个词以捷克语为词干，配希腊语学科词尾；两半的来源差异很大。

latinIntro.en: Neither half is Latin: robot is Czech and -ics is Greek, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都不是拉丁语：「机器人」来自捷克语，学科词尾来自希腊语，因此拉丁词条留空。

items.example: The root supplies the image of work without choice.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供「无从选择的工作」这一画面。

items.structure: Czech coinage used in a 1920 play
items.example: The noun entered English with the play's success.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词随该剧的成功进入英语。

items.meaning: a field of study or practice
items.example: The ending turns a thing into a discipline.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把某事物变成一门学科。

items.example: The compound names the discipline that builds and uses robots.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词命名建造与使用机器人的学科。

items.example: A robotic arm repeats the same weld.
items.exampleCN: 机械臂重复同一道焊接。

items.example: The hand moved robotically across the bench.
items.exampleCN: 那只手机械地掠过工作台。

items.example: The plant robotized its painting line.

definition_en: A bag carried on the back by two shoulder straps; as a verb, to travel cheaply carrying such a bag.
core_image: 两条肩带把全部家当挂在背上
scene: 他把两天的衣物塞进背包就出门了。 He stuffed two days of clothes into his backpack and left.

senses.title: A bag worn on the back
senses.definition: a bag with two shoulder straps, carried on the back to leave the hands free
senses.definitionCN: 带两条肩带、背在背上以腾出双手的包
senses.example: Her backpack held a tent and a stove.
senses.exampleCN: 她的背包里装着一顶帐篷和一个炉子。
senses.why: Backpack is back plus pack, so it names a load by where it is carried rather than by its shape.
senses.whyCN: backpack 是 back 加 pack，因此它用「背在哪里」而不是形状来命名这份负载。

senses.title: To travel with one
senses.definition: to travel cheaply and independently, carrying one’s belongings in such a bag
senses.definitionCN: 以背包携带行李，廉价而自主地旅行
senses.example: They backpacked across three countries.
senses.exampleCN: 他们背包走过三个国家。
senses.why: The bag came to stand for a whole style of travel, so the noun turned into a verb for that style.
senses.whyCN: 这种包代表了一整种旅行方式，于是名词转为表示该方式的动词。

intro.en: Backpack is back plus pack; pack came through Middle Dutch pakke, of uncertain origin, and the compound is recorded in American English in the 1910s.
intro.cn: backpack 是 back 加 pack；pack 经中古荷兰语 pakke 传入，来源不确定，这个复合词于 1910 年代在美式英语中有记载。

items.en: Old English baec meant the back, the surface that carries a load.
items.cn: 古英语 baec 意为「背」，即承载负荷的那一面。

items.en: Middle Dutch pakke meant a bundle or bale, a word of trade rather than learning.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 pakke 意为「捆、包」，是商贸用语而非学术词。

items.en: Middle English packe named a bundle carried by a person or an animal.
items.cn: 中古英语 packe 指由人或牲畜驮运的捆包。

items.en: American English formed backpack in the 1910s for a bag with shoulder straps.
items.cn: 美式英语在 1910 年代造出 backpack，指带肩带的包。

items.en: The verb meaning to travel with a backpack spread in the 1960s.
items.cn: 表示背包旅行的动词用法在 1960 年代流行开来。

items.en: The noun became standard for school bags and for hiking gear alike.
items.cn: 这个名词同时成为学生书包与徒步装备的标准说法。

definition_zh: 镶嵌艺术；马赛克艺术
definition_en: the art of making pictures and patterns by setting small pieces into a surface
core_image: 一面长墙上，成千上万块碎瓷砖各就各位，拼出远看才显形的一幅大画
scene: 社区中心邀请居民把旧瓷砖敲碎，一起贴在长墙上。 The community invited residents to turn broken tiles into a large wall of mosaic art.
sceneCN: 这里指「以小块材料拼嵌成画面的艺术门类」（第 1 个义项：镶嵌作为一门艺术）；句意为社区邀请居民把碎瓷砖拼成长墙上的镶嵌艺术墙。可辨识物件：碎瓷砖、长墙、胶桶、居民的手。

senses.title: The art form itself
senses.definition: the art of composing images from small pieces of stone, glass or tile set into a surface
senses.definitionCN: 把石头、玻璃或瓷砖的小块嵌进表面、组成画面的艺术
senses.example: The community invited residents to turn broken tiles into mosaic art.
senses.exampleCN: 社区邀请居民把碎瓷砖变成镶嵌艺术。
senses.why: The phrase adds the word for art to the word for the work, so it names the discipline rather than any single object.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语在表示作品的词后面加上「艺术」，因此命名的是门类，而不是某一件成品。

senses.title: Ancient floor tradition
senses.definition: the tradition of decorated floors practised in Greek, Roman and later Mediterranean buildings
senses.definitionCN: 希腊、罗马及后来地中海建筑中装饰地面的传统
senses.example: Ancient mosaic art survives best in the floors of villas.
senses.exampleCN: 古代镶嵌艺术保存得最好的是别墅地面。
senses.why: Floors were the first large surface that could take the technique. The art grew where people walked, not where they looked up.
senses.whyCN: 地面是最早能承载这种技法的大面积表面。这门艺术成长于人行走之处，而不是人抬头仰望之处。

senses.title: Byzantine wall and vault work
senses.titleCN: 拜占庭墙面与穹顶镶嵌
senses.definition: the use of glass mosaic on church walls and vaults to create luminous sacred images
senses.definitionCN: 在教堂墙面与穹顶上用玻璃镶嵌营造发光的神圣图像
senses.example: Byzantine mosaic art fills the vault with gold light.
senses.exampleCN: 拜占庭镶嵌艺术用金光填满穹顶。
senses.why: Glass pieces reflect light from every angle, so the technique moved from the floor to the ceiling, where light could make the image glow.
senses.whyCN: 玻璃小块从各个角度反光，于是这门技法从地面移到天花板，让光把图像点亮。

senses.title: Modern revival
senses.definition: the renewed use of mosaic art by nineteenth and twentieth century designers and architects
senses.definitionCN: 十九、二十世纪设计师与建筑师对镶嵌艺术的重新运用
senses.example: Modern mosaic art returned to public buildings and metro stations.
senses.exampleCN: 现代镶嵌艺术重新回到公共建筑与地铁站。
senses.why: Industrial tiles made the pieces cheap and regular, so architects could cover large modern surfaces with the old technique.
senses.whyCN: 工业生产的瓷砖让小块变得便宜而规整，建筑师因此能用这门古老技法覆盖现代的大面积表面。

senses.title: Community and public work
senses.definition: mosaic art made collectively by residents or volunteers in a public place
senses.definitionCN: 由居民或志愿者在公共场所共同完成的镶嵌艺术
senses.example: The school's mosaic art project gave every pupil one tile.
senses.exampleCN: 学校的镶嵌艺术项目让每个学生负责一块瓷砖。
senses.why: The technique naturally divides a picture into many small tasks, so it suits a group where each person contributes one piece.
senses.whyCN: 这种技法天然把一幅画拆成许多小任务，因此适合每人负责一块的集体创作。

senses.title: Studio craft and teaching
senses.definition: mosaic art as a taught craft practised in studios with cutters, nippers and adhesives
senses.definitionCN: 作为可教授的手艺，在工作室里借助切割器、钳子与黏合剂来制作
senses.example: She teaches mosaic art to adults on Saturday mornings.
senses.exampleCN: 她周六上午教成年人镶嵌艺术。
senses.why: Once the work became a subject in art schools, the phrase named a course and a set of tools rather than a monument.
senses.whyCN: 当这门作品成为艺术学校的科目后，这个短语就指一门课程与一套工具，而不再指某座纪念碑。

senses.title: Digital photographic mosaic
senses.definition: a digital form in which many small photographs are arranged to form a larger image
senses.definitionCN: 把许多小照片排布成更大图像的数字形式
senses.example: Digital mosaic art builds a portrait from hundreds of snapshots.
senses.exampleCN: 数字镶嵌艺术用数百张快照拼出一幅肖像。
senses.why: The computer repeats the old logic without stone: each small image is complete in itself, yet together they form one face.
senses.whyCN: 计算机不用石头却重复了旧逻辑：每张小图自身完整，合起来却构成一张脸。

senses.title: Architectural surface design
senses.definition: the integration of mosaic art into the surfaces of a building as part of its design
senses.definitionCN: 把镶嵌艺术整合进建筑表面，作为建筑设计的一部分
senses.example: Mosaic art turns the station wall into a map of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 镶嵌艺术把车站墙面变成一幅河流地图。
senses.why: Because the pieces are fixed to the structure, the art can act as skin. This sense joins the craft back to architecture.
senses.whyCN: 因为小块被固定在结构上，艺术可以充当皮肤。这一义项把这门工艺重新接回建筑。

intro.en: Mosaic art joins two borrowings: mosaic, which came through French and Italian from a Latin word for mosaic work, and art, which came through Old French from Latin ars 'skill'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mosaic art 由两个借词组合而成：mosaic 经法语与意大利语来自一个表示镶嵌作品的拉丁词，art 经古法语来自拉丁 ars「技艺」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin ars (genitive artis) meant 'skill, craft, method'. Its deeper origin is source uncertain; a link to a root meaning 'to fit together' is a reconstructed form, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 拉丁 ars（属格 artis）意为「技艺、手艺、方法」。其更深来源属「来源不确定」；把它连到某个意为「拼合」的词根，只是重构形式，并非有记录的真实词形。

items.en: Old French art carried both 'skill' and 'knowledge' into English, where the word long meant learned technique before it narrowed to the fine arts.
items.cn: 古法语 art 把「技艺」与「知识」两层意思带进英语；这个词长期指习得的技法，后来才收窄到美术。

items.en: Latin musa 'muse' and the late Latin adjective musaicus are generally believed to stand behind mosaic, although the exact chain from the Muse to stonework is not settled.
items.cn: 拉丁 musa「缪斯」与晚期拉丁形容词 musaicus 一般认为与 mosaic 有关，但从缪斯到石头工艺的确切链条并未定论。

items.en: Italian mosaico and French mosaïque supplied the English noun in the sixteenth century, first for decorated floors and walls.
items.cn: 意大利语 mosaico 与法语 mosaïque 在十六世纪提供了英语名词，最初指装饰过的地面与墙面。

items.en: The compound mosaic art appears in art writing once mosaics were discussed as a discipline with its own history and schools.
items.cn: 当镶嵌被当作一门有自身历史与流派的手艺来讨论时，复合词 mosaic art 才出现在艺术写作中。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin history of both ars and musa is unsettled, and the route from the Muse to mosaic remains a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定：ars 与 musa 在拉丁语之前的历史都无定论，而从缪斯到 mosaic 的路径仍属假说，并非已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one holds compounds that share the mosaic word but name other things; group two holds names for related art forms.
note.cn: 第一组是共用 mosaic 一词、却指别的事物的复合词；第二组是相邻艺术门类的名称。

entries.definition: the single word names a work or the craft in general; the longer phrase names the art as a discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 单词形式指一件作品或笼统的工艺；较长的短语则把镶嵌当作一门艺术门类。

entries.definition: one small piece of tile used in the technique; it is a material, not an art form.
entries.definitionCN: 这门技法使用的一小块瓷砖；它是材料，不是艺术门类。

entries.definition: a decorated floor made in this technique; it names a place or object, not the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 用这种技法做的装饰地面；它指场所或物件，而非学科。

entries.definition: a person who makes mosaics; it names the maker rather than the art.
entries.definitionCN: 制作镶嵌画的人；它指创作者，而非艺术本身。

entries.definition: the finished picture or pattern; mosaic art is the discipline that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 完成的画面或图案；镶嵌艺术则是产出它的那门学科。

entries.definition: a pattern of shapes fitted together without gaps or overlaps; it stresses geometry rather than picture-making.
entries.definitionCN: 形状无缝无叠地拼合的图案；强调几何，而非造像。

entries.definition: the craft of setting contrasting material into a hollowed surface; it is a technique cousin with a narrower material range.
entries.definitionCN: 把对比材料嵌进挖空表面的工艺；是技法上的近亲，材料范围更窄。

entries.definition: wall painting done on fresh lime plaster; it shares the architectural setting but uses paint, not pieces.
entries.definitionCN: 在未干石灰层上作的壁画；同样依附建筑，但用颜料而非小块。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The phrase is simply the noun for the work plus the noun for skill: the skill of making mosaics.
normal.cn: 这个短语就是把表示作品的词与表示技艺的词并在一起：制作镶嵌画的技艺。

normal.en: Art goes back to Latin ars 'skill', so mosaic art is literally the skill of setting pieces.
normal.cn: art 上溯到拉丁 ars「技艺」，因此这个短语字面上就是「嵌置小块的技艺」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort its periods: ancient, Byzantine, modern, public.
normal.cn: 固定搭配按时期分类：古代的、拜占庭的、现代的、公共的。

normal.en: A mosaic artist is the person; mosaic art is the field.
normal.cn: mosaic artist 指人；mosaic art 指领域。

normal.en: The plural mosaic arts names the branches taught under one heading.
normal.cn: 复数形式指同一名目下所教的各个分支。

abstract.en: Picture a classroom where thirty children each hold one coloured square and the picture appears only when all stand together.
abstract.cn: 想象一间教室，三十个孩子各拿一块彩色方片，只有全部站到一起，图画才出现。

abstract.en: Picture a wall that changes colour as you walk past because each tiny piece turns the light differently.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙，你走过时颜色不断变化，因为每颗小片反光的角度都不同。

abstract.en: Picture an art that cannot be moved without becoming rubble.
abstract.cn: 想象一门艺术，一旦搬动就会变成碎石。

examples.en: Roman mosaic art spread with the legions across the empire.
examples.cn: 罗马镶嵌艺术随军团传遍帝国。

examples.en: The city commissioned mosaic art for the new metro entrance.
examples.cn: 市政府为新地铁入口委约了镶嵌艺术。

examples.en: Students learn mosaic art by copying a small Byzantine panel.
examples.cn: 学生通过临摹一小块拜占庭镶嵌板来学习镶嵌艺术。

root: 由 mosaic 与 art 组合：mosaic 经法语、意大利语上溯至晚期拉丁 musaicus，一般认为与缪斯有关但链条不确定；art 经古法语上溯至拉丁 ars「技艺」，其更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one discipline through its settings: it begins as a named art, moves from ancient floors to Byzantine vaults, is revived by modern architects, practised by communities and studios, rebuilt digitally, and finally treated as the skin of a building.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一门艺术穿过不同场景：它先被命名为一门艺术，从古代地面走到拜占庭穹顶，被现代建筑师复兴，由社区与工作室实践，再以数字方式重建，最后被当作建筑的皮肤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one wall made of thousands of separate pieces, readable only when they are all in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面由成千上万小块组成的墙，只有全部就位才读得成画。

branches.en: THE NAME: the phrase first sets the craft apart as an art with a history.
branches.cn: 名目：这个短语首先把这门工艺确立为一门有历史的艺术。

branches.en: FROM FLOOR TO VAULT: the same technique moves from the ground people walk on to the ceiling they look up at.
branches.cn: 从地面到穹顶：同一技法从人脚下的地面移到人仰望的天花板。

branches.en: ART IN ARCHITECTURE: modern revival and surface design both put the craft back onto buildings.
branches.cn: 建筑中的艺术：现代复兴与表面设计都把工艺重新放回建筑上。

branches.en: HANDS AND TEACHING: community projects and studio classes turn the art into shared practice.
branches.cn: 手与教学：社区项目与工作室课程把这门艺术变成共同实践。

branches.en: DIGITAL COUNTERPART: photographs replace stone while the rule of small units stays the same.
branches.cn: 数字对应物：照片取代石头，而小单元拼合的规则保持不变。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two old borrowings, one for the work and one for skill, and both carry large families into English.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个古老借词构成，一个表示作品，一个表示技艺，两者都为英语带来庞大的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ars and Latin musa stand behind the two halves; art, artist, artistic and artisan come from the first, while mosaic and museum come from the second.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ars 与拉丁 musa 分别是两半的来源；art、artist、artistic 与 artisan 出自前者，mosaic 与 museum 出自后者。

items.example: Ars names learned skill rather than mere labour.
items.exampleCN: ars 指习得的技艺，而不只是体力劳动。

items.example: Art once meant any learned skill.
items.exampleCN: art 原指任何习得的技艺。

items.example: The artist works in glass and stone.
items.exampleCN: 这位艺术家用玻璃与石头创作。

items.example: The mosaic has real artistic value.
items.exampleCN: 这幅镶嵌画有真正的艺术价值。

items.example: The artisan cuts each tile by hand.
items.exampleCN: 工匠亲手切割每一块砖。

items.meaning: an object made by human skill
items.example: The floor yielded many small artifacts.
items.exampleCN: 这处地面出土了许多小件人工制品。

items.structure: Italian mosaico, from late Latin musaicus
items.meaning: a picture set in small pieces
items.example: The mosaic fills the apse.
items.exampleCN: 镶嵌画铺满半圆殿。

items.example: The mosaicist planned the colour scheme.
items.exampleCN: 镶嵌师规划了配色。

items.example: Mosaic art is taught in the studio.
items.exampleCN: 工作室教授镶嵌艺术。

items.meaning: a person who practises mosaic art
items.example: The mosaic artist worked on site.
items.exampleCN: 镶嵌艺术家在现场创作。

definition_zh: adj. 失职的；有过失的；（尤指青少年）违法的；拖欠的 n. 违法者（尤指青少年）；失职者
definition_en: failing in a duty or breaking the law, especially of a young person; such a person
core_image: 一个少年站在打碎的橱窗前，手里还握着石子，警察的记录本翻开新的一页
scene: 那个失职的官员被停职了。 The delinquent officer was suspended.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：delinquent 指失职的；句意是那个失职的官员被停职了。

pos.zh: 失职的；有过失的；（尤指青少年）违法的；拖欠的
违法者（尤指青少年）；失职者

senses.title: Failing a duty
senses.definition: not doing what a job or a duty requires
senses.definitionCN: 没有做到工作或职责要求的事
senses.example: The delinquent officer was suspended.
senses.exampleCN: 那个失职的官员被停职了。
senses.why: A badge left on an empty desk.
senses.whyCN: 一枚留在空桌上的徽章。

senses.title: Breaking the law
senses.definition: committing minor crimes, especially of a young person
senses.definitionCN: 犯下轻微罪行，尤指年轻人
senses.example: The programme helps delinquent teenagers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目帮助违法的少年。
senses.why: A stone still warm in a young hand.
senses.whyCN: 一只年轻手里还温热的石子。

senses.title: A young offender
senses.definition: a young person who commits minor crimes
senses.definitionCN: 犯下轻微罪行的年轻人
senses.example: The court sent the delinquent to a youth centre.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭把这名少年犯送到青少年中心。
senses.why: A name written on a police file.
senses.whyCN: 写在警方档案上的一个名字。

senses.title: Overdue
senses.definition: not paid by the date required
senses.definitionCN: 未在规定日期前支付的
senses.example: They collected the delinquent taxes.
senses.exampleCN: 他们收上了拖欠的税款。
senses.why: An invoice stamped past due.
senses.whyCN: 一张盖着逾期章的发票。

intro.en: Delinquent comes from Latin delinquens, the participle of delinquere, to leave a duty undone.
intro.cn: delinquent 源自拉丁语 delinquens，是 delinquere（把职责留下不做）的分词。

items.en: Linquere meant to leave.
items.cn: linquere 意为留下、离开。

items.en: Delinquere meant to leave a duty undone.
items.cn: delinquere 意为把职责留下不做。

items.en: Delinquens meant failing in duty.
items.cn: delinquens 意为失职的。

items.en: Delinquent entered English as an adjective for fault.
items.cn: 十六世纪 delinquent 以有过失的形容词义进入英语。

items.en: It became a noun for a young offender.
items.cn: 十八世纪成为指少年犯的名词。

items.en: It also described payments left overdue.
items.cn: 它也用来描述逾期未付的款项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the linqu- leaving family; the near-meaning group names other kinds of failing.
note.cn: 形近组共享 linqu-（留下）家族；近义组是其他「没做到」的说法。

entries.definition: The state of failing a duty or breaking the law.
entries.definitionCN: 失职；违法行为。

entries.definition: To give up or hand over something.
entries.definitionCN: 放弃；交出。

entries.definition: Left empty and uncared for, or failing a duty.
entries.definitionCN: 废弃的；失职的。

entries.definition: Not taking proper care.
entries.definitionCN: 疏忽的。

entries.definition: Breaking a rule or a law.
entries.definitionCN: 违规的；冒犯的。

entries.definition: Not done or paid by the expected time.
entries.definitionCN: 逾期的。

normalIntro.en: Delinquent is de- plus linqu- leave plus -ent: the one who leaves the duty undone.
normalIntro.cn: delinquent 就是 de- 加 linqu-（留下）加 -ent：把职责留下不做的那个人。

normal.en: Linqu- means to leave.
normal.cn: linqu- 意为留下。

normal.en: -ent marks the doer or the quality.
normal.cn: -ent 表示做事的人或性质。

normal.en: A delinquent officer leaves the duty.
normal.cn: 失职的官员把职责留下了。

normal.en: A juvenile delinquent is a young offender.
normal.cn: juvenile delinquent 指少年犯。

normal.en: Delinquent taxes are taxes left unpaid.
normal.cn: delinquent taxes 是被留下未缴的税。

abstract.en: A stone still warm in a young hand.

abstract.en: A name written on a police file.

examples.en: The delinquent taxes were finally paid.
examples.cn: 拖欠的税款终于缴清了。

examples.en: Two delinquents were given community work.
examples.cn: 两名少年犯被判社区劳动。

examples.en: He was delinquent in reporting the fault.
examples.cn: 他在报告故障这件事上失职了。

dict_mnemonic.text: delinquent 谐音「弟林昆特」——不如记 de（离开）＋ linqu（留下）＋ ent（…的／…者）＝把该做的留下不做的人，「失职的、违法者」。

root: 拉丁语 linquere（留下）→ delinquere（失职）→ delinquens（失职的）→ 英语 delinquent

sensesIntro.en: One duty left: an officer, a teenager, a name on file and a late bill.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一件被留下的职责：一名官员、一个少年、档案上的名字与一张逾期账单。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a teenager before a broken shop window, a stone still in his hand

branches.en: A badge left on an empty desk.

intro.cn: delinquent 由 de- 加 linqu- 加 -ent 构成；留下这个词根造出过失一族词。

definition_zh: 民谣；叙事歌谣；伤感情歌
definition_en: a narrative song passed among people, or a slow sentimental love song
core_image: 一把琴走村串巷，把故事唱给不会写字的人听
scene: 火塘边老人抱着琴，孩子们围坐着听故事被唱出来。 The old man sang a ballad about the shipwreck.
sceneCN: 这里 ballad 指「叙事民谣」（第 1 个义项：用歌讲述故事的民谣）；句意：老人唱了一首关于海难的民谣。

pos.zh: 民谣；叙事歌谣；流行情歌
以民谣形式唱述（罕用）

collocations.zh: 劲抒情歌（摇滚乐队慢歌）
边境歌谣（苏格兰边区传统）

derivatives.zh: 三节同韵诗体（法语借回的近亲词）
民谣歌剧（18 世纪英国用流行曲调填词的歌剧）

senses.title: A narrative folk song
senses.definition: a song that tells a story, passed on orally among ordinary people
senses.definitionCN: 以歌讲故事的歌谣，在民间口耳相传
senses.example: The ballad of the outlaw spread from tavern to tavern.
senses.exampleCN: 那首亡命徒的歌谣从小酒馆传到小酒馆。
senses.why: Before print, dancing and singing carried the news, and the dance word named the song.
senses.whyCN: 印刷术之前，消息靠歌舞传递，舞蹈一词顺势为歌命名。

senses.title: A literary poem in song form
senses.definition: a poem imitating the folk song, with stanzas, refrain, and a story
senses.definitionCN: 仿民歌的歌谣体诗，有分节、叠句与故事
senses.example: Keats wrote his ballad about the knight in purple light.
senses.exampleCN: 济慈以歌谣体写了那首紫光中骑士的诗。
senses.why: Poets borrowed the folk form once print made songs into literature.
senses.whyCN: 印刷术把歌变成文学后，诗人反过来借用民间形式。

senses.title: A slow love song
senses.definition: in popular music, a slow, emotional song, usually about love
senses.definitionCN: 流行乐中指缓慢深情的歌曲，多为情歌
senses.example: The band closed the concert with a tender ballad.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队以一首温柔的情歌结束演唱会。
senses.why: Tin Pan Alley kept the song-sheet habit, and the word softened into sentiment.
senses.whyCN: 流行歌业沿用了印歌卖歌的旧俗，这个词随之柔化为「深情慢歌」。

senses.title: The refrain form
senses.definition: a song structure of four-line stanzas with a repeated refrain
senses.definitionCN: 以四行诗节加反复副歌构成的歌体
senses.example: The ballad's refrain stayed in the child's head all night.
senses.exampleCN: 那首歌的叠句在孩子脑海里回荡了一夜。
senses.why: Memory is the singer's tool, and the refrain is the hook memory bites.
senses.whyCN: 歌手靠记忆谋生，叠句正是记忆咬住的钩子。

senses.title: A news song
senses.definition: a song reporting a recent event, murder, battle, or scandal
senses.definitionCN: 报道凶案、战役或丑闻等时事的歌曲
senses.example: Printers sold a fresh ballad the morning after the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 火灾次日清晨，印刷商就卖起了新编的时事歌。
senses.why: Broadside sheets were the newspapers of the illiterate world.
senses.whyCN: 传单歌页就是不识字时代的报纸。

senses.title: The heroic ballad
senses.definition: a ballad celebrating heroes, battles, or clan deeds
senses.definitionCN: 歌颂英雄、战役或氏族功业的歌谣
senses.example: Border ballads kept the riders' feuds alive for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 边境歌谣让骑手的世仇传唱了数百年。
senses.why: Some old ballads began as epics, cut down to fit a tune.
senses.whyCN: 一些古老歌谣本由史诗裁短，以合曲调。

senses.title: The ballet root, dancing
senses.definition: in the word's first life, a song sung while dancing
senses.definitionCN: 词的初义：边舞边唱的歌
senses.example: French wrote the dance-song as ballade before English kept it as ballad.
senses.exampleCN: 法语把舞歌写作 ballade，英语保留为 ballad。
senses.why: The Latin root is ballare, to dance; the song was first the dance's voice.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根是 ballare「跳舞」；歌最初是舞蹈的嗓音。

senses.title: Balladry, the whole tradition
senses.definition: in balladry, the body of ballads and the art of writing them
senses.definitionCN: 集合词 balladry，指歌谣总体与歌谣创作艺术
senses.example: Scottish balladry shaped the whole romantic revival.
senses.exampleCN: 苏格兰歌谣传统滋养了整场浪漫主义复兴。
senses.why: Collect the songs and the collection earns its own name.
senses.whyCN: 歌攒成传统，传统便自己挣得一个名字。

intro.en: Ballad comes from Old French balade, a dancing song, from Provençal balada, from Latin ballare, to dance; English took the word in the fifteenth century, first for songs to dance by, later for the narrative songs collectors recorded.
intro.cn: ballad 出自古法语 balade「舞歌」，经普罗旺斯语 balada 上溯拉丁语 ballare「跳舞」；英语 15 世纪借入，先指伴舞之歌，后指采录的叙事歌谣。

items.en: The reconstructed root *gweh- meant to leap and dance.
items.cn: 重构词根 *gweh- 意为跳跃、起舞。

items.en: ballare named dancing; it also gives ballet through Italian.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ballare 指跳舞；经意大利语也派生出 ballet。

items.en: balada was a song for dancing, with -ada as the action ending.
items.cn: 普罗旺斯语 balada 指伴舞之歌，-ada 为动作名词尾。

items.en: balade named both the dance song and the three-stanza poem form.
items.cn: 古法语 balade 兼指舞歌与三节同韵诗体。

items.en: English borrowed the word, spelling it ballad or balade.
items.cn: 英语借入该词，拼作 ballad 或 balade。

items.en: Broadside ballads sold street news, collectors gathered the folk ballads, and pop music finally turned the word to slow love songs.
items.cn: 16 至 19 世纪间，传单歌贩卖街闻，学者采录民歌；至流行乐时代，此词终指慢速情歌。

note.en: Group one holds the dance-root family and look-alikes; group two holds the song-and-story field.
note.cn: 第一组收舞根词族与形近词；第二组收歌与故事义场的词。

entries.definition: the fixed three-stanza poem form, kept in French spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 三节同韵的定式诗体，保留法语拼写。

entries.definition: a staged dance; from the same Latin ballare through Italian.
entries.definitionCN: 舞台舞蹈；同出拉丁语 ballare，经意大利语而来。

entries.definition: ship's gravel weight; from Scandinavian, only the spelling misleads.
entries.definitionCN: 船之压舱石；出自斯堪的纳维亚语，仅拼写相近，词源无关。

entries.definition: of projectiles; from Greek ballein, to throw.
entries.definitionCN: 弹道的；出自希腊语 ballein「投掷」。

entries.definition: brave or courtly; from French galant, one letter apart.
entries.definitionCN: 英勇或殷勤的；出自法语 galant，仅一字母之差。

entries.definition: a long heroic narrative; the ballad's grand cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 长篇英雄叙事诗；歌谣的宏大表亲。

entries.definition: a song of praise, religious in the main line.
entries.definitionCN: 赞美之歌；多指宗教颂歌。

entries.definition: a slow mourning song.
entries.definitionCN: 哀歌；挽歌。

entries.definition: a solemn or rousing communal song.
entries.definitionCN: 颂歌；庄重或振奋人心的合唱曲。

entries.definition: a traditional tale; the story the ballad often sings.
entries.definitionCN: 传说；歌谣所唱的故事本身。

normalIntro.en: ballad is ballet's song: both come from Latin ballare, to dance.
normalIntro.cn: ballad 是 ballet 的歌：两者同出拉丁语 ballare「跳舞」。

normal.en: ballare, to dance, is the root; ballet is its cousin.
normal.cn: 词根是 ballare「跳舞」；ballet 是它的表亲。

normal.en: A ballad tells a story in stanzas with a refrain.
normal.cn: ballad 用分节加叠句讲一个故事。

normal.en: Ballade with an e is the strict French poem form.
normal.cn: 带 e 的 ballade 是严格的法语诗体。

normal.en: Power ballad: a rock band's slow, loud love song.
normal.cn: power ballad 指摇滚乐队的劲抒情歌。

normal.en: Balladry, with -ry, names the whole song tradition.
normal.cn: 加 -ry 的 balladry 指整个歌谣传统。

abstract.en: See firelight move while the story walks by foot through the dark.
abstract.cn: 看火光摇曳，故事赤脚走夜路。

abstract.en: A ballad is news set to a beat, so nobody forgets it.
abstract.cn: ballad 是配了节拍的消息，让人忘不掉。

abstract.en: Hear the refrain return like a wave, and carry the story out again.
abstract.cn: 听叠句如浪回返，把故事再送出去一遍。

examples.en: Collectors recorded every ballad the shepherds still sang.
examples.cn: 采集者把牧人仍在吟唱的歌谣一一录下。

examples.en: The album's quietest track is a bare ballad for voice and piano.
examples.cn: 专辑里最安静的一首是仅有嗓音与钢琴的抒情曲。

examples.en: Ballad singers once made a living on the week's disasters.
examples.cn: 当年的歌谣歌手靠一周的灾祸卖唱为生。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伴来的」——跳舞时伴来的歌，边跳边唱就是歌谣

root: 出自拉丁语 ballare「跳舞」（上溯原始印欧语 *gweh-「跳跃」），经普罗旺斯语 balada「伴舞之歌」、古法语 balade 进入英语；与 ballet 同根异路：ballet 经意大利语 balletto 留在舞，ballad 留在歌；后世歌从舞中独立，遂成叙事民谣与慢速情歌。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses dance out of one root: the song for dancing, the song for telling, the printed news song, the hero's song, the love song, the refrain form, the tradition, and the old root itself.
