definition_zh: 不可或缺的；完整的；固有的；整数的；积分；（古）正直的
definition_en: forming an essential part of a whole, or being whole and complete in itself; (n.) a mathematical integral, or a whole number
core_image: 一块拼图正好卡在整幅画的正中央——抽走它，画面就永远缺一角
scene: 这里指「不可或缺的」。 Trust is an integral part of any long partnership.
sceneCN: 这里 integral 是「不可或缺的」（第 01 个义项：作为整体必需的一部分）；句意：信任是任何长期伙伴关系中不可或缺的一部分。画面里那块拼图卡在中央，四周的图都靠它才连成一片。

pos.zh: 不可或缺的；完整的；固有的；整数的
积分；整体；整数

collocations.zh: 某事物不可或缺的一部分

senses.title: Essential part: the piece the whole needs
senses.titleCN: 不可或缺：整体少不得的那一块
senses.definition: necessary to make a whole complete; belonging to something as one of its essential parts
senses.definitionCN: 为使整体完整所必需的；作为本质组成部分属于某事物的
senses.example: Teamwork is an integral part of the job.
senses.exampleCN: 团队合作是这份工作不可或缺的一部分。
senses.why: Latin integralis meant 'forming a whole'. A part is integral when the whole would no longer be whole without it: the piece is not an extra but a condition of completeness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 integralis 意为“构成一个整体”。当缺了它整体就不再完整时，这一部分就是 integral：它不是附加物，而是完整性的条件。

senses.title: Whole and complete: nothing missing
senses.definition: whole, complete, and undivided; having all its parts present
senses.definitionCN: 完整的、齐全的、未被分割的；所有部分都在
senses.example: The archive holds an integral set of the letters, with none missing.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆藏有这批信件完整的一套，一封不缺。
senses.why: English used integral in the Latin sense 'whole, entire' from about 1500. The base integer is literally 'untouched': a thing with no part taken away is a thing that is whole.
senses.whyCN: 大约从 1500 年起，英语就用 integral 表达拉丁语的“完整、全部”。词基 integer 字面是“未被碰过”：没有哪一部分被拿走的东西，就是完整的东西。

senses.title: Built in: intrinsic to the thing itself
senses.definition: belonging naturally to something as part of its own nature, not added from outside
senses.definitionCN: 作为某物本性的一部分天然属于它，而非从外部添加
senses.example: The lens is integral to the camera, not an accessory.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚镜头是相机固有的部分，不是配件。
senses.why: The late 15c. sense was 'intrinsic, belonging as a part to a whole'. If a part belongs to the whole by nature, it is already inside the definition of the thing, not bolted on later.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪后期的义项是“内在的、作为一部分属于整体的”。如果一个部分天然属于整体，它就已经在这件事物的定义之内，而不是后来拧上去的。

senses.title: Calculus: the sum of infinitely many slices
senses.titleCN: 积分：把无穷多小片加起来
senses.definition: a mathematical quantity obtained by summing infinitely many infinitesimal parts; the result of integration
senses.definitionCN: 把无穷多个无穷小部分相加而得到的数学量；积分运算的结果
senses.example: She evaluated the integral from zero to one in a single step.
senses.exampleCN: 她一步就算出了从 0 到 1 的积分。
senses.why: The noun is recorded from the 1610s, and calculus fixed it as the name of a total built from infinitesimal pieces. The mathematical operation is still 'making a whole' out of slices, so it keeps the oldest image.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词在 17 世纪 10 年代已有记录，微积分把它固定为“由无穷小片拼成的总量”的名称。这个运算仍然是把切片“做成整体”，所以保留着最古老的画面。

senses.title: Whole-number: values that do not split
senses.definition: in mathematics, involving or consisting of whole numbers rather than fractions
senses.definitionCN: 数学中涉及或由整数而非分数构成的
senses.example: The equation has an integral solution, x = 4.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方程有一个整数解 x = 4。
senses.why: Integer, 'a whole number', is recorded from the 1570s. An integral solution is one that lands exactly on a whole number, with no fraction left over: again the idea is a value that is complete in itself.
senses.whyCN: integer“整数”自 16 世纪 70 年代有记录。integral solution 指恰好落在一个整数上的解，不剩分数：仍然是“自身完整”的那个想法。

senses.title: Indivisible: one unit that cannot be split
senses.titleCN: 不可分割：拆开就失去它本身的一个单元
senses.definition: forming a single undivided unit whose parts cannot be separated without destroying it
senses.definitionCN: 构成一个不可分割的整体；各部分一旦分开，该整体就不复存在
senses.example: The two departments now operate as an integral unit.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个部门现在作为一个不可分割的整体运作。
senses.why: Integer literally means 'untouched, whole'. An integral unit is one whose parts have not been cut apart; to divide it is to stop it being what it is.
senses.whyCN: integer 字面是“未被触碰、完整”。an integral unit 就是各部分没有被切开的一个单元；把它分开，它就不再是原来的东西。

senses.title: Calculus: the branch that sums wholes
senses.titleCN: 积分学的：把无穷小片加回整体的那套运算
senses.definition: of or relating to mathematical integration, as in integral calculus
senses.definitionCN: 与数学积分有关的，如 integral calculus（积分学）
senses.example: She signed up for a course in integral calculus.
senses.exampleCN: 她报名了一门积分学课程。
senses.why: The noun integral (1610s) named a whole built by summing parts; the adjective then labelled the calculus that computes such wholes.
senses.whyCN: 名词 integral（17 世纪 10 年代）指把各部分加起来所得的整量；形容词随后用来标记计算这种整量的那门微积分。

senses.title: The whole itself: a complete entity
senses.titleCN: 整体本身：一个完整的存在
senses.definition: a whole considered as a single complete entity (now rare)
senses.definitionCN: 被视为单一完整实体的整体（今罕用）
senses.example: The essay treats the city as one integral rather than a set of districts.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章把这座城市当作一个整体，而不是一组城区。
senses.why: The noun is recorded from the 1610s as a use of the adjective: what is integral can be named as the integral, the whole thing itself. Modern English prefers whole in this sense, leaving integral mostly to mathematics.
senses.whyCN: 名词在 17 世纪 10 年代由形容词转用而来：完整的东西可以被叫作“那个整体”，即整体本身。现代英语在这个义项上更常用 whole，把 integral 大体留给了数学。

senses.title: Whole-making view: seeing the parts as one design
senses.titleCN: 整体化视角：把各部分看成一个设计
senses.definition: combining all parts into a single coherent view or design, rather than treating them separately
senses.definitionCN: 把所有部分结合成一个连贯的视角或设计，而非分开处理
senses.example: The plan takes an integral view of transport, housing and schools.
senses.exampleCN: 这个规划对交通、住房和学校采取整体化的视角。
senses.why: The modern 'integral approach' extends the old whole-making base from things to methods. When a way of thinking leaves nothing outside, the method itself becomes integral: it makes its object whole.
senses.whyCN: 现代的 integral approach 把古老的“使成整体”词基从事物扩展到方法。当一种思路不把任何东西留在外面，方法本身也就成了 integral：它在把对象做成整体。

intro.en: Integral comes from Medieval Latin integralis 'forming a whole', from Latin integer 'whole, complete', literally 'untouched' — in- 'not' plus the root of tangere 'to touch'. Old French intégral passed it to English in the late 15c., first as an adjective, then as a noun in the 1610s.
intro.cn: integral 来自中世纪拉丁语 integralis“构成一个整体的”，再上溯拉丁语 integer“完整的、完全的”，字面“未被碰过”——in-“不”加上 tangere“触碰”的词根。古法语 intégral 在 15 世纪后期把它传给英语，先作形容词，17 世纪 10 年代再作名词。

items.en: Integer meant 'intact, whole, complete' and figuratively 'untainted, upright', literally 'untouched': in- 'not' plus the root of tangere 'to touch'. The PIE root *tag- 'to touch, handle' behind tangere is a reconstructed form with no written record, so that deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: integer 意为“完好的、完整的、完全的”，比喻义为“未受污染的、正直的”，字面是“未被碰过”：in-“不”加上 tangere“触碰”的词根。tangere 背后的原始印欧词根 *tag-“触摸、把持”是重构形式，没有书面记录，因此更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Integralis 'forming a whole' was built on integer for scholastic and mathematical writing. The word names not just a whole thing but the quality of making or belonging to a whole.
items.cn: integralis“构成一个整体的”在中世纪拉丁语的经院与数学写作中由 integer 构成。这个词不只命名一个完整之物，也命名“构成整体”或“属于整体”的性质。

items.en: Old French intégral carried the adjective sense 'whole, complete'. French also gave English the noun integer through Latin, so the whole family arrived in two waves.
items.cn: 古法语 intégral 带有形容词义“完整的、完全的”。法语也通过拉丁语把名词 integer 给了英语，因此整个词族分两波到达。

items.en: English records integral as 'of or pertaining to a whole; intrinsic, belonging as a part to a whole'. From the start it points two ways at once: the whole, and the part that the whole requires.
items.cn: 英语记录 integral 为“与整体有关的；内在的、作为一部分属于整体的”。它从一开始就同时指向两头：整体，以及整体所必需的那一部分。

items.en: The noun appears in the 1610s, formed from the adjective. In 17c. calculus the same word became the name of a total summed from infinitesimal parts; the exact first written date of that technical use is not recorded in the standard etymology.
items.cn: 名词在 17 世纪 10 年代由形容词构成。17 世纪微积分里，同一个词成为“由无穷小部分相加而成的总量”的名称；这一专科用法的确切最早书面年代，标准词源记录未载。

items.en: Modern usage settles into 'an integral part of' and 'integral to', and mathematical 'integral solution' draws on integer 'whole number' (1570s). The untouched whole and the necessary part now live in one word.
items.cn: 现代用法固定为 an integral part of 与 integral to；数学的 integral solution 则取自 integer“整数”（16 世纪 70 年代）。未受碰触的整体与必需的那一部分，如今住在同一个词里。

note.en: The first group is the integer family: same Latin base, different endings and meanings. The second group approaches integral from the side of meaning, where whole, essential and built-in overlap.
note.cn: 第一组是 integer 词族：同一个拉丁词基，不同的词尾与词义。第二组从词义一侧靠近 integral，在“完整、必需、内置”上交叠。

entries.definition: the state of being whole and unbroken, or the quality of being honest. It is the noun of the same 'untouched' base.
entries.definitionCN: 完整、未受损的状态，或诚实的品质。它是同一个“未被碰过”词基的名词。

entries.definition: a whole number, positive, negative, or zero, with no fractional part. It is the source word, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 整数（正、负或零，无小数部分）。它是源词，不是近义词。

entries.definition: to make whole by bringing parts together. It is the verb of the family, while integral is the state or the part.
entries.definitionCN: 整合；使成整体。它是这个词族的动词，而 integral 是状态或部分。

entries.definition: complete and not damaged. It shares the literal 'untouched' image with integer but entered English separately.
entries.definitionCN: 完好无损的。它与 integer 共用“未被碰过”的字面画面，但另走一路进入英语。

entries.definition: absolutely necessary; forming the basic nature of something. It matches integral in the 'indispensable' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 必不可少的；本质的。对应 integral 的“不可或缺”义。

entries.definition: complete, with every part present and nothing missing. It matches integral's 'complete' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 完整的；全部的。对应 integral 的“完整”义。

entries.definition: belonging to a thing by its own nature rather than by addition. It matches integral in the 'built-in' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 固有的；内在的。对应 integral 的“内置、本来就有”义。

entries.definition: too important to be without. It is the strongest near-match for 'an integral part'.
entries.definitionCN: 不可或缺的。它是“不可或缺的一部分”最强的近义表达。

entries.definition: having all necessary parts or elements. It matches integral in the 'whole' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 完整的；齐全的。对应 integral 的“整体”义。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: in- 'not' plus tangere 'touch' behind integer, intact and contact, the 1570s integer 'whole number', and the calculus integral that sums slices into a whole.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真的：integer、intact、contact 背后 in-“不”+ tangere“触碰”，16 世纪 70 年代的 integer“整数”，以及把切片加成整体的微积分 integral。

normal.en: integral = in- 'not' + tang- 'touch': a thing nobody has broken off is still whole, and a part the whole cannot lose is integral.
normal.cn: integral = in-“不”+ tang-“碰”：没有谁把它掰掉一块的东西仍然完整，而整体丢不起的那一块就是 integral。

normal.en: integral and intact are the same picture: untouched, therefore undamaged.
normal.cn: integral 和 intact 是同一幅画：没被碰过，所以没有损伤。

normal.en: integer is a number that cannot be split without leaving the family; an integral part is a piece the whole cannot split off.
normal.cn: integer 是一旦拆开就不再是同类数的数；integral part 是整体一拆开就不复完整的那一块。

normal.en: integral and integrate are state and action: integrate makes it whole, integral says it is needed for the whole.
normal.cn: integral 与 integrate 是状态与动作：integrate 把它做成整体，integral 说它是整体所必需的。

normal.en: In calculus the integral is the whole rebuilt from thin slices, so even the math sense is 'make whole'.
normal.cn: 微积分里的 integral 是用薄片重新拼出的整体，所以连数学义也还是“使完整”。

abstract.en: The word's two faces are one: to be indispensable is to be the part without which the whole is no longer whole.
abstract.cn: 这个词的两副面孔其实是一副：不可或缺，就是缺了它整体便不再完整的那一部分。

abstract.en: Integrity of body and integrity of character use the same measure: nothing has been taken away or broken.
abstract.cn: 身体的完整与人格的正直用的是同一把尺：没有东西被拿走，也没有东西被折断。

abstract.en: An integral view is not a view of everything; it is a view in which nothing relevant is left outside.
abstract.cn: 整体化视角并不是把一切都收进来，而是不让任何相关的东西留在外面。

examples.en: Practice is integral to learning a language well.
examples.cn: 要学好一门语言，练习是不可或缺的。

examples.en: The two volumes form one integral work and should not be sold separately.
examples.cn: 这两卷构成一部完整的作品，不应分开出售。

examples.en: The integral of a positive function is the area under its curve.
examples.cn: 正函数的积分是其曲线下方的面积。

dict_mnemonic.text: “因特格柔”——in（不）+ teg（碰）：没被碰过的一块，才是完整、不可或缺的

root: 源自拉丁语 integer“完整的、未受碰触的”（in-“不”+ tangere“触碰”的词根），经中世纪拉丁语 integralis“构成整体的”与古法语 intégral 于 15 世纪后期进入英语；tangere 上溯重构的原始印欧词根 *tag-“触摸”（重构形式，无书面记录，来源不确定）。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of integral, all held by one image: a thing untouched and therefore whole, and a part whose removal would break that wholeness. Mathematics adds the integral, the whole rebuilt from slices.
sensesIntro.cn: integral 的九个义项由一个画面托住：一件未被碰过因而完整的东西，以及拿掉就会破坏这份完整的那一部分。数学再加进“积分”——用切片重新拼出的整体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an untouched, unbroken whole — and the one piece whose loss would leave a hole in it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个未被碰过、未曾断裂的整体——以及失去就会留下缺口的那一块。

branches.en: THE NEEDED PART: what is essential to the whole, and what belongs to it by nature rather than by addition.
branches.cn: 必需的那部分：整体少不得的东西，以及天然属于它而非外加的东西。

branches.en: THE UNBROKEN WHOLE: complete with every part present, and held together as one unit that cannot be split.
branches.cn: 未断的整体：所有部分都在的完整，以及作为一个不可拆分单元而保持一体。

branches.en: NUMBER AND CALCULUS: the integral sums infinitesimal slices, and an integral solution lands on a whole number.
branches.cn: 数与微积分：积分把无穷小切片相加，整数解则恰好落在整数上。

branches.en: CALCULUS AND THE WHOLE: the branch that sums infinitesimal slices, and the whole named as one entity.
branches.cn: 微积分与整体：把无穷小切片加总的那门运算，以及被命名为一个实体的整体。

branches.en: THE WHOLE-MAKING VIEW: a method that leaves no relevant part outside its design.
branches.cn: 使成整体的视角：一种不让任何相关部分落在设计之外的方法。

intro.en: Integral belongs to the Latin integer family: integrity, integrate and integration grow from the same base, while intact, tangible and contact share the 'touch' root that in- negates.
intro.cn: integral 属于拉丁语 integer 词族：integrity、integrate、integration 由同一词基长出，而 intact、tangible、contact 共用那个被 in- 否定的“触碰”词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin integer 'untouched, whole' gives integralis 'forming a whole' and integrare 'to make whole'. The root tangere 'to touch' also yields tangibilis 'touchable' and contingere 'to touch together'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 integer“未被碰过、完整”生出 integralis“构成整体的”与 integrare“使完整”。词根 tangere“触碰”还生出 tangibilis“可触的”与 contingere“相触、接触”。

items.meaning: forming a whole; essential to a whole
items.meaningCN: 完整的；不可或缺的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: Water is integral to every living cell.
items.exampleCN: 水对每一个活细胞都不可或缺。

items.meaning: the quality of being whole or essential
items.meaningCN: 完整性；不可或缺性（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: The integrality of the collection makes it unique.
items.exampleCN: 这套收藏的完整性使它独一无二。

items.meaning: in a way that forms part of a whole
items.meaningCN: 完整地；作为整体地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The two systems are integrally connected.
items.exampleCN: 这两个系统作为一个整体相连。

items.meaningCN: 完整；正直（-ity 构成名词）
items.example: The integrity of the data must be protected.
items.exampleCN: 数据的完整性必须受到保护。

items.meaning: to make whole by joining parts
items.meaningCN: 整合；使成整体（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: The school integrates art into every subject.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校把艺术融入每一门学科。

items.meaning: the act of making whole; also the math operation
items.meaningCN: 整合；一体化；积分（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: Economic integration changed the border towns.
items.exampleCN: 经济一体化改变了这些边境城镇。

items.meaning: a whole number; literally an untouched whole
items.meaningCN: 整数（字面“未受碰触的完整之物”）
items.example: Five and minus three are both integers.
items.exampleCN: 5 和 -3 都是整数。

items.meaningCN: 未受碰触的；完好无损的
items.example: The vase survived the move intact.
items.exampleCN: 这只花瓶搬动后仍完好无损。

items.meaningCN: 可触的；有形的（-ible 表“能被……的”）
items.example: The benefits were tangible, not just promised.
items.exampleCN: 好处是看得见摸得着的，不只是承诺。

items.meaning: the state of touching or communicating
items.meaningCN: 接触；联系（con- 共同 + tact 触碰）
items.example: The two wires must not make contact.
items.exampleCN: 这两根电线不得接触。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 未受碰触的；完整的；正直的

definition_zh: 史前的；有文字记录之前的；极古老、过时落后的（口语）
definition_en: belonging to the period before written records, or extremely old and out of date in everyday speech
core_image: 洞穴深处的赭红野牛，被火把的烟熏得发暗，画者没有留下名字
scene: 洞穴深处，手电光扫过岩壁上一群赭红色的野牛，线条被烟熏得发暗。 The cave paintings belong to a prehistoric hunt that no written record describes.
sceneCN: 这里 prehistoric 指「属于有文字记录之前时期的」（第 1 个义项：史前时代的）；句意为这些洞穴壁画属于一场没有任何文字记录的史前狩猎。图中可辨识物件：赭红野牛、烟熏痕迹、手电光、洞穴岩壁。

pos.zh: 史前的；有文字记录之前的；（口语）极其古老、过时的

forms.label: 对比形容词（有史以来的）

derivatives.zh: 原史时期的（介于史前与有史之间）
历史上有名的；有重大意义的

senses.title: Before written records
senses.definition: belonging to the period before a society kept written records
senses.definitionCN: 属于某个社会尚未留下文字记录的时期
senses.example: Prehistoric burial mounds dot the chalk downs.
senses.exampleCN: 史前墓葬土丘散布在白垩丘陵上。
senses.why: pre- 'before' plus historic marks a boundary, and the boundary is writing, not a fixed date.
senses.whyCN: pre-「之前」加 historic 标出一条界线，这条界线是文字，而非某个固定年代。

senses.title: Of early human cultures
senses.definition: relating to human societies known only through material traces such as tools, art and burials
senses.definitionCN: 指只能通过工具、艺术与墓葬等物质遗存了解的人类社会
senses.example: Prehistoric tool-making spread faster than any written account could show.
senses.exampleCN: 史前工具制造的传播速度，是任何文字记载都显示不出的。
senses.why: archaeology uses the word for cultures without texts, so the emphasis falls on material evidence.
senses.whyCN: 考古学用这个词指没有文本的文化，因此重点落在实物证据上。

senses.title: Of ancient animals and plants
senses.definition: describing organisms that lived before recorded history, especially the large extinct forms
senses.definitionCN: 指生活在有记录历史之前、尤指已灭绝的大型生物
senses.example: Prehistoric mammals filled the valley after the ice withdrew.
senses.exampleCN: 冰川退去后，史前哺乳动物遍布这个山谷。
senses.why: popular writing applies the word to extinct fauna, where it overlaps with prehistoric in the everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 通俗写作把这个词用于已灭绝的动物群，此处它与日常义重叠。

senses.title: Of ancient sites and art
senses.definition: belonging to the material remains of pre-literate societies, such as caves, monuments and carvings
senses.definitionCN: 属于前文字社会的物质遗存，如洞穴、巨石与雕刻
senses.example: The prehistoric cave was closed to protect its paintings.
senses.exampleCN: 这座史前洞穴为保护壁画而关闭。
senses.why: heritage usage fixes the word to objects and places, which is why it appears on signs and in management plans.
senses.whyCN: 遗产管理把这个词固定用于物件与场所，因此它出现在标牌与管理计划中。

senses.title: Extremely old in everyday speech
senses.definition: used exaggeration for something absurdly old-fashioned or long out of use
senses.definitionCN: 夸张地指某物老得离谱或早已不用
senses.example: His phone is prehistoric; it still has a physical keyboard.
senses.exampleCN: 他的手机老掉牙了，还带实体键盘。
senses.why: the exaggeration works because prehistory is by definition beyond memory, so 'old' becomes 'unimaginably old'.
senses.whyCN: 夸张之所以有效，是因为史前按定义在记忆之外，于是「旧」变成「旧得不可想象」。

senses.title: Hopelessly out of date technology
senses.definition: describing equipment or software so outdated that it is a liability
senses.definitionCN: 指设备或软件过时到成为负担
senses.example: The lab still runs prehistoric software on one machine.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室还有一台机器跑着极为陈旧的软件。
senses.why: this sense is the technical version of sense five, and it usually carries a recommendation to replace.
senses.whyCN: 这一义是第五义的技术版，通常暗含「该换掉」的建议。

senses.title: Before a field's own record
senses.titleCN: 某领域尚无记录的阶段
senses.definition: describing the early, undocumented phase of a discipline or institution
senses.definitionCN: 指某一学科或机构尚无记录的早期阶段
senses.example: The department's prehistoric years survive only as gossip.
senses.exampleCN: 该系的「史前」岁月只以传闻的形式留存。
senses.why: the word can be used relatively: prehistory ends wherever a field starts keeping records.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可相对使用：某个领域一开始记事，它的「史前」便告结束。

senses.title: Before humans in geological time
senses.titleCN: 地质时间上人类出现之前的
senses.definition: belonging to the long span of earth history before humans existed, when read in a geological frame
senses.definitionCN: 在地质框架下指人类出现之前那段漫长的地球历史
senses.example: The prehistoric rocks of the shield carry no trace of people.
senses.exampleCN: 地盾上的远古岩层没有留下任何人的痕迹。
senses.why: geology uses the word loosely for 'before people', which is much earlier than 'before writing'.
senses.whyCN: 地质学宽松地用这个词指「在人之前」，那比「在文字之前」早得多。

intro.en: Prehistoric joins Latin prae- 'before' to historic, from Greek historia 'inquiry, account'. The word was coined in the early nineteenth century for the period before written records. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: prehistoric 由拉丁 prae-「之前」加 historic（来自希腊 historia「探究、记述」）构成，十九世纪初为指文字记录之前的时期而造。年代均为约数。

items.en: Prae- meant 'before, in front of' and survives in English pre-, which marks precedence in time or place.
items.cn: 一般认为 prae- 意为「在前、在……之前」，在英语中留存为 pre-，标出时间或位置上的在先。

items.en: Historia meant 'inquiry, account, narrative', from histōr 'witness'; English historic and history both descend from it.
items.cn: historia 意为「探究、记述、叙述」，来自 histōr「见证者」；英语 historic 与 history 均源于此。

items.en: The compound was formed when writers needed a term for human existence before any written account existed.
items.cn: 当写作者需要一个词指尚无任何文字记述的人类存在时，这个复合词便被造出。

items.en: Archaeology made the word a technical label for cultures known only from material remains.
items.cn: 考古学把这个词固定为指「只能由实物遗存了解的文化」的技术标签。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word became a joking intensifier for anything absurdly old-fashioned.
items.cn: 在二十世纪，这个词成了戏谑的加强语，指任何老得离谱的东西。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dating only): the elements are certain, but the first English use is dated approximately and varies by source.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：成分确定，但英语中最早的使用只能约略定年，且各家说法不一。

note.en: Group one separates prehistoric from words with the same historic stem; group two separates it from adjectives for 'very old'.
note.cn: 第一组把 prehistoric 与同出 historic 词干的词分开；第二组区分它与表「很古老」的其它形容词。

entries.definition: The period itself; the adjective describes what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指那个时期本身；形容词描写属于该时期的事物。

entries.definition: Meaning 'momentous or recorded in history'; pre- adds 'before records', not 'important'.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「有重大意义的、载入史册的」；pre- 增添「在记录之前」，而非「重要」。

entries.definition: Meaning 'relating to history as a study'; it is the ordinary adjective for the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「与历史学有关的」，是该学科的普通形容词。

entries.definition: Proto- 'first' plus historic: the period when a society is just beginning to be described by outsiders.
entries.definitionCN: proto-「最初」加 historic：某社会刚开始被外来者记述的时期。

entries.definition: Very old, with no reference to writing; it can describe a recent but venerable custom.
entries.definitionCN: 很古老，但不涉及文字；也可形容新近却受尊崇的习俗。

entries.definition: Early in development, often with a tone of inferiority; prehistoric is neutral about development.
entries.definitionCN: 发展早期，常带低劣意味；prehistoric 对发展程度保持中性。

entries.definition: Of the earliest ages of the earth, before life of any complexity; it goes much deeper than prehistory.
entries.definitionCN: 指地球最古老的年代，复杂生命尚未出现；比史前深得多。

entries.definition: Literally 'before the flood', used jokingly for absurdly old things; it is a stylistic cousin of sense five.
entries.definitionCN: 字面「洪水之前」，戏指老得离谱的东西；是第五义的风格近亲。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: pre- 'before' + historic 'recorded': before the record begins.
normal.cn: pre-「之前」+ historic「有记录的」：记录开始之前。

normal.en: The family runs prehistory, prehistorian, prehistorically, protohistoric.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 prehistory、prehistorian、prehistorically、protohistoric。

normal.en: The boundary is writing, not a date, so the same adjective covers different centuries in different places.
normal.cn: 界线是文字而非某个年代，因此同一形容词在不同地方覆盖不同世纪。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: prehistoric site, prehistoric art, prehistoric animals.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：史前遗址、史前艺术、史前动物。

normal.en: The everyday sense is exaggeration: prehistoric phone, prehistoric software.
normal.cn: 日常义是夸张：老掉牙的手机、极为陈旧的软件。

abstract.en: Picture a handprint on a cave wall made before anyone could write.
abstract.cn: 想象一个印在洞壁上的手印，那时还没有人会书写。

abstract.en: Picture a machine still running after everyone who designed it has died.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器仍在运转，设计它的人已全部离世。

abstract.en: Picture a joke told so often that its first teller is forgotten.
abstract.cn: 想象一个笑话被讲得太久，最初讲它的人已被遗忘。

examples.en: The site contains prehistoric pottery and no written material.
examples.cn: 该遗址有史前陶器，没有任何文字材料。

examples.en: Their booking system is prehistoric but functional.
examples.cn: 他们的预订系统极为陈旧，但还能用。

examples.en: Prehistoric lakes left thick beds of clay across the valley.
examples.cn: 史前湖泊在山谷中留下厚厚的黏土层。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pre（之前）+ historic（有历史的）」——有历史记录之前 → 史前的；引申为老掉牙

root: 拉丁 prae-「之前」（英语 pre-）+ historic（希腊 historia「探究、记述」，源自 histōr「见证者」）；十九世纪初造词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one boundary, the start of records: before writing, then human material cultures, extinct animals, cave art, and finally anything so old that the boundary becomes a joke.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一条界线——记录的开始：先是有文字之前，再是人类的实物文化、已灭绝动物、洞穴艺术，最后是老到让这条界线变成玩笑的任何东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a painted animal on a wall, made by hands that left no name.
core.cn: 核心意象：壁上画的动物，由没留下名字的手所画。

branches.en: THE BOUNDARY AND THE PEOPLE: writing ends prehistory, and material traces are all we have of it.
branches.cn: 界线与人：文字终结史前，而实物痕迹是我们仅有的一切。

branches.en: LIFE AND ART: extinct animals and cave walls are the popular face of the word.
branches.cn: 生命与艺术：已灭绝动物与洞穴岩壁是这个词的大众面孔。

branches.en: HYPERBOLE: old enough to be a joke, and equipment old enough to be a liability.
branches.cn: 夸张：老到成为玩笑，设备旧到成为负担。

branches.en: RELATIVE PREHISTORY: every field has a phase before its own records start.
branches.cn: 相对的史前：每个领域都有自己记录开始前的阶段。

branches.en: DEEP FRAME: geology uses the word for 'before people', far earlier than 'before writing'.
branches.cn: 深时框架：地质学用这个词指「在人之前」，远早于「在文字之前」。

intro.en: Prehistoric is a Latin prefix plus a Greek-derived adjective, so it reads as 'before the recorded'.
intro.cn: prehistoric 是拉丁前缀加希腊来源的形容词，可读作「在有记录之前」。

latinIntro.en: Latin prae- gives pre-, and Greek historia gives historic; latinEntries records prae- and historia's Latin transmission.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 prae- 给出 pre-，希腊 historia 给出 historic；latinEntries 记录 prae- 与 historia 的拉丁传写。

items.example: The prefix marks precedence in time.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出时间上的在先。

items.example: Historic implies a written account.
items.exampleCN: historic 含文字记述之意。

items.example: Prehistoric sites lack texts.
items.exampleCN: 史前遗址没有文字。

items.example: Prehistory is read from objects.
items.exampleCN: 史前史由实物读出。

items.example: The prehistorian dated the mound.
items.exampleCN: 这位史前史研究者给土丘定年。

items.meaning: in a prehistoric way or time
items.example: The valley was prehistorically wooded.
items.exampleCN: 这山谷在史前覆盖森林。

items.example: Protohistoric trade left both texts and goods.
items.exampleCN: 原史时期的贸易留下文字与货物。

items.example: Historical method reads documents.
items.exampleCN: 历史学方法阅读文献。

items.meaningCN: 有重大意义的；载入史册的
items.example: A historic treaty was signed here.
items.exampleCN: 一项历史性条约在此签署。

definition_zh: 先锋物种；先锋种
definition_en: a species that is among the first to colonize bare or newly disturbed ground and help make it suitable for later species
core_image: 第一株在火山灰上扎根的地衣，背后还是一片灰白
scene: 在退冰川后的砾石地上，仙女木与苔藓是最早扎根的先锋物种，它们固定氮并积累薄土。 On the gravel left by a retreating glacier, Dryas and mosses are the pioneer species that root first, fixing nitrogen and building a thin soil.
sceneCN: 这里 pioneer species 是「先锋物种」（第 1 个义项：最先定殖裸地的物种）；句意：在退冰川后的砾石地上，仙女木与苔藓是最早扎根的先锋物种，它们固氮并积累薄土。

pos.zh: 先锋物种；先锋种（单复数同形，复数为 pioneer species）

senses.title: First colonizers of bare ground
senses.definition: species that establish first on rock, lava, ash, or sand with little or no soil
senses.definitionCN: 在几乎没有土壤的岩石、熔岩、火山灰或沙地上最先建立的物种
senses.example: Lichens are pioneer species on the fresh lava.
senses.exampleCN: 地衣是新鲜熔岩上的先锋物种。
senses.why: Pioneer comes from French pionnier 'foot soldier': the first to enter dangerous ground. Ecologically, these species enter a site before any soil exists.
senses.whyCN: pioneer 来自法语 pionnier「步兵」：最先进入险地的人。生态学上，这些物种在任何土壤形成之前就进入地点。

senses.title: Early successional species generally
senses.definition: species characteristic of the early stages of succession, including fast-growing herbs and shrubs
senses.definitionCN: 演替早期阶段的特征物种，包括速生草本与灌木
senses.example: Fireweed is a pioneer species after forest fires in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 柳兰是北方森林火灾后的先锋物种。
senses.why: The term broadens from bare rock to any early stage: what matters is arriving early and growing fast, not the substrate type.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从裸岩扩展到任何早期阶段：关键是最先到达并快速生长，而不是基质类型。

senses.title: Facilitators that build soil
senses.definition: pioneer species that add organic matter or nutrients and make the site habitable for later species
senses.definitionCN: 添加有机物或养分、使地点可供后来物种居住的先锋物种
senses.example: Nitrogen-fixing pioneers act as facilitators for the whole succession.
senses.exampleCN: 固氮先锋物种作为整个演替的促进者。
senses.why: Ecological theory calls this facilitation: the first species changes the environment, so its own success creates the conditions for its replacement.
senses.whyCN: 生态学理论称此为促进：首批物种改变环境，因此它们自身的成功为被替代创造了条件。

senses.title: Nurse plants in restoration
senses.definition: pioneer species deliberately planted to shelter or enrich the soil for target species
senses.definitionCN: 为遮蔽或改良土壤以利于目标物种而有意种植的先锋物种
senses.example: The project used a legume pioneer species as a nurse crop.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目用豆科先锋物种作为保育作物。
senses.why: Restoration turns the ecological role into a tool: a hardy pioneer is planted not for itself but for what it does to the site.
senses.whyCN: 恢复把生态角色变成工具：种植耐逆先锋不是为了它本身，而是为了它对地点所做的改变。

senses.title: Weedy or invasive early colonizers
senses.titleCN: 杂草型或入侵性早期定殖者
senses.definition: fast-spreading species that dominate disturbed ground, sometimes hindering native succession
senses.definitionCN: 迅速扩散、支配受扰地面、有时阻碍本地演替的物种
senses.example: An invasive grass became the pioneer species on every cleared slope.
senses.exampleCN: 一种入侵草成为每片清理坡地的先锋物种。
senses.why: The same early-arrival strategy that makes a species a pioneer can make it a weed: rapid dispersal and growth are advantageous in bare sites.
senses.whyCN: 使物种成为先锋的同一“早到”策略也能使它成为杂草：在裸地中，快速扩散与生长占优势。

senses.title: Pioneers of secondary succession
senses.definition: species that first return after fire, logging, or abandonment where soil already exists
senses.definitionCN: 在火灾、采伐或弃耕后土壤已存在的地点最先回归的物种
senses.example: Annual weeds were the pioneers of secondary succession in the old field.
senses.exampleCN: 一年生杂草是旧田次生演替的先锋。
senses.why: With soil present, the pioneer need not build one; it only needs to germinate fast and tolerate full sun, so the pioneer role shifts to ruderal species.
senses.whyCN: 土壤已存在时，先锋不必造土，只需快速萌发并耐全光，因此先锋角色转向路旁杂草型物种。

senses.title: A role, not a fixed list
senses.titleCN: 一种角色而非固定名单
senses.definition: the functional category of first colonizers, which different species may fill in different regions
senses.definitionCN: 最先定殖者的功能类别，不同地区可由不同物种承担
senses.example: Pioneer species differ between tropical and alpine sites; the role is the same.
senses.exampleCN: 热带与高山地点的先锋物种不同，但角色相同。
senses.why: Ecologists treat the term as a role: any species with the right traits can be a pioneer, which is why no single species list defines it.
senses.whyCN: 生态学家把这个词当作角色：任何具备相应性状的物种都能当先锋，因此没有单一物种名单能定义它。

senses.title: Pioneers in island biogeography
senses.titleCN: 岛屿生物地理学中的先锋
senses.definition: the first species to reach a new island or habitat island and establish a population
senses.definitionCN: 最先到达新岛屿或栖息地“岛”并建立种群的物种
senses.example: The first pioneer species on the new island were wind-borne ferns.
senses.exampleCN: 新岛上的第一批先锋物种是风传播的蕨类。
senses.why: Island biogeography extends the idea from succession to dispersal: arrival order matters because the first colonist faces no competitors.
senses.whyCN: 岛屿生物地理学把这一观念从演替扩展到扩散：到达顺序很重要，因为首个定殖者没有竞争者。

intro.en: Pioneer comes through French from a word for a foot soldier; species comes from Latin specere 'to look'. Their combination is a modern ecological label.
intro.cn: pioneer 经法语来自指“步兵”的词；species 来自拉丁语 specere「看」。两者的组合是现代生态学标签。

items.en: Old French paonier, later pionnier, meant 'foot soldier, pioneer'. It derives from peon 'foot soldier', from Late Latin pedonem, from Latin pes 'foot'.
items.cn: 古法语 paonier（后为 pionnier）意为“步兵、先锋”，来自 peon「步兵」，再来自晚期拉丁语 pedonem 与拉丁语 pes「脚」。

items.en: A pioneer was a soldier sent ahead to clear roads and prepare ground for the main army — exactly the image ecology later used for first colonizers.
items.cn: pioneer 原指先遣清理道路、为大部队准备地面的士兵——正是生态学后来用于首批定殖者的意象。

items.en: species 'a particular sort, kind, appearance' comes from specere 'to look at'; the plural species is identical in form.
items.cn: species「某一类别、外观」来自 specere「看」，其复数形式 species 与单数同形。

items.en: Pioneer was applied to plant colonizers in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, when succession studies named the first seral stage the pioneer stage.
items.cn: pioneer 在 19 世纪末至 20 世纪初被用于植物定殖者，演替研究把第一个阶段命名为先锋阶段。

items.en: Modern ecology uses pioneer species for early colonists with fast dispersal and growth; the phrase is a role description, not a taxonomic group.
items.cn: 现代生态学用 pioneer species 指扩散与生长迅速的最早定殖者；该短语是角色描述，不是分类群。

note.en: The first group separates related succession terms, the second compares ecological categories of species.
note.cn: 第一组区分演替相关术语，第二组比较生态学物种类别。

entries.definition: the late, relatively stable community; pioneer species name the first stage.
entries.definitionCN: 演替后期相对稳定的群落；pioneer species 指第一阶段。

entries.definition: the first seral stage itself; the species are the organisms that occupy it.
entries.definitionCN: 第一个演替阶段本身；物种是占据该阶段的生物。

entries.definition: the adjective meaning 'first or innovative'; it does not name a species.
entries.definitionCN: 意为“开创性的”形容词，不指物种。

entries.definition: any organism that establishes in a new place; a pioneer species is a colonizer of early, often bare, sites.
entries.definitionCN: 任何在新地点建立的生物；先锋物种是早期、常为裸地的定殖者。

entries.definition: a plant of disturbed, nutrient-rich ground; it overlaps with pioneers of secondary succession.
entries.definitionCN: 受扰动、养分丰富地面的植物；与次生演替先锋重叠。

entries.definition: a plant that shelters seedlings of other species; a pioneer can serve as a nurse.
entries.definitionCN: 庇护其他物种幼苗的植物；先锋可作为保育植物。

entries.definition: a non-native species that spreads and causes harm; a pioneer may or may not be invasive.
entries.definitionCN: 扩散并造成危害的非本地物种；先锋未必是入侵种。

entries.definition: a species of the early stages of succession, often used interchangeably with pioneer.
entries.definitionCN: 演替早期阶段的物种，常与 pioneer 互换使用。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real etymological images, standard terms, and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实词源意象、标准术语与真实同族词。

normal.en: Pioneer was a foot soldier sent ahead: pioneer species go in first, before soil exists.
normal.cn: pioneer 是先遣步兵：先锋物种最先进入，那时还没有土壤。

normal.en: Species is both singular and plural: one pioneer species, many pioneer species.
normal.cn: species 单复数同形：一个 pioneer species，许多 pioneer species。

normal.en: Facilitation is the key mechanism: pioneers build soil, later species use it.
normal.cn: 促进是关键机制：先锋造土，后来物种用土。

normal.en: In secondary succession the pioneer is often a fast annual weed, not a lichen.
normal.cn: 次生演替中的先锋常是速生一年生杂草，而非地衣。

normal.en: Climax community is the far end of the ladder; pioneer species is the bottom rung.
normal.cn: climax community 是梯子的远端；pioneer species 是最底一级。

abstract.en: Picture a single lichen on grey rock: it is the first resident, and its death creates the first patch of soil.
abstract.cn: 想象灰色岩石上的一片地衣：它是第一个住户，它的死亡造出第一块土壤。

abstract.en: The term names a job, not a family: fast arrival, fast growth, tolerance of harsh conditions.
abstract.cn: 这个词命名的是“岗位”而非“家系”：快速到达、快速生长、耐受恶劣条件。

abstract.en: The pioneer's success is self-limiting: by improving the site it makes room for its successors.
abstract.cn: 先锋的成功是自我限制的：它改善地点，从而为后继者腾出空间。

examples.en: Mosses and lichens are the pioneer species on the new lava flow.
examples.cn: 苔藓与地衣是新熔岩流上的先锋物种。

examples.en: The restoration plan selected a nitrogen-fixing pioneer species to start soil formation.
examples.cn: 恢复计划选择一种固氮先锋物种来启动成土过程。

examples.en: Pioneer species on the abandoned field were mostly wind-dispersed annuals.
examples.cn: 弃耕地上的先锋物种多是风传播的一年生植物。

dict_mnemonic.text: “派你先”——先派你上去占住裸地 → pioneer species 先锋物种

root: pioneer 经法语来自 peon「步兵」（拉丁语 pes「脚」）；species 来自拉丁语 specere「看」，指类别。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of pioneer species: bare-ground first colonists, early seral species, soil-building facilitators, restoration nurse plants, invasive early colonizers, secondary-succession pioneers, the functional role itself, and first arrivals in island biogeography.
sensesIntro.cn: pioneer species 的八个义项：裸地首批定殖者、早期演替物种、造土促进者、恢复保育植物、入侵性早期定殖者、次生演替先锋、功能角色本身与岛屿生物地理学中的首批到达者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lichen on grey rock, the first living patch on a blank surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：灰色岩石上的一片地衣，是空白表面的第一块生命斑块。

branches.en: FIRST ARRIVAL: bare ground and post-disturbance fields both reward fast colonization.
branches.cn: 最先到达：裸地与受扰动后的土地都奖赏快速的定殖。

branches.en: GENERAL LABEL: early seral species of any kind are called pioneers, even where the ground was not bare.
branches.cn: 通用标签：任何类型的早期演替物种都被称作先锋，即使地面原本并非裸地。

branches.en: FACILITATION: the pioneer changes soil and can be planted as a nurse.
branches.cn: 促进：先锋物种改变土壤，也可作为保育植物被栽种。

branches.en: RISK: the same fast-growth strategy can turn a pioneer into a weed.
branches.cn: 风险：同样的快速生长策略可能把先锋变成杂草。

branches.en: ROLE AND DISPERSAL: any suitable species can fill the job, and first arrivals on islands face no competitors.
branches.cn: 角色与扩散：任何合适的物种都能胜任这一角色，而岛屿上的首批到达者没有竞争者。

intro.en: Pioneer species is a two-word technical phrase; neither word is analysable with a living English prefix. Pioneer has a French agent suffix, species a Latin noun ending.
intro.cn: pioneer species 是双词技术短语；两词都不含活的英语前缀。pioneer 有法语施事后缀，species 有拉丁名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin pes 'foot' yields pedal, pedestrian, and expedite through the pion- branch; specere 'to look' yields species, spectrum, inspect, and perspective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pes「脚」经 pion- 一支衍生 pedal、pedestrian、expedite；specere「看」衍生 species、spectrum、inspect、perspective。

items.meaningCN: 先遣者；先锋（-ier 施事后缀）
items.example: Pioneers cleared the road.
items.exampleCN: 先遣队清理了道路。

items.example: Pioneering work described the stage.
items.exampleCN: 开创性工作描述了该阶段。

items.meaningCN: 类别；外观（-ies 名词词尾）
items.example: Several species share the role.
items.exampleCN: 多个物种共享这一角色。

items.example: Speciation on islands is rapid.
items.exampleCN: 岛屿上的物种形成很快。

items.example: The pioneer stage lasts a few years.
items.exampleCN: 先锋阶段持续数年。

items.meaning: making a site easier for others
items.meaningCN: 使地点更易被他人利用；促进
items.example: Facilitation speeds succession.
items.exampleCN: 促进加速演替。

items.example: Ruderal plants follow clearing.
items.exampleCN: 路旁植物随清理出现。

items.meaning: one that establishes in a new place
items.example: Wind is the main colonizer agent.
items.exampleCN: 风是主要的定殖媒介。

definition_zh: 污染；玷污；使（样品、食品、环境）混入有害物
definition_en: to introduce a harmful or unwanted substance into something that was clean or pure
core_image: 一滴墨落进清水，整缸水从中心向外染成灰色
scene: 工厂把清洗溶剂的废水直接排进河里，下游的取水口被迫关闭。 Waste solvent from the factory contaminated the river downstream.
sceneCN: 这里指有害物质进入水体使其不再洁净（第 1 个义项：把有害物排入水体、土壤或空气）；句意：工厂排出的废溶剂污染了下游的河水。

pos.zh: 污染；弄脏；使混入杂质；玷污

senses.title: To pollute water, soil or air
senses.definition: to put a harmful substance into the environment so that it is no longer safe
senses.definitionCN: 把有害物质排入环境，使其不再安全
senses.example: Waste solvent from the factory contaminated the river downstream.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂排出的废溶剂污染了下游的河水。
senses.why: The verb names the entry of foreign matter into something clean, and the environment is its largest stage.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词指异物进入原本洁净之物，环境是它最大的舞台。

senses.title: To infect food or a surface
senses.definition: to bring bacteria, viruses or other pathogens into food, water or a contact surface
senses.definitionCN: 把细菌、病毒或其他病原带入食物、饮水或接触表面
senses.example: Unwashed hands contaminated the sandwiches on the counter.
senses.exampleCN: 没洗的手污染了柜台上的三明治。
senses.why: Once the intruder is a living organism, contamination becomes infection, and the same verb covers it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦入侵者是活的生物体，污染就变成传染，同一个动词仍然管用。

senses.title: To spoil a scientific sample
senses.definition: to mix an unwanted substance into a sample so that a measurement no longer reflects the original
senses.definitionCN: 把不需要的物质混入样品，使测量结果不再反映原状
senses.example: A dirty pipette contaminated the blood sample.
senses.exampleCN: 一支不干净的吸管污染了血液样本。
senses.why: Laboratory work lives on purity, so the smallest intruder ruins the sample and the verb is used constantly.
senses.whyCN: 实验室工作依赖纯净，最小的入侵物就能毁掉样品，因此这个动词被频繁使用。

senses.title: To corrupt a language or culture
senses.definition: to mix foreign or inferior elements into a language, tradition or style until its character changes
senses.definitionCN: 把外来或低劣成分混入语言、传统或风格，使其性质改变
senses.example: Purists complained that slang contaminated the written language.
senses.exampleCN: 纯粹主义者抱怨俚语污染了书面语言。
senses.why: A language is imagined as a clear liquid, and borrowed elements as the drop of ink that darkens it.
senses.whyCN: 语言被想象成一缸清水，借入的成分则是把它染深的那滴墨。

senses.title: To pollute a dataset
senses.definition: to insert wrong, duplicated or irrelevant records into a dataset so that its results cannot be trusted
senses.definitionCN: 把错误、重复或无关的记录放进数据集，使结果不可信赖
senses.example: A faulty sensor contaminated the climate records for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 一个故障传感器污染了整整两年的气候记录。
senses.why: Data is treated like a sample: one bad entry spreads through every calculation made from it.
senses.whyCN: 数据被当作样品：一条坏记录会扩散到由它得出的每一次计算。

senses.title: To make something radioactive
senses.definition: to introduce radioactive material into an object, a place or a body
senses.definitionCN: 把放射性物质带入某件物体、某个场所或某个身体
senses.example: The accident contaminated the groundwater around the plant.
senses.exampleCN: 事故使电厂周围的地下水带上了放射性。
senses.why: Radiation is invisible and travels, so it became the most feared form of contamination.
senses.whyCN: 辐射看不见又会传播，因此成了最令人恐惧的污染形式。

senses.title: To taint a mind or morals
senses.definition: to fill a person or a group with ideas considered corrupting
senses.definitionCN: 用被认为败坏的观念充满某个人或某个群体
senses.example: The pamphlet warned that foreign films contaminated the young.
senses.exampleCN: 这本小册子警告说外国电影败坏了年轻人。
senses.why: The old religious sense of moral stain survived inside the modern word for physical pollution.
senses.whyCN: 古老的宗教性「道德污损」含义，保存在现代这个表示物质污染的词语里。

senses.title: To compromise a scene or evidence
senses.titleCN: 破坏现场或证据的纯净
senses.definition: to disturb a place or a piece of evidence so that traces are lost or no longer reliable
senses.definitionCN: 搅动现场或证据，使痕迹丢失或不再可靠
senses.example: Officers who walk through the room may contaminate the crime scene.
senses.exampleCN: 走进房间的警员可能破坏犯罪现场。
senses.why: Evidence must stay as it was found, so any added trace is contamination in the legal sense.
senses.whyCN: 证据必须保持发现时的样子，因此任何新增痕迹在法律意义上都是污染。

intro.en: Contaminate comes from a Latin verb of defilement built on a noun for the stain left by contact. The link to the Latin verb for touching is widely accepted, but the exact formation of the noun is still debated, so the deeper source is marked as unsettled.
intro.cn: 本词出自一个表示玷污的拉丁动词，其基础名词指接触留下的污损。它与拉丁语中表示触碰的动词有关，这一点被广泛接受，但那个名词的具体构成仍有争议，因此更早的来源标注为未有定论。

items.en: Tangere meant to touch, and the same root stands behind English words for contact and for contagion.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为触碰，英语中表示接触与传染的词都出自同一词根。

items.en: Contamen named the defilement that contact leaves behind; its own formation and variant spellings are still discussed.
items.cn: 这个拉丁名词指接触留下的污损；它自身的构成与拼写变体至今仍有讨论。

items.en: The verb meant to defile or to make unclean, and early writers used it for religious and legal pollution.
items.cn: 这个动词意为玷污或使不洁，早期作者用它指宗教与法律意义上的污损。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the sixteenth century, when the first sense was moral and religious rather than chemical.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，当时最初的义项是道德与宗教性的，而不是化学性的。

items.en: Hygiene, chemistry and microbiology later moved the word to physical pollution of water, food and samples.
items.cn: 卫生学、化学与微生物学后来把这个词转向水、食品与样品的物质污染。

items.en: Source uncertain: the derivation of the noun for contact-stain from the verb for touching is the usual account, not a settled fact, so no single ancestral form is claimed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：把表示接触污损的名词追溯到表示触碰的动词，只是通行的解释，并非定论，因此不主张单一祖形。

note.en: The first group shares the contact root or looks close to it; the second group names ways of making something impure. Contaminate is about mixing in foreign matter, while distort is about twisting a shape or a story, and the two are not interchangeable.
note.cn: 第一组共享接触词根或字形相近；第二组是使某物不纯的各种方式。本词指混入异物，扭曲类词则指扭歪形状或歪曲叙述，两者不能互换。

entries.definition: The state or the act of being made impure.
entries.definitionCN: 被弄得不纯的状态或动作。

entries.definition: The intruding substance itself, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指入侵的物质本身，而不是动作。

entries.definition: Touching or communication; it keeps the literal sense of the root.
entries.definitionCN: 接触或联系；保留了词根的字面义。

entries.definition: The spread of disease by contact; it names transmission, not impurity.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病经接触传播；指传播，而非不纯。

entries.definition: To make the environment dirty, usually on a large scale; it is the public word for the same act.
entries.definitionCN: 使环境变脏，通常指大规模；是同一动作的公共说法。

entries.definition: To bring a pathogen into a body; it requires a living host.
entries.definitionCN: 把病原带入身体；需要有活的宿主。

entries.definition: To spoil something with a small amount of something bad, often figuratively.
entries.definitionCN: 用少量坏东西败坏某物，常用于比喻。

entries.definition: To put a toxic substance into something that will be eaten or drunk.
entries.definitionCN: 把有毒物质放进将被吃喝的东西。

entries.definition: To add an inferior substance to a product, usually for profit.
entries.definitionCN: 为获利在产品中掺入劣质成分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the contact root, the real family and the laboratory phrases that show where the word lives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用接触词根、真实同族词，以及能显示使用场合的实验室搭配。

normal.en: The root means to touch, and the noun inside the verb means the stain that touching leaves.
normal.cn: 词根意为触碰，动词内部的名词指触碰留下的污损。

normal.en: The family runs contamination, contaminant, contaminated and decontaminate.
normal.cn: 同族词有表示污染的名词、污染物、受污染的与去除污染。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: contaminate water, contaminate a sample, contaminated food.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：污染水源、使样品受污染、受污染的食品。

normal.en: The laboratory is its home: one dirty pipette ruins a whole sample.
normal.cn: 实验室是它的主场：一支脏吸管毁掉整个样品。

normal.en: The opposite is built with a removal prefix: to decontaminate is to take the intrusion out.
normal.cn: 反义靠一个表示去除的前缀构成：去污就是把入侵物清走。

abstract.en: Picture one drop of ink falling into a glass of clear water.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴墨落进一杯清水。

abstract.en: Picture a footprint appearing on a page that was supposed to stay blank.
abstract.cn: 想象一页本该空白的纸上多出一个脚印。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour that enters a quiet town and colours every conversation.
abstract.cn: 想象一则传言进入平静的小镇，把每场谈话都染上颜色。

examples.en: Heavy metals contaminated the soil near the old factory.
examples.cn: 重金属污染了老厂附近的土壤。

examples.en: One careless handler can contaminate a whole batch of food.
examples.cn: 一个粗心的操作者就能污染整批食品。

examples.en: The virus contaminated the cell culture within days.
examples.cn: 病毒在几天之内就污染了这批细胞培养物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肯」加「摊」加「米内特」——脏东西摊进米里，整袋都不干净：污染

root: 拉丁语「触碰」词根衍生出表示接触污损的名词，再加动词词尾构成「玷污、使不洁」；名词的具体构成仍有争议，故更早来源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a harmful outsider enters something clean, whether river, food, sample, language, dataset, body, mind or evidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一个动作：有害的外来者进入原本洁净之物，可以是河流、食品、样品、语言、数据集、身体、心灵或证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of ink entering clear water and darkening the whole glass from the centre outward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴墨落进清水，整缸水从中心向外染成灰色。

branches.en: THE ENVIRONMENT: water, soil and air, including the invisible spread of radiation.
branches.cn: 环境：水、土壤与空气，也包括辐射那种看不见的扩散。

branches.en: THE BODY AND THE SCENE: pathogens in food, and a crime scene no longer clean.
branches.cn: 身体与现场：食品中的病原，以及不再洁净的犯罪现场。

branches.en: THE RECORD: a spoiled sample and a polluted dataset, where one intruder ruins every reading.
branches.cn: 记录：被毁的样品与被污染的数据集，一个入侵者毁掉所有读数。

branches.en: THE CULTURE: a language or tradition mixed with foreign elements until its character changes.
branches.cn: 文化：语言或传统混入外来成分，直到性质改变。

branches.en: THE MIND: morals imagined as a clear surface that can be stained.
branches.cn: 心灵：道德被想象成一块可以被染污的洁净表面。

intro.en: Contaminate is a Latin verb of touching and defilement; its family divides into the substance that intrudes and the act of removing it.
intro.cn: 本词是一个表示触碰与玷污的拉丁动词；其词族分为入侵的物质与去除污染的动作两支。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb for touching and the noun for contact-stain are the two pieces behind the English word; the noun ending is Latin as well.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示触碰的动词与表示接触污损的名词，是英语词背后的两个构件；名词词尾同样来自拉丁语。

items.example: It marks the meeting of two substances.
items.exampleCN: 它标记两种物质的相遇。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of contact.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供接触的观念。

items.example: The noun turns contact into a stain.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把接触变成污损。

items.example: The verb is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: It gives the Latin stem an English verb shape.
items.exampleCN: 它给拉丁词干披上英语动词外形。

items.example: It builds the name of the process.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示过程的名称。

items.meaning: the thing or person that does
items.example: It builds the name of the intruding substance.
items.exampleCN: 它构成入侵物质的名称。

items.example: It builds the verb for taking the intrusion out.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示清除入侵物的动词。

items.example: It marks the state of an object already made impure.
items.exampleCN: 它标记已被弄脏的对象状态。

definition_zh: 因此，结果；由于（后接名词或动名词）
definition_en: as a result of something; used to introduce an effect that follows from a cause
core_image: 第一张多米诺骨牌倒下，第二张随之倾覆
scene: 第一张骨牌倒下，第二张跟着倾覆。 As a consequence, the whole line collapsed.
sceneCN: 这里取「因此、结果」（第 1 个义项：句首结果连接语）；句意为结果整条骨牌线都倒了。

pos.zh: 状语短语：因此、结果
介词短语：由于

senses.title: The sentence-opening result marker
senses.definition: placed at the start of a sentence to introduce the effect of what was just said
senses.definitionCN: 置于句首，引出前述内容造成的效果
senses.example: As a consequence, the whole line collapsed.
senses.exampleCN: 结果整条骨牌线都倒了。
senses.why: The phrase opens the effect after the cause has been stated, which is why it usually follows a full sentence.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语在原因说完后开启结果，因此通常跟在完整句子之后。

senses.title: The mid-sentence result
senses.definition: used after and or a semicolon inside a sentence to attach a result
senses.definitionCN: 在句中用「并且」或分号之后接出结果
senses.example: The road was closed, and as a consequence the delivery was late.
senses.exampleCN: 道路封闭，因而送货迟了。
senses.why: Inside one sentence the phrase keeps cause and effect together, which suits short chains of events.
senses.whyCN: 在同一句内，这个短语把因果放在一起，适合短事件链。

senses.title: Naming the cause with a noun
senses.definition: used before of and a noun to name the cause rather than the effect
senses.definitionCN: 用在介词加名词之前，点出原因而非结果
senses.example: As a consequence of the drought, food prices rose.
senses.exampleCN: 由于旱情，食品价格上涨。
senses.why: Adding of reverses the direction: the phrase now points back to the cause and forward to the consequence.
senses.whyCN: 加上介词就调转方向：短语现在回指原因、前指后果。

senses.title: Naming the cause with a gerund
senses.titleCN: 后接介词加动名词：由于做……
senses.definition: used before of and an -ing form when the cause is an activity
senses.definitionCN: 在介词与动名词前使用，表示原因是一项活动
senses.example: As a consequence of cutting the budget, two services closed.
senses.exampleCN: 由于削减预算，两项服务被关停。
senses.why: Because the phrase is prepositional, an activity after of must appear as a gerund, not as a bare verb.
senses.whyCN: 由于这是介词短语，介词后的活动必须以动名词出现，不能用光秃秃的动词。

senses.title: The academic causal chain
senses.definition: in research writing, used to link a finding to the effect that follows from it
senses.definitionCN: 在学术写作中，把一项发现与随之而来的效果相连
senses.example: As a consequence, later studies used a much smaller sample.
senses.exampleCN: 结果，后续研究所用的样本小得多。
senses.why: Academic argument needs a formal marker that a result is being drawn from evidence already presented.
senses.whyCN: 学术论证需要一个正式标记，表明结果是从已呈现的证据推出的。

senses.title: The formal cousin of a plainer phrase
senses.titleCN: 语域：比口语因果说法更正式
senses.definition: in formal prose it replaces the shorter phrase as a result and often carries a hint of seriousness
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文字中替代更短的「结果是」，并常带一丝严重意味
senses.example: As a consequence, the scheme was abandoned.
senses.exampleCN: 结果，这个方案被放弃了。
senses.why: The longer noun sounds weightier than the short phrase, which is why reports and judgments prefer it.
senses.whyCN: 较长的名词比短说法更有分量，因此报告与判决偏爱它。

senses.title: The sense of an unwelcome outcome
senses.definition: used especially when the effect is unwelcome or damaging
senses.definitionCN: 尤用于效果不受欢迎或带有损害时
senses.example: As a consequence, the firm lost two major clients.
senses.exampleCN: 结果，这家公司失去了两个大客户。
senses.why: The noun itself suggests something that follows unavoidably, so the phrase often introduces loss rather than gain.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词本身暗示不可避免的后续，因此短语常引出损失而非收益。

senses.title: The conclusion marker in reasoning
senses.definition: used in argument to mark a conclusion drawn from stated premises
senses.definitionCN: 在论证中标记从已述前提出发的结论
senses.example: As a consequence, the two claims cannot both be true.
senses.exampleCN: 因此，这两个主张不可能同时为真。
senses.why: Reasoning needs a word that separates premises from conclusion, and this phrase does that formally.
senses.whyCN: 推理需要一个把前提与结论分开的词，这个短语正式地承担了。

intro.en: Consequence comes from Latin consequentia, from consequi, to follow after, itself con-, with, and sequi, to follow. The Latin line is clear; the English phrase is modern.
intro.cn: consequence 来自拉丁语 consequentia，词根 consequi 意为「跟随」，由 con-「共同」与 sequi「跟随」构成。拉丁语线索清楚，英语短语属近代。

items.en: Sequi, to follow, is also the root of sequence and sequel.
items.cn: sequi 意为「跟随」，也是 sequence 与 sequel 的词根。

items.en: Consequi meant to follow closely or to result from something.
items.cn: consequi 意为紧随，或由某事物导致。

items.en: The noun named what follows from a cause, and Old French consequence carried it to English.
items.cn: 这个名词指由原因导致的结果，古法语 consequence 把它带入英语。

items.en: English consequence appears in the Middle English period; the date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语 consequence 见于中古英语，年代为约数。

items.en: The phrase with this article and noun settles in modern formal writing.
items.cn: 带冠词与名词的这个短语在近代正式文字中定型。

note.en: The first group also marks a result but differs in register or direction; the second group holds adverbs and phrases of effect.
note.cn: 第一组同样标记结果，但语域或方向不同；第二组是表效果与结论的副词短语。

entries.definition: It is the plainer and more common result marker.
entries.definitionCN: 它是更朴素、更常见的结果标记。

entries.definition: It points back to a cause rather than forward to an effect.
entries.definitionCN: 它回指原因，而非前指效果。

entries.definition: A British written variant with the same result sense.
entries.definitionCN: 英式书面变体，结果义相同。

entries.definition: With of it names the cause instead of the effect.
entries.definitionCN: 加上介词后点出原因而非结果。

entries.definition: It marks a result in one word and often opens a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 用一个词标记结果，常开句。

entries.definition: It draws a conclusion rather than narrating an effect.
entries.definitionCN: 它引出结论，而非叙述效果。

entries.definition: It marks an action taken in response to a fact.
entries.definitionCN: 标记针对事实采取的行动。

entries.definition: A short formal word meaning for this reason.
entries.definitionCN: 一个简短的正式词，意为「因此」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real follow root, the real cause-and-effect pattern and the real register.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实「跟随」词根、真实因果结构与真实语域。

normal.en: To follow is the root, so a consequence is what comes after a cause.
normal.cn: 词根是「跟随」，后果就是原因之后跟来的东西。

normal.en: It takes of to name the cause and stands alone to name the effect.
normal.cn: 加介词点原因，单独用则点结果。

normal.en: The object after of may be a noun or a gerund, never a bare verb.
normal.cn: 介词后的宾语可以是名词或动名词，不能是光秃秃的动词。

normal.en: Reports and judgments prefer it because the noun sounds weighty.
normal.cn: 报告与判决偏爱它，因为这个名词听起来有分量。

normal.en: It often introduces loss, since what follows unavoidably is rarely good news.
normal.cn: 它常引出损失，因为不可避免的后续很少是好消息。

abstract.en: Like one domino tipping the next, and the next, until the line is down.
abstract.cn: 像一张骨牌推倒下一张，再下一张，直到整排倒下。

abstract.en: Like a receipt printed only after the purchase has gone wrong.
abstract.cn: 像只有购买出了问题之后才打印出来的收据。

abstract.en: Like the last line of a proof, where the conclusion finally appears.
abstract.cn: 像证明的最后一行，结论终于出现。

examples.en: As a consequence, the project was delayed by three months.
examples.cn: 结果，项目被延误了三个月。

examples.en: As a consequence of the flood, the bridge was closed.
examples.cn: 由于洪水，这座桥被关闭了。

examples.en: The company cut costs and, as a consequence, lost several clients.
examples.cn: 公司削减成本，因而失去了几个客户。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿兹 额 康西昆斯」——一张骨牌推倒下一张：因此、结果

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split by position and direction: a sentence opener, a mid-sentence link, of plus a noun, of plus a gerund, an academic chain, formal register, an unwelcome outcome, and a conclusion marker.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项按位置与方向区分：句首、句中、介词加名词、介词加动名词、学术因果链、正式语域、负面后果、结论标记。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one domino tipping the next until the line is down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张骨牌推倒下一张，直到整排倒下。

branches.en: THE EFFECT: front and mid positions introduce what follows.
branches.cn: 效果：句首与句中引出后续。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: of turns the phrase backward to a noun or an activity.
branches.cn: 原因：介词把短语转向名词或活动。

branches.en: THE CHAIN: research and logic use it to draw a conclusion from evidence.
branches.cn: 链条：研究与逻辑用它从证据推出结论。

branches.en: THE REGISTER: the longer noun carries more weight than the short phrase.
branches.cn: 语域：较长名词比短说法更有分量。

branches.en: THE LOSS: what follows unavoidably is often unwelcome.
branches.cn: 损失：不可避免的后续常不受欢迎。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin noun of following with English prepositions; the follow root is the core.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语「跟随」名词与英语介词结合；「跟随」词根是核心。

latinIntro.en: The Latin etyma are consequi, to follow after, and sequi, to follow.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词源是 consequi「跟随」与 sequi「跟随」。

items.example: The verb also gives sequence and sequel.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词也给出两个相关英语词。

items.example: The prefix binds the following to its source.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把「跟随」绑到源头。

items.example: The noun names the effect itself.
items.exampleCN: 名词直接指效果。

items.example: English keeps both the effect and the weight senses.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留「结果」与「分量」两义。

items.example: The adjective describes what follows.
items.exampleCN: 形容词描述随之而来的东西。

items.example: The adverb marks a result in one word.
items.exampleCN: 副词用一个词标记结果。

items.example: The adjective stresses weight rather than order.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词强调分量而非顺序。

items.example: The phrase is the formal result marker.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语是正式的结果标记。

definition_zh: 黑色素
definition_en: the dark brown or black pigment produced in skin, hair, eyes, feathers and some other tissues
core_image: 皮肤基底层里一排装满深褐色颗粒的细胞，像一排小墨囊
scene: 同一双眼睛在强光下显得近乎黑色。 More melanin in the iris makes the eyes look dark brown rather than blue.
sceneCN: 这里 melanin 指「决定皮肤、毛发与眼睛深浅的深色色素」（第 1 个义项：黑色素在组织中的含量决定颜色深浅）；句意为虹膜中黑色素越多，眼睛就越呈深褐色而不是蓝色。图中可辨识物件：虹膜、深褐与浅蓝的对照、一束强光。

pos.zh: 黑色素（不可数）

senses.title: Pigment of skin and hair
senses.titleCN: 皮肤与毛发中的黑色素
senses.definition: the brown-black pigment produced by melanocytes that determines the shade of skin and hair
senses.definitionCN: 黑色素细胞产生的棕黑色色素，决定皮肤与毛发的深浅
senses.example: More melanin in the iris makes the eyes look dark brown rather than blue.
senses.exampleCN: 虹膜中黑色素越多，眼睛就越呈深褐色而不是蓝色。
senses.why: The Greek word for black gave the pigment its name; the amount, not the presence, sets the visible colour.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语中表示「黑」的词给了这种色素名称；决定可见颜色的是含量，而不是有无。

senses.title: Pigment in the iris
senses.definition: melanin in the front layers of the iris, whose density produces brown, hazel or apparently blue eyes
senses.definitionCN: 虹膜前层中的黑色素，其密度形成褐色、淡褐色或看似蓝色的眼睛
senses.example: Blue eyes contain little melanin, so light scatters at short wavelengths.
senses.exampleCN: 蓝眼睛含黑色素很少，光线在短波长上散射。
senses.why: The iris is a thin pigmented layer, so its colour is read directly from melanin density.
senses.whyCN: 虹膜是一层薄薄的带色素组织，其颜色直接由黑色素密度读出。

senses.title: Pigment in feathers and fur
senses.titleCN: 羽毛与毛皮中的黑色素
senses.definition: melanin deposited in feathers or hair that produces black, brown and grey coats
senses.definitionCN: 沉积在羽毛或毛发中的黑色素，形成黑、褐、灰色被毛
senses.example: The crow's black feathers are dense with melanin.
senses.exampleCN: 乌鸦的黑色羽毛中黑色素很密。
senses.why: Feathers are dead tissue packed with pigment, the same surface logic as skin.
senses.whyCN: 羽毛是装满色素的死组织，与皮肤遵循同一表面逻辑。

senses.title: Pigment in insect cuticle
senses.definition: melanin in the outer skeleton of insects that darkens the cuticle and hardens it
senses.definitionCN: 昆虫外骨骼中的黑色素，使表皮变深并增强硬度
senses.example: Melanin thickens the beetle's cuticle as well as darkening it.
senses.exampleCN: 黑色素既加深甲虫表皮的颜色，也使它更坚硬。
senses.why: In insects melanin also hardens the cuticle, so the pigment serves structure as well as colour.
senses.whyCN: 在昆虫中，黑色素还使表皮硬化，因此它既供颜色也供结构。

senses.title: Pigment in fungi
senses.definition: melanin produced by fungi that protects them from radiation, enzymes and immune attack
senses.definitionCN: 真菌产生的黑色素，保护它们免受辐射、酶与免疫攻击
senses.example: Many soil fungi use melanin as a shield against ultraviolet light.
senses.exampleCN: 许多土壤真菌把黑色素当作抵御紫外线的盾牌。
senses.why: Fungi use the same dark polymer as a shield, extending the name beyond animals.
senses.whyCN: 真菌用同一种深色聚合物作盾牌，把这个名称扩展到动物之外。

senses.title: Natural sunscreen
senses.definition: the function of melanin in absorbing ultraviolet radiation before it damages DNA
senses.definitionCN: 黑色素在紫外线损伤 DNA 之前将其吸收的功能
senses.example: Melanin absorbs part of the ultraviolet light that reaches the skin.
senses.exampleCN: 黑色素吸收了到达皮肤的一部分紫外线。
senses.why: The pigment's colour is a consequence of its light absorption, so protection becomes a named function.
senses.whyCN: 色素的颜色是其吸光的后果，于是保护成了被命名的功能。

senses.title: Pigment in cephalopod ink
senses.titleCN: 头足类墨汁中的黑色素
senses.definition: the melanin that gives squid and octopus ink its dark colour
senses.definitionCN: 使鱿鱼与章鱼墨汁呈深色的黑色素
senses.example: The squid's ink owes its blackness to melanin.
senses.exampleCN: 鱿鱼墨汁的黑色来自黑色素。
senses.why: Squid ink is a concentrated suspension of the same pigment, used as a screen rather than a colour.
senses.whyCN: 鱿鱼墨汁是同一色素的浓缩悬浮液，用作烟幕而非颜色。

senses.title: Synthetic melanin in materials research
senses.titleCN: 材料研究中的合成黑色素
senses.definition: laboratory-made melanin used to study pigmentation or to build light-absorbing materials
senses.definitionCN: 实验室制造的黑色素，用于研究色素或制造吸光材料
senses.example: The team grew a synthetic melanin film that absorbs nearly all visible light.
senses.exampleCN: 团队培育出一种合成黑色素薄膜，几乎吸收全部可见光。
senses.why: Once the polymer can be synthesized, the biological noun follows it into materials science.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这种聚合物可以合成，生物名词就跟着它进入材料科学。

intro.en: Melanin joins Greek melas, genitive melanos, 'black, dark', to the chemical suffix -in. It was coined in the early nineteenth century for the dark pigment of tissue. No reliable Latin relative exists, so the Latin list is empty.
intro.cn: melanin 把希腊 melas（属格 melanos）「黑的、暗的」与化学后缀 -in 结合，于 19 世纪初为组织中的深色色素造出。没有可靠的拉丁同族词，故拉丁条目留空。

items.en: Greek melas, genitive melanos, meant 'black, dark' and supplied the first element of the name.
items.cn: 希腊 melas（属格 melanos）意为「黑的、暗的」，提供名称的第一个成分。

items.en: The suffix -in, used for substances such as proteins and pigments, came through French -ine from Latin -ina.
items.cn: 用于蛋白质与色素等物质名称的后缀 -in，经法语 -ine 来自拉丁 -ina。

items.en: The term is generally dated to the 1830s, when chemists isolated the dark pigment of the eye and of tumours.
items.cn: 这个术语一般认为是 1830 年代所造，当时化学家从眼睛与肿瘤中分离出深色色素。

items.en: Twentieth-century work identified melanin as a family of polymers rather than one compound, so the word now covers several related pigments.
items.cn: 20 世纪的研究确认黑色素是一族聚合物而非单一化合物，因此这个词现在覆盖数种相关色素。

items.en: Greek melas is often linked to a reconstructed Indo-European root for 'dark, black'; the link is a reconstruction, not a recorded form.
items.cn: 希腊 melas 常被联系到一个重构的印欧词根，意为「暗、黑」；此联系属重构形式，并非有记录的形式。

items.en: Source uncertain (root and first date): the Indo-European root is reconstructed, the Greek word's earlier history is unclear, and the 1830s coinage date is approximate. The Greek melas layer is secure.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：印欧词根属重构，希腊词更早的历史不清楚，1830 年代的造词年代为约数；希腊 melas 这一层可靠。

note.en: Group one separates the pigment from the cells, bodies and conditions named after it; group two separates the main biological pigments by colour and chemistry.
note.cn: 第一组把黑色素与以它命名的细胞、结构和病症分开；第二组按颜色与化学性质区分主要生物色素。

entries.definition: The cell that produces melanin; melanin is the substance it makes.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生黑色素的细胞；melanin 是它制造的物。

entries.definition: The organelle inside a melanocyte that carries melanin; it is a container, not the pigment.
entries.definitionCN: 指黑色素细胞内装载黑色素的细胞器；是容器，不是色素本身。

entries.definition: The condition of being unusually dark because of excess melanin; the pigment is the cause, not the condition.
entries.definitionCN: 指因黑色素过多而异常深色的状态；色素是成因，不是状态。

entries.definition: A cancer of melanin-producing cells; the name is built on melanin but denotes a disease.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生黑色素的细胞所患的癌症；名称由 melanin 构成，但指一种疾病。

entries.definition: Any colouring substance; melanin is one specific dark pigment among many.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何着色物质；melanin 只是众多种深色色素中的一种。

entries.definition: The brown-to-black form of melanin; the word melanin also covers the reddish pheomelanin.
entries.definitionCN: 指黑色素中棕黑的一型；melanin 一词也包含偏红的褐黑色素。

entries.definition: The red-yellow form of melanin found in hair and freckles; it is a subtype, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 指毛发与雀斑中偏红黄的黑色素类型；是亚型，不是同义词。

entries.definition: An orange plant pigment stored in fat; it is chemically unrelated to melanin.
entries.definitionCN: 指储存在脂肪中的橙色植物色素；与黑色素在化学上无关。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek word for black, the real chemical suffix, and the genuine medical family built on the term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊语「黑」、真实的化学后缀，以及由该术语构成的真实医学词族。

normal.en: melas 'black' + -in: the black substance.
normal.cn: melas「黑」+ -in：黑色的物质。

normal.en: The family runs melanin, melanocyte, melanosome, melanoma, melanism.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 melanin、melanocyte、melanosome、melanoma、melanism。

normal.en: Two subtypes: eumelanin for brown-black, pheomelanin for red-yellow.
normal.cn: 两个亚型：棕黑的真黑色素与红黄的褐黑色素。

normal.en: It colours skin, hair, iris, feathers, cuticle, fungi and ink.
normal.cn: 它给皮肤、毛发、虹膜、羽毛、表皮、真菌与墨汁上色。

normal.en: Its other job is shielding DNA from ultraviolet light.
normal.cn: 它的另一项职责是替 DNA 遮挡紫外线。

abstract.en: Picture a row of tiny ink sacs packed beneath the skin.
abstract.cn: 想象皮肤下排着一列小小的墨囊。

abstract.en: Picture an iris whose brown is the density of the dots behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只褐色的虹膜，那褐色就是背后小点的密度。

abstract.en: Picture a squid writing its escape in one black stroke.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鱿鱼用一道黑色笔触写下自己的逃脱。

examples.en: Melanin protects the skin by absorbing ultraviolet radiation.
examples.cn: 黑色素通过吸收紫外线保护皮肤。

examples.en: Albinism results from a failure to produce melanin.
examples.cn: 白化病源于无法产生黑色素。

examples.en: The fossil feather retained traces of melanin arranged like modern patterns.
examples.cn: 这块化石羽毛保留了黑色素痕迹，排列方式与现代图案相似。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「melan（黑）+ -in（素）」——让皮肤变黑的那种素 → 黑色素

root: 希腊 melas（属格 melanos）「黑的、暗的」+ 化学后缀 -in（经法语 -ine，出自拉丁 -ina）；更早的印欧词根为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one dark polymer: skin and hair, iris, feathers, insect shell, fungi, sun defence, squid ink and a laboratory film.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种深色聚合物展开：皮肤与毛发、虹膜、羽毛、昆虫外壳、真菌、防晒、鱿鱼墨汁与实验室薄膜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of dark granules packed under a thin layer of skin.
core.cn: 核心意象：薄薄一层皮肤下排满深色颗粒。

branches.en: BODY COLOUR: skin and iris shade report melanin density.
branches.cn: 身体颜色：皮肤与虹膜的深浅反映黑色素密度。

branches.en: FUNGI: moulds and yeasts make their own dark pigment.
branches.cn: 真菌：霉菌与酵母自行制造深色色素。

branches.en: PROTECTION: the pigment absorbs ultraviolet light before it reaches DNA.
branches.cn: 保护：色素在紫外线触及 DNA 之前将其吸收。

branches.en: SYNTHESIS: the same polymer can be grown as a film.
branches.cn: 合成：同一种聚合物可以被培育成薄膜。

branches.en: MATERIAL RANGE: feathers, cuticle and ink show the same chemistry in different tissues.
branches.cn: 材料范围：羽毛、表皮与墨汁展示同一化学在不同组织中的表现。

intro.en: Melanin is a Greek adjective stem plus the chemical suffix -in; later terms add Greek suffixes for cell, body and tumour.
intro.cn: melanin 是希腊语形容词词干加化学后缀 -in；后续术语再加希腊后缀表示细胞、体和肿瘤。

latinIntro.en: No Latin etymon is recoverable for melanin; the -in suffix reached English through French -ine from Latin -ina, but that is a suffix, not a root, so the Latin entry list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: melanin 无法追溯到拉丁词源；后缀 -in 虽经法语 -ine 来自拉丁 -ina，但那只是后缀而非词根，因此拉丁条目留空。

items.example: Melas is the Greek word behind the name.
items.exampleCN: melas 是名称背后的希腊词。

items.example: The suffix marks a named chemical substance.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记一种被命名的化学物质。

items.example: Melanin absorbs light across the visible range.
items.exampleCN: 黑色素吸收可见光范围内的光。

items.example: A melanocyte transfers pigment to skin cells.
items.exampleCN: 黑色素细胞把色素转交给皮肤细胞。

items.example: Each melanosome is a packet of granules.
items.exampleCN: 每个黑色素体都是一包颗粒。

items.example: Melanoma begins in pigment cells.
items.exampleCN: 黑素瘤起于色素细胞。

items.example: Melanism is common in some moths.
items.exampleCN: 黑化在某些蛾类中很常见。

items.example: A melanistic leopard is called a black panther.
items.exampleCN: 黑化的豹被称为黑豹。

items.example: Eumelanin dominates dark hair.
items.exampleCN: 真黑色素在深色毛发中占主导。

definition_zh: adj. 可疑的；靠不住的；半信半疑的；犹豫的
definition_en: probably not honest, safe or reliable; feeling doubt about something; of questionable value or quality
core_image: 一份合同里几处条款被荧光笔涂黄，签字的手停在半空；一个人歪着头看对方，一条眉毛挑起而嘴不动；货架上一罐标签褪色的果酱，盖子微微鼓起
scene: 合同里几处条款被荧光笔涂黄，签字的手停在半空，笔尖离纸面只差一厘米。 He was dubious about the clauses marked in yellow.
sceneCN: 这里 dubious 指「心存疑虑、不愿轻易接受」（第 2 个义项：半信半疑的）；句意是他对那些涂黄的条款半信半疑。图中可辨识物件：荧光笔涂黄的条款、停在半空的手、笔尖与纸面的一厘米间隙。

pos.zh: 可疑的；靠不住的；半信半疑的；犹豫的

senses.title: Not to be trusted
senses.definition: probably not honest, safe or reliable
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）很可能不诚实、不安全或不可靠的
senses.example: The firm made a dubious claim about its returns.
senses.exampleCN: 那家公司对收益提出了可疑的说法。
senses.why: A contract with clauses marked in yellow while the signing hand stops in mid air.
senses.whyCN: 一份合同里几处条款被涂黄，签字的手停在半空。

senses.title: Feeling doubt
senses.definition: feeling doubt about something and not ready to accept it
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）对某事心存疑虑、不愿轻易接受的
senses.example: He was dubious about the clauses marked in yellow.
senses.exampleCN: 他对那些涂黄的条款半信半疑。
senses.why: A head tilted to one side with one eyebrow raised and the mouth kept still.
senses.whyCN: 头歪向一侧，一条眉毛挑起，嘴却不动。

senses.title: Of doubtful quality
senses.definition: of questionable value, quality or usefulness
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）价值、质量或用处成问题的
senses.example: The shop sold sweets of dubious freshness.
senses.exampleCN: 那家店卖的糖果新鲜度成问题。
senses.why: A jar on a shelf with a faded label and a lid that bulges a little.
senses.whyCN: 货架上一罐标签褪色的果酱，盖子微微鼓起。

intro.en: Dubious comes from Latin dubius, moving in two directions: a mind that can go either way has not settled, so the word first described the thing that causes doubt and later the person who feels it.
intro.cn: dubious 来自拉丁语 dubius「朝两个方向移动」：一颗能往两边走的心还没有定下来，所以这个词先指引起怀疑的事物，后来也指心存疑虑的人。

items.en: Latin duo means two.
items.cn: 拉丁语 duo 意为二。

items.en: Latin dubius means moving in two directions, hence uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dubius 意为朝两个方向移动，因而指不确定。

items.en: Latin dubitare means to doubt or to hesitate.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dubitare 意为怀疑或犹豫。

items.en: English dubious is borrowed for something that causes doubt.
items.cn: 英语 dubious 被借入，指引起怀疑的事物。

items.en: The word is also used of a person who feels doubt.
items.cn: 这个词也用于指心存疑虑的人。

items.en: Dubious now covers unsafe claims, hesitant people and goods of doubtful quality.
items.cn: dubious 如今涵盖不可靠的说法、犹豫的人与质量成问题的货物。

note.en: Dubious shares its ending with obvious and previous, while its neighbours name other shades of not being sure.
note.cn: dubious 与 obvious、previous 共用词尾，而它的近义词则指「拿不准」的其他层次。

dict_mnemonic.text: dubious ＝ 拉丁语 dubius（朝两个方向移动）＋ -ous（形容词后缀）。心往两边走，就是「拿不定」：说事物是「可疑的」（a dubious claim），说人是「半信半疑的」（be dubious about），说质量是「靠不住的」（of dubious value）。同源的 doubt、dubitable 都带着这个「二」；反义词 obvious 是「摆在眼前、无需怀疑」。

root: 拉丁语 duo（二）→ dubius（朝两个方向、不确定）→ dubitare（怀疑）→ 英语 dubious（可疑的；半信半疑的）
