definition_zh: 热液的；水热作用的（指热水或热流体在岩层与海底循环所形成的地质过程）
definition_en: relating to hot water or hot fluids circulating through rock, especially in the crust beneath the seafloor
core_image: 海水沿裂缝渗入灼热的岩层，被加热后又带着溶解的矿物喷回海底
scene: 科研人员从岩脊的裂缝中取到一管滚烫的矿物流体。 Scientists sampled the hydrothermal fluids escaping from the ridge.
sceneCN: 这里 hydrothermal 指「与地下热水或热流体有关」（第 1 个义项：泛指由热流体参与的地质过程与产物）；句意为科学家采集从洋脊逸出的热液流体。

pos.zh: 热液的；水热作用的（地质学中指热水或热流体参与的过程）

derivatives.zh: therm-（希腊 thermē「热」）+ -al（形容词后缀）→ 热的：热量的、保暖的
hydrothermal + -ly（副词后缀）→ 以热液方式：经由热水或热流体作用地
hydrothermal + -ism（表过程或体系的名词后缀）→ 热液活动：热流体循环这一整套过程
geo-（希腊「大地」）+ thermal（热）→ 地热的：来自地球内部热量的（与 hydrothermal 共享 thermal 词根）

senses.title: Relating to hot water processes
senses.titleCN: 热液的：由热水或热流体参与的地质过程
senses.definition: concerning geological processes in which hot water or hot fluids move through rock
senses.definitionCN: 指热水或热流体在岩石中运移所形成的地质过程
senses.example: Scientists sampled the hydrothermal fluids escaping from the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家采集从洋脊逸出的热液流体。
senses.why: hydro- supplies water and thermal supplies heat, so the adjective simply names processes in which both are present.
senses.whyCN: hydro- 提供水，thermal 提供热，这个形容词因此直接命名同时具备两者的过程。

senses.title: Seawater heated by magma
senses.titleCN: 海水被岩浆加热的循环
senses.definition: the circulation in which seawater sinks into hot rock, is heated, and rises again
senses.definitionCN: 海水下渗进入灼热岩石、被加热后再上升的循环
senses.example: Hydrothermal circulation transfers heat from magma to the ocean.
senses.exampleCN: 热液循环把热量从岩浆传送到海洋。
senses.why: the adjective describes the fluid, and the circulation is the large-scale version of that same hot fluid moving.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词描述流体，而循环正是同一种热流体在大尺度上运动。

senses.title: Alteration of the surrounding rock
senses.titleCN: 热液蚀变：热流体改变岩石
senses.definition: the chemical change of rock caused by hot fluids passing through it
senses.definitionCN: 热流体穿过岩石时引起的化学变化
senses.example: Hydrothermal alteration turned the basalt into clay minerals.
senses.exampleCN: 热液蚀变把玄武岩变成了黏土矿物。
senses.why: hot water carries dissolved substances, so wherever it passes it exchanges material with the rock.
senses.whyCN: 热水携带溶解物质，因此它经过之处都会与岩石交换物质。

senses.title: The vent environment
senses.definition: the setting around a seafloor opening where hot fluid discharges
senses.definitionCN: 热流体从海底开口排出处的周边环境
senses.example: Hydrothermal conditions support chemosynthetic bacteria.
senses.exampleCN: 热液环境供养化能合成细菌。
senses.why: the adjective commonly modifies vent, field and plume, naming the environment rather than a single object.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词常修饰 vent、field 与 plume，命名的是环境，而不只是单个物体。

senses.title: Ore-forming hot fluids
senses.titleCN: 热液成矿：金属硫化物沉淀
senses.definition: the deposition of metal sulphides when hot mineral-rich fluid cools
senses.definitionCN: 富含金属的热流体冷却时沉淀出金属硫化物
senses.example: The deposit formed from hydrothermal solutions rich in copper.
senses.exampleCN: 该矿床由富含铜的热液沉淀形成。
senses.why: cooling fluid cannot hold its dissolved metals, so they settle out where the hot water meets cold seawater.
senses.whyCN: 热流体冷却后无法继续溶解金属，于是它们在热水与冷海水相遇处沉淀下来。

senses.title: Laboratory hydrothermal synthesis
senses.definition: a method of growing crystals in hot water under pressure
senses.definitionCN: 在高温高压的水中生长晶体的方法
senses.example: Quartz crystals are grown by a hydrothermal method.
senses.exampleCN: 石英晶体用水热法生长。
senses.why: the same two ingredients, water and heat, are used in a sealed vessel, so laboratory chemistry borrowed the geological adjective.
senses.whyCN: 同样的两个要素——水与热——被用在密闭容器里，于是实验室化学借用了这个地质形容词。

senses.title: Hydrothermal activity on other worlds
senses.titleCN: 其他天体上的热液活动
senses.definition: hot-fluid activity inferred beneath the icy crusts of other planets and moons
senses.definitionCN: 在其他行星与卫星冰壳之下推断出的热流体活动
senses.example: Hydrothermal activity is suspected beneath the ice of that moon.
senses.exampleCN: 那颗卫星的冰层之下疑似存在热液活动。
senses.why: the word describes a physical process rather than a place, so it travels to any body where water and heat meet.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述物理过程而非地点，因此可以迁移到任何水与热相遇的天体。

senses.title: A label in compound terms
senses.titleCN: 复合术语中的限定成分
senses.definition: the first element in fixed terms such as hydrothermal vent, field and plume
senses.definitionCN: 在 hydrothermal vent、field、plume 等固定术语中充当限定成分
senses.example: The hydrothermal plume spread hundreds of metres from the vent.
senses.exampleCN: 热液羽流从喷口扩散出数百米。
senses.why: technical English builds long names by stacking modifiers, and hydrothermal marks which kind of vent, field or plume is meant.
senses.whyCN: 技术英语靠层层修饰构成长名，hydrothermal 标明是何种喷口、热液场或羽流。

intro.en: Hydrothermal is built from two Greek roots and is a modern scientific coinage rather than an inherited word. Hydro- goes back to Greek hydor 'water', and thermal goes back to Greek therme 'heat'. Latin has no cognates of either root. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: hydrothermal 由两个希腊词根构成，是近代科学新造词，而非承继词。hydro- 上溯希腊 hydor「水」，thermal 上溯希腊 therme「热」。两个词根在拉丁语中都没有同族词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Hydor, with the stem hydat-, meant 'water' and appears in English in hydrology, hydrogen and dehydration.
items.cn: hydor（词干 hydat-）意为「水」，出现在英语的 hydrology、hydrogen 与 dehydration 中。

items.en: Therme meant 'heat' and also named hot springs; it produced thermal, thermometer and thermos.
items.cn: therme 意为「热」，也用来称温泉；它衍生出 thermal、thermometer 与 thermos。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geologists needed one adjective for the action of hot water on rock and combined the two roots to make it.
items.cn: 十九世纪的地质学家需要一个形容词来描述热水对岩石的作用，于是把两个词根合成了它。

items.en: The term spread through the study of ore deposits, where hot fluids were recognised as the carriers of metals.
items.cn: 这个词在矿床研究中传播开来，因为人们认识到热流体是金属的搬运者。

items.en: After the discovery of seafloor vents in the late twentieth century, hydrothermal became a standard word in oceanography and biology.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期海底喷口被发现后，hydrothermal 成为海洋学与生物学的标准用词。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Greek origin of hydor is debated, and forms such as *wed- are reconstructions rather than attested words.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源存疑）：hydor 在希腊语之前的来源有争议，*wed- 一类形式属重构，而非有书证的词。

note.en: Group one holds the heat-related adjectives most often confused with hydrothermal; group two holds the process words that name the same setting from other angles.
note.cn: 第一组是常与 hydrothermal 混淆的热相关形容词；第二组是从别的角度命名同一环境的近义词。

entries.definition: Relating to heat from the Earth's interior; it does not require water, whereas hydrothermal always involves hot fluid.
entries.definitionCN: 指来自地球内部的热；不要求有水，而 hydrothermal 始终涉及热流体。

entries.definition: Relating to the movement and distribution of water; heat plays no part in the definition.
entries.definitionCN: 指水的运动与分布；定义中不含热。

entries.definition: Relating to heat or temperature in general; it is the second half of hydrothermal but lacks the water element.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指与热或温度有关；它是 hydrothermal 的后半，但没有水的成分。

entries.definition: The seafloor opening itself; hydrothermal alone describes the process or the fluid, not the opening.
entries.definitionCN: 指海底的那个开口本身；单用 hydrothermal 描述过程或流体，不指开口。

entries.definition: Relating to magma; it names the heat source, while hydrothermal names the water that the magma heats.
entries.definitionCN: 指与岩浆有关；它命名热源，而 hydrothermal 命名被岩浆加热的水。

entries.definition: Relating to volcanoes and their products; a hydrothermal system may be volcanic in origin but need not erupt.
entries.definitionCN: 指火山及其产物；热液系统可能源于火山，但并不需要喷发。

entries.definition: Relating to water in solution; it says nothing about temperature, which is the point of hydrothermal.
entries.definitionCN: 指水溶液中的；不涉及温度，而温度正是 hydrothermal 的要点。

entries.definition: Beneath the sea; it gives the setting but not the hot-fluid process.
entries.definitionCN: 指海面之下；只给出环境，不含热流体过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: two real Greek roots and real technical compounds, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的希腊词根与真实的技术复合词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: hydro- means water, thermal means heat: hydrothermal is exactly water plus heat.
normal.cn: hydro- 是水，thermal 是热：hydrothermal 就是水加热。

normal.en: The pair of roots also builds hydrology and thermometer, so the family is easy to read.
normal.cn: 同一对词根还构成 hydrology 与 thermometer，词族容易读懂。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: hydrothermal vent, hydrothermal field, hydrothermal plume.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：热液喷口、热液场、热液羽流。

normal.en: The process has three steps: seawater sinks, rock heats it, mineral-rich water rises.
normal.cn: 这个过程有三步：海水下渗、岩石加热、富含矿物的水上升。

normal.en: Ore deposits are the trace it leaves: metals precipitate where hot fluid meets cold seawater.
normal.cn: 矿床是它留下的痕迹：金属在热流体与冷海水相遇处沉淀。

abstract.en: Hydrothermal is the ocean breathing through hot stone.
abstract.cn: 热液是海洋透过灼热石头在呼吸。

abstract.en: It is a kitchen under pressure: water, heat and dissolved minerals in a sealed pot of rock.
abstract.cn: 它是一间加压的厨房：水、热与溶解矿物装在岩石这只密封锅里。

abstract.en: Where hot water meets cold sea, the invisible becomes stone.
abstract.cn: 热水与冷海相遇之处，看不见的东西变成了石头。

examples.en: Hydrothermal fluids carry dissolved metals from deep rock to the seafloor.
examples.cn: 热液把溶解的金属从深部岩石带到海底。

examples.en: The team mapped a hydrothermal field along the spreading ridge.
examples.cn: 团队沿扩张洋脊测绘了一处热液场。

examples.en: Hydrothermal alteration left a pale band in the dark basalt.
examples.cn: 热液蚀变在深色玄武岩中留下一条浅色带。

dict_mnemonic.text: hydro（水）+ thermal（热）＝热水参与的；记成「水加热，穿石头，带矿物，回海底」。

root: 希腊 hydor「水」+ 希腊 therme「热」；为十九世纪科学新造词，两个词根在拉丁语中均无同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hot fluid: it circulates, alters rock, marks an environment, deposits ore, is imitated in a lab, works on other worlds and finally becomes a fixed label in compound terms.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种热流体展开：它循环、改变岩石、标出环境、沉淀矿床、被实验室仿效、在其他天体上运作，最后成为复合术语中的固定标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cold seawater slips into hot rock and returns carrying dissolved minerals.
core.cn: 核心意象：冷海水渗入灼热岩石，再带着溶解的矿物回来。

branches.en: THE CYCLE: water plus heat is first a general process, then a measurable circulation.
branches.cn: 循环：水加热先是泛指的过程，再是可测量的循环。

branches.en: ROCK CHANGED: passing fluid exchanges matter with the wall rock.
branches.cn: 岩石被改变：流经的流体与围岩交换物质。

branches.en: VENT AND ORE: the discharge point, and the metals that settle out of it.
branches.cn: 喷口与矿石：排出口，以及从中沉淀的金属。

branches.en: LABORATORY COPY: the same water and heat reproduced in a sealed vessel.
branches.cn: 实验室复制：同样的水与热在密闭容器中被重现。

branches.en: OTHER WORLDS AND FIXED LABELS: the process travels, and the word becomes a modifier.
branches.cn: 其他天体与固定标签：过程可以迁移，词本身变成限定成分。

intro.en: Hydrothermal is a combining-form compound: two bound Greek roots joined by a linking vowel, with no prefix of its own.
intro.cn: hydrothermal 是组合形式构成的复合词：两个黏着希腊词根以连接元音相接，本身不带前缀。

latinIntro.en: Both roots are Greek, so there are no Latin entries. Latin aqua 'water' and calor 'heat' express the same ideas from different roots and are not cognates.
latinIntro.cn: 两个词根都属希腊语，因此没有拉丁条目。拉丁 aqua「水」与 calor「热」用不同词根表达相同概念，并非同源。

items.example: Hydro- appears in hydrology and hydroelectric.
items.exampleCN: hydro- 出现在 hydrology 与 hydroelectric 中。

items.example: Hydor is the Greek source of the combining form.
items.exampleCN: hydor 是这个组合形式的希腊语来源。

items.example: Therme also named warm baths.
items.exampleCN: therme 也用来称温水浴场。

items.example: Thermal springs feed the pool.
items.exampleCN: 温泉为这个水池供水。

items.meaning: relating to hot water in rock
items.example: Hydrothermal fluids altered the basalt.
items.exampleCN: 热液改变了玄武岩。

items.example: Hydrothermalism shaped the ridge crest.
items.exampleCN: 热液活动塑造了洋脊顶部。

items.example: The hydrothermal vent supports dense life.
items.exampleCN: 这个热液喷口供养密集的生物。

items.meaning: a group of vents in one area
items.meaningCN: 同一区域内的一组喷口
items.example: The hydrothermal field extends for a kilometre.
items.exampleCN: 这处热液场延伸一公里。

items.meaning: the rising cloud of hot particle-rich water
items.meaningCN: 上升的、富含颗粒的热水云
items.example: A hydrothermal plume rose above the vent.
items.exampleCN: 一团热液羽流升到喷口上方。

items.example: Geothermal power uses steam from hot rock.
items.exampleCN: 地热发电利用热岩产生的蒸汽。

definition_zh: 隐私；不受他人打扰的状态，以及对个人信息的控制权
definition_en: the state of being free from public attention or disturbance, and the control a person has over personal information
core_image: 一间只亮着一盏灯的屋子，窗帘拉严，门外的人只能看见布上的影子，却进不来
scene: 深夜的屋子里只亮着一盏台灯，窗帘拉得很严，门外的人只能看见布上的影子。 She drew the curtain because privacy mattered more to her than the view.
sceneCN: 这里 privacy 指不受他人注视与打扰的状态（第 1 个义项：独处不受扰）；句意：她拉上窗帘，因为对她来说，不被打扰比窗外的景色更重要。

pos.zh: 隐私；私生活；独处不受扰；信息控制权

senses.title: Freedom from being disturbed
senses.definition: the condition of being alone and free from other people's interruption
senses.definitionCN: 独处且不被他人打断的状态
senses.example: He reads in the garden for an hour of privacy each morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天早上在花园里读一小时书，享受不被打扰的时光。
senses.why: the Latin adjective described something withdrawn from public life, and withdrawal begins as simple freedom from company.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁形容词指从公共生活中退开，而退开最初就是免于他人陪伴。

senses.title: Freedom from public attention
senses.definition: the state of not being watched, reported on or discussed by the public
senses.definitionCN: 不被公众注视、报道或议论的状态
senses.example: The family moved inland to raise the children in privacy.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人搬到内陆，想在不受注视的环境里抚养孩子。
senses.why: publicity is the opposite pole, and the word names the absence of it rather than the presence of walls.
senses.whyCN: 「公开」是对立的一端，这个词指公开的缺席，而不是墙的存在。

senses.title: Control over one's own information
senses.definition: a person's power to decide who learns what about them
senses.definitionCN: 个人决定谁能知道自己哪些情况的权力
senses.example: Privacy means the choice to tell, not the duty to hide.
senses.exampleCN: 隐私意味着「可以选择说」，而不是「必须藏」。
senses.why: once information could be copied and shared at scale, withdrawal became a matter of control rather than of distance.
senses.whyCN: 当信息能被大规模复制与共享，退开就从「隔开距离」变成了「掌握控制权」。

senses.title: Data privacy as a field of practice
senses.titleCN: 数据隐私这一实务领域
senses.definition: the handling of personal data by organisations under rules of collection, use and deletion
senses.definitionCN: 机构按收集、使用与删除规则处理个人数据
senses.example: The company hired a lawyer to lead its data privacy work.
senses.exampleCN: 公司聘请了一位律师主管数据隐私工作。
senses.why: a social value is turned into a managed operation, and its name follows the operation.
senses.whyCN: 一项社会价值被转化为可管理的业务，其名称便随业务走。

senses.title: The legal right to seclusion
senses.definition: the recognised claim that others may not intrude into one's personal sphere
senses.definitionCN: 被承认的、他人不得侵入个人领域的主张
senses.example: The court treated privacy as a limit on how evidence may be gathered.
senses.exampleCN: 法院把隐私视为取证方式的一条界限。
senses.why: a value argued in courts becomes a right, and the abstract noun carries that legal weight.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭上被论证的价值会变成一项权利，这个抽象名词便承担了法律分量。

senses.title: Settings that limit visibility
senses.definition: the options in an app or account that decide who can see what
senses.definitionCN: 应用或账号中决定谁能看到什么的选择项
senses.example: She changed her privacy so that only friends could see the album.
senses.exampleCN: 她改动了隐私设置，只有好友能看到那本相册。
senses.why: when exposure is governed by menus, the value word is used for the switches themselves.
senses.whyCN: 当曝光由菜单控制时，这个价值名词就被用来指那些开关。

senses.title: Confidentiality of a matter
senses.definition: the quality of a discussion or document that stays within a trusted circle
senses.definitionCN: 谈话或文件只留在可信圈子内的性质
senses.example: They asked for privacy during the settlement talks.
senses.exampleCN: 他们要求和解谈判过程保持保密。
senses.why: a thing kept from outsiders is private in the old sense, and the abstract noun covers that condition.
senses.whyCN: 不让外人知道的事在旧义上就是「私下的」，抽象名词涵盖这种状态。

senses.title: Physical seclusion of a place
senses.definition: the shielding of a room or home from view, sound or entry
senses.definitionCN: 房间或住宅在视线、声音与进入上受到的遮蔽
senses.example: The hedge gives the terrace a little privacy from the road.
senses.exampleCN: 那道树篱让露台与马路之间有了一点遮蔽。
senses.why: walls, hedges and curtains are the oldest tools of withdrawal, so the word attaches to physical shelter.
senses.whyCN: 墙、树篱与窗帘是「退开」最古老的工具，因此这个词也依附于实体的遮蔽。

senses.title: Protection against surveillance
senses.definition: the expectation that states and companies will not track a person without cause
senses.definitionCN: 国家对个人的追踪需有正当理由这一期待
senses.example: Cameras on every corner turned privacy into a public argument.
senses.exampleCN: 街角的摄像头把隐私变成了公共议题。
senses.why: the word sharpens when watching becomes cheap, because the old freedom now needs defending.
senses.whyCN: 当「观看」变得廉价，这个词就变得尖锐，因为旧的自由如今需要辩护。

senses.title: Personal space in shared settings
senses.titleCN: 共享场所中的个人空间
senses.definition: the informal room a person keeps around themselves among others
senses.definitionCN: 在他人之间为自己留出的非正式余地
senses.example: Open desks leave almost no privacy for a phone call.
senses.exampleCN: 开放式工位几乎不给人打电话的私人余地。
senses.why: the word stretches from legal seclusion to the small distance people maintain in a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从法律的清静延伸到人群中人们维持的那点距离。

intro.en: Privacy comes from Latin privatus, withdrawn from public office and belonging to oneself. The abstract ending -acy names a state, so the word names a condition rather than a thing.
intro.cn: privacy 来自拉丁语 privatus，指「退出公职、属于个人」。抽象词尾 -acy 表示状态，因此这个词指一种处境，而不是一件东西。

items.en: Latin privus meant single, each for itself, and the derived verb privare meant to set apart or deprive.
items.cn: 拉丁语 privus 意为「单个的、各自的」，派生动词 privare 意为「分开、剥夺」。

items.en: Privatus described a person withdrawn from public office, a private citizen as opposed to a magistrate.
items.cn: privatus 描述退出公职的人，即与官员相对的普通公民。

items.en: French privé carried the sense of personal or secluded, and English borrowed the adjective as private.
items.cn: 法语 privé 带有「个人的、僻静的」之意，英语借入形容词 private。

items.en: The ending -acy, from Latin -acia, turns an adjective into the name of a state, so privacy is the state of being private.
items.cn: 词尾 -acy 来自拉丁 -acia，把形容词变成状态之名，因此 privacy 就是「处于私人状态」。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word moved from seclusion to information, as records became easy to copy and share.
items.cn: 二十世纪，随着记录变得易于复制与共享，这个词从「清静」转向「信息」。

items.en: Source uncertain: the link between privus and the wider family of Latin separating words is debated, and the deeper forms are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：privus 与拉丁语中其他表示「分开」的词是否同源仍有争论，更古的形式属于重构形式。

note.en: The first group is built on the same private root; the second group is the neighbouring ideas of secrecy, solitude and protection.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个「私人」词根上；第二组是保密、独处与保护这些相邻概念。

entries.definition: Belonging to a person rather than the public; a private room is the place where privacy is possible.
entries.definitionCN: 属于个人而非公众；private 的房间就是能有 privacy 的地方。

entries.definition: In a way that avoids public view; it describes how something is done, not the state itself.
entries.definitionCN: 以避开公众视线的方式；它描述做事方式，而不是状态本身。

entries.definition: To take something away from someone; it comes from the same Latin verb of setting apart but means loss, not seclusion.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从某人处拿走；出自同一个表示「分开」的拉丁动词，但指失去，不是清静。

entries.definition: A special right granted to a person or group; the root idea of a private law applied to one party survives here.
entries.definitionCN: 授予个人或群体的特殊权利；这里保留的是「针对一方的私人法规」这一词根含义。

entries.definition: The keeping of information from others; privacy protects a person's sphere, secrecy hides a fact.
entries.definitionCN: 把信息瞒住；privacy 保护个人领域，secrecy 隐藏某个事实。

entries.definition: The state of being alone, often chosen for calm; privacy can be enjoyed in company by being left undisturbed.
entries.definitionCN: 独处的状态，常为求安宁而选择；privacy 也可以在人群中通过不被打扰而获得。

entries.definition: The obligation not to pass on information given in trust; it is a duty, while privacy is a condition or right.
entries.definitionCN: 不转述受托信息的义务；它是义务，而 privacy 是状态或权利。

entries.definition: The state of not being identified; privacy may keep a known person unobserved, anonymity removes the name itself.
entries.definitionCN: 不被识别的状态；privacy 可让已知的人不被注视，anonymity 则连名字都去掉。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the real Latin root and the real legal and technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自真实拉丁词根与真实的法律、技术搭配。

normal.en: The adjective is private and the state is privacy: the ending -acy names a condition.
normal.cn: 形容词是 private，状态名词是 privacy：词尾 -acy 表示状态。

normal.en: The old sense is a private citizen withdrawn from office, not a secret kept from a friend.
normal.cn: 旧义是退出公职的普通公民，而不是对朋友隐瞒的秘密。

normal.en: Fixed phrases run from law to software: right to privacy, privacy policy, privacy settings.
normal.cn: 固定搭配从法律延伸到软件：隐私权、隐私政策、隐私设置。

normal.en: The verb is invade or protect: privacy is something done to, not something done.
normal.cn: 动词是 invade 或 protect：privacy 是被对待的对象，而不是动作。

normal.en: Data privacy is the modern centre of gravity of the word.
normal.cn: 数据隐私是这个词现代的重心所在。

abstract.en: Picture a lit room whose curtain lets light out but keeps eyes out.
abstract.cn: 想象一间亮灯的屋子，窗帘把光放出去，却把目光挡在外面。

abstract.en: Picture a door with no handle on the outside and no lock on the inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，外面没有把手，里面没有锁。

abstract.en: Picture a name written in water and read only by the person who wrote it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个写在水上的名字，只有写下它的人读得到。

examples.en: Privacy is not secrecy; it is the power to decide what is shared.
examples.cn: 隐私不是保密，而是决定分享什么的权力。

examples.en: The new rules give patients more privacy over their records.
examples.cn: 新规让患者对自己的病历拥有更多隐私掌控。

examples.en: A thin wall gave the neighbours almost no privacy.
examples.cn: 一堵薄墙几乎没给邻居留下任何私人空间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来（pri）为谁（vacy）」——扑过来想知道「为谁」，正是要守住隐私

root: 拉丁 privus「单个的、各自的」→ privare「分开、剥夺」→ privatus「退出公职的私人」→ 法语 privé → 英语 private；加 -acy（拉丁 -acia）表状态构成 privacy。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses start from being left alone, pass through public attention, information control, professional handling, legal right, app settings, confidentiality and physical shelter, and end at surveillance and shared space.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项从「不被打扰」出发，经过公众注视、信息控制、行业实务、法律权利、应用设置、保密与实体遮蔽，最后落在监控与共享空间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit room sealed by a curtain, visible as a glow from outside but not open to eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间亮灯的屋子被窗帘封住，外面只看见光，却看不进去。

branches.en: QUIET AND SHELTER: being undisturbed, and the walls or hedges that make it possible.
branches.cn: 清静与遮蔽：不被打扰，以及使之成为可能的墙与树篱。

branches.en: PUBLICITY AND WATCHING: the absence of public notice, and the defence of that absence against surveillance.
branches.cn: 公开与注视：不受公众关注，以及针对监控为这种缺席辩护。

branches.en: INFORMATION CONTROL: deciding who may know what about oneself.
branches.cn: 信息控制：决定谁能知道自己哪些情况。

branches.en: ROUTINE AND SETTINGS: organisational data handling, and the switches that govern visibility.
branches.cn: 实务与设置：机构的数据处理，以及控制可见性的开关。

branches.en: RIGHT, CONFIDENCE, SPACE: a legal claim, a confidential circle, and the small room kept in a crowd.
branches.cn: 权利、信任与空间：法律主张、可信圈子，以及在人群中留出的余地。

intro.en: Privacy is a Latin adjective turned into a state noun by the ending -acy; English later built private and privately from the same base.
intro.cn: privacy 是拉丁形容词加 -acy 构成的状态名词；英语后来又从同一词基造出 private 与 privately。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is privus, single or separate, with privatus as its adjective of withdrawal; -acia supplied the abstract ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 privus「单个的、分开的」，其形容词 privatus 表示退出；抽象词尾来自 -acia。

items.example: The adjective begins the idea of what belongs to one person.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词开启了「属于一个人」的观念。

items.example: The verb supplies both the sense of separation and of loss.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词同时提供「分开」与「失去」两层含义。

items.example: The adjective describes a private citizen rather than a magistrate.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述普通公民而非官员。

items.example: The ending turns the adjective into the name of a condition.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把形容词变成状态之名。

items.example: Private is the adjective behind the state noun.
items.exampleCN: private 是状态名词背后的形容词。

items.example: The adverb describes the manner of doing something.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词描述做某事的方式。

items.example: The prefixed verb names loss rather than seclusion.
items.exampleCN: 带前缀的动词指失去，而不是清静。

items.example: The same base appears in a word for a special right.
items.exampleCN: 同一词基也出现在表示特殊权利的词中。

items.example: The second element ties the word to a private law.
items.exampleCN: 第二个构件把这个词与「私人法规」联系起来。

definition_zh: 人工制品；文物；考古出土器物；（仪器或方法造成的）伪影、人为产物
definition_en: an object made by a person, especially one of historical or cultural interest; also a false feature produced by an instrument or method rather than by the thing being studied
core_image: 一只手把石块敲出刃口，几千年后手早已消失，那块石头还躺在土层里等人编号
scene: 考古系的学生在实验室里给一件石制小刀贴标签，标签上写着它出自哪一层土。 An archaeology student labels the artifact, a small stone blade, with the layer it came from.
sceneCN: 这里 artifact 指「由人制作、具有历史或文化价值的实物」（第 1 个义项：经人手加工并作为研究或收藏对象的器物）；句意为学生给这件石制小刀贴上标明出土层位的标签。可辨识物件：石刃、标签纸、卡尺、标本盒、记录本。

pos.zh: 人工制品；文物；出土器物
伪影；人为产物；由方法造成的假象

derivatives.zh: 人工制品（英式拼写，与 artifact 同义）
人工制品的；器物层面的

senses.title: A thing made by human skill
senses.titleCN: 人工制品：人手做出的实物
senses.definition: an object shaped or made by a person rather than formed by nature
senses.definitionCN: 由人加工制作、而非自然形成的实物
senses.example: The museum displays artifacts from the bronze age.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展出青铜时代的人工制品。
senses.why: Artifact joins ars, skill or craft, with factum, something made, so the literal reading is a thing made by skill; a natural stone becomes an artifact only after a hand has worked it.
senses.whyCN: artifact 由 ars「技艺、手艺」与 factum「做成之物」合成，字面就是「以手艺做成的东西」；天然石块要等人手加工之后才算 artifact。

senses.title: An excavated find
senses.titleCN: 出土器物：从遗址里取出的古物
senses.definition: a portable object recovered from an archaeological deposit and used to study past behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 从考古堆积中取出、用于研究过去行为的手持器物
senses.example: Fragments of pottery are the most common artifacts at the site.
senses.exampleCN: 陶片是该遗址最常见的出土器物。
senses.why: Archaeology narrows the word to what can be lifted, bagged and numbered; walls and ditches remain features, while movable things become artifacts.
senses.whyCN: 考古学把这个词收窄到能拿起、装袋、编号的物件；墙基与沟槽算遗迹，能移动的东西才叫 artifact。

senses.title: A false result from a method
senses.titleCN: 伪影：仪器或方法造成的假结果
senses.definition: a spurious feature in an observation that comes from the instrument, the sample preparation or the procedure rather than from the subject
senses.definitionCN: 观察中由仪器、样品制备或操作程序造成、并非研究对象本身的虚假特征
senses.example: The dark line on the scan is an artifact of the staining process.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描图上的那条暗线是染色过程造成的伪影。
senses.why: Once making is separated from the object, the word can also name what the procedure made: a mark the method added rather than found.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把「造」与「对象」分开，这个词也能指流程造出来的东西：图像里由方法添上、而非对象本身存在的部分。

senses.title: A digital glitch
senses.titleCN: 数字伪影：压缩或显示产生的杂点
senses.definition: a visible or audible fault introduced by compression, sampling or display rather than present in the original signal
senses.definitionCN: 由压缩、采样或显示引入、原信号中并不存在的可见或可听瑕疵
senses.example: Heavy compression left blocky artifacts around the edges.
senses.exampleCN: 过度压缩在边缘留下了方块状伪影。
senses.why: The scientific sense moved into computing unchanged: the tool chain itself leaves marks that look like part of the picture.
senses.whyCN: 科学的伪影义原样进入计算机领域：工具链自己留下的痕迹，看上去却像画面的一部分。

senses.title: A trace made by the medium
senses.titleCN: 照片上并非实物的影像
senses.definition: a mark on a photograph or film produced by the lens, the sensor or the processing rather than by the scene
senses.definitionCN: 由镜头、传感器或冲洗过程产生、并非场景中实物的影像痕迹
senses.example: The pale spot on the old print is a photographic artifact.
senses.exampleCN: 这张老照片上的浅色斑点是一处摄影伪影。
senses.why: Film and lenses have their own chemistry and geometry; dust, flare and scratches are made by the medium, so the same label fits.
senses.whyCN: 胶片与镜头有自己的化学与几何：灰尘、眩光和划痕是介质造出来的，因此用同一个标签。

senses.title: A byproduct of a system
senses.titleCN: 系统的产物：制度或设计造成的现象
senses.definition: a result that arises from the way a system is built or measured rather than from the thing it claims to describe
senses.definitionCN: 由系统的构造或测量方式产生、而非其所声称描述的对象本身的结果
senses.example: The apparent rise in cases was an artifact of the new reporting rule.
senses.exampleCN: 病例数看似上升，其实是新报告规则造成的产物。
senses.why: Abstracted from instruments, an artifact is any outcome manufactured by the frame: change the frame and the effect disappears.
senses.whyCN: 从仪器义抽象出来后，artifact 指由框架制造的任何结果：换掉框架，效应就消失。

senses.title: Cultural property in a collection
senses.titleCN: 藏品：作为文化财产被收藏的器物
senses.definition: an item held, catalogued and protected as cultural property, often subject to ownership and repatriation rules
senses.definitionCN: 作为文化财产被收藏、编目并保护、常涉及归属与归还规则的器物
senses.example: The government asked for the return of artifacts taken during the war.
senses.exampleCN: 政府要求归还战争期间被取走的文物。
senses.why: The museum and legal sense adds a claim: the object is not only made by humans but is valued as part of a heritage that can be owned.
senses.whyCN: 博物馆与法律义增加了一层主张：这件物品不仅由人制作，还被当作可被拥有的遗产来珍视。

senses.title: The made opposed to the natural
senses.titleCN: 人为之物：与自然物相对的技术造物
senses.definition: anything whose form is produced by human technique, used when contrasting the made with the grown
senses.definitionCN: 形态由人的技术产生之物，用于与自然生成之物对照
senses.example: Philosophers ask whether a city is an artifact or a natural growth.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家追问城市是人为之物还是自然生长之物。
senses.why: This is the oldest and widest reading: the moment skill shapes material, the result belongs to the class of made things, whatever its size.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老也最宽的读法：技艺一旦作用于材料，产物就归入「人造之物」，不论其规模大小。

intro.en: Artifact is a Latin phrase turned into one English word: arte, by skill, plus factum, a thing made. It entered English in the seventeenth century as a learned term and only later became the ordinary word for an excavated object. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: artifact 是把一个拉丁短语压成一个英语词：arte「以技艺」加 factum「做成之物」。它在十七世纪作为学术用语进入英语，后来才成为指称出土器物的常用词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin ars, genitive artis, meant skill, craft or technique; the ablative arte means by skill, and it is the form that appears inside artifact.
items.cn: 拉丁 ars（属格 artis）意为技艺、手艺或技术；夺格 arte 意为「以技艺」，正是出现在 artifact 里的形式。

items.en: Facere meant to make or do; its supine factum supplied both the noun thing made and the ending that builds factory, manufacture and factitious.
items.cn: facere 意为制作、做；其目的动名词 factum 既提供名词「做成之物」，也提供构成 factory、manufacture、factitious 的词尾。

items.en: The earliest English records use the word in anatomy and medicine for structures produced by disease or by technique, a sense close to the modern false-result reading.
items.cn: 最早的英语记录把它用在解剖学与医学中，指由疾病或技术造成的结构，这一用法接近现代「假结果」的读法。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word was applied to the objects of ancient craft, and that museum sense now dominates everyday use.
items.cn: 十九世纪起，这个词被用于古代工艺的制品，这一博物馆义如今在日常使用中占主导。

items.en: American usage settled on artifact, British usage on artefact; both spellings continue the same Latin source and mean the same thing.
items.cn: 美式用法定为 artifact，英式用法定为 artefact；两种拼写都延续同一拉丁来源，意思相同。

items.en: Source uncertain: no attested Latin noun artifactus exists, so the English word is a later combination rather than a direct borrowing, and dictionaries do not name the first author who used it.
items.cn: 来源不确定：拉丁语中并无已证实的名词 artifactus，因此这个英语词属后世组合，而非直接借词；辞书也没有指出最早使用它的作者。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same Latin stock of skill and making; the second group holds words for objects close in meaning but not made by human hands in the same sense.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「技艺与制作」词干的词；第二组是意思相近、但并非同样意义上由人手制作的物件。

entries.definition: The same word in British spelling; it is a variant, not a separate term with its own history.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的英式拼写，只是变体，并非另有来历的独立术语。

entries.definition: From ars plus facere as well, but it names a clever device or a trick, not the object produced.
entries.definitionCN: 同样由 ars 加 facere 构成，但它指巧妙的装置或诡计，而不是做出来的物件。

entries.definition: The adjective describing something made by skill rather than occurring naturally; it does not name a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述由技艺而非自然生成的事物；它并不指称物件本身。

entries.definition: An object that survives from an earlier time, often valued for its age or holiness; the stress is on survival, not on being made.
entries.definitionCN: 从更早时代留存下来的物件，常因年代或神圣性受珍视；重点是「留存」，而非「被制作」。

entries.definition: An item kept as a sample of its kind for study; a specimen may be natural, while an artifact must be made.
entries.definitionCN: 作为同类样本保存以供研究的物件；样本可以是天然的，而人工制品必须由人制作。

entries.definition: Any thing that can be handled; it makes no claim about who made it or why it matters.
entries.definitionCN: 任何可拿取的物；它不主张由谁制作，也不说明为何重要。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real Latin pieces, the archaeology rule, the scientific reversal and the spelling split.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的拉丁成分、考古学的区分规则、科学义的反转，以及拼写分歧。

normal.en: ars, skill, plus factum, made: an artifact is literally a thing made by skill.
normal.cn: ars「技艺」加 factum「做成之物」：artifact 字面就是「以技艺做成的东西」。

normal.en: The same ars stock gives art, artifice, artificial and artifact; the same facere stock gives factory, manufacture and factitious.
normal.cn: 同出 ars 的有 art、artifice、artificial、artifact；同出 facere 的有 factory、manufacture、factitious。

normal.en: Field rule: if it can be bagged and numbered, it is an artifact; if it stays in the ground, it is a feature.
normal.cn: 田野规则：能装袋编号的叫器物；留在地里不动的叫遗迹。

normal.en: The scientific sense reverses the maker: there the instrument makes the mark, not the hand.
normal.cn: 科学义把制作者换了人：那里留下痕迹的是仪器，不是手。

normal.en: American artifact, British artefact; the meaning does not change with the spelling.
normal.cn: 美式 artifact，英式 artefact；意思不随拼写改变。

abstract.en: Abstractly, an artifact is anything a system adds to its own picture, including the distortion in the lens.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，artifact 是任何系统添进自身图景的东西，包括镜头里的畸变。

abstract.en: Every made thing carries a signature of its maker, which is why artifacts can be read as evidence.
abstract.cn: 每一件人造之物都带着制作者的签名，正因如此器物才能被当作证据来读。

abstract.en: The word keeps asking one question: was this shaped, or did it grow?
abstract.cn: 这个词始终在追问一件事：它是被塑造的，还是自己长成的？

examples.en: Radiocarbon dating placed the artifact at about three thousand years old.
examples.cn: 放射性碳测年把这件器物的年代定在约三千年前。

examples.en: The ring around the star in the image is an optical artifact, not a real structure.
examples.cn: 图像中恒星周围的光环是光学伪影，并非真实结构。

examples.en: Researchers must separate the artifact of the measuring device from the signal they want.
examples.cn: 研究者必须把测量仪器造成的伪影与真正想要的信号区分开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「艺术（art）+ 事实（fact）」——用艺术手艺做出来的实体 → 人工制品、文物

root: 拉丁 ars/artis「技艺」的夺格 arte「以技艺」+ factum「做成之物」（facere「制作」的目的动名词）；字面为「以技艺做成之物」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: a hand works material into a thing, and that thing is then dug up, faked by an instrument, produced by a system and finally owned as heritage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：人手把材料做成物件，这件物件随后被挖出、被仪器伪造、被系统产出，最后被当作遗产拥有。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand shaping stone, and the shaped stone outliving the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把石头打出形状，而被塑形的石头比手活得更久。

branches.en: MAKING ITSELF: craft applied to stuff is the root sense, and the broad contrast with nature is only its widest form.
branches.cn: 制作本身：技艺作用于材料是根义，与自然相对只是它最宽的形态。

branches.en: THE KEPT OBJECT: once lifted and numbered, a made thing becomes evidence, and once owned it becomes heritage.
branches.cn: 被保存的物件：被取出编号后成为证据，被拥有后成为遗产。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT MAKES TOO: the method adds a mark of its own, and the same logic explains digital faults.
branches.cn: 仪器也在制作：方法自己添上一道痕迹，同一逻辑解释了数字瑕疵。

branches.en: THE MEDIUM LEAVES TRACES: lens, film and sensor write on the image as surely as a hand writes on clay.
branches.cn: 介质留下痕迹：镜头、胶片与传感器在影像上书写，如同手在陶土上书写。

branches.en: THE FRAME INVENTS: abstracted once more, any system can manufacture an effect that vanishes when its frame is changed.
branches.cn: 框架会发明：再抽象一层，任何系统都能制造出换掉框架就消失的效应。

intro.en: Artifact is built from two Latin pieces that also build a large English family, so the word can be read morpheme by morpheme: skill plus making.
intro.cn: artifact 由两个拉丁成分构成，这两个成分还构成一大批英语词，因此可以逐语素读出：技艺加制作。

latinIntro.en: Latin ars, genitive artis, gives art, artist, artifice and artificial; Latin facere gives fact, factory, manufacture and factitious. The artifact family sits exactly where the two meet.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ars（属格 artis）衍生 art、artist、artifice、artificial；拉丁 facere 衍生 fact、factory、manufacture、factitious。artifact 一族正处在这两条线的交点上。

items.example: Ars in Latin covered both craft and cunning.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 ars 兼指手艺与机巧。

items.structure: art (English, from Latin ars through Old French)
items.meaning: the practice of skill, especially in making or expressing
items.meaningCN: 技艺的实践，尤指制作或表达上的
items.example: The art of stone working changed human history.
items.exampleCN: 石作技艺改变了人类历史。

items.structure: artifice (Latin ars + facere, a thing made by skill)
items.meaning: a clever device or a trick
items.example: The lock was an artifice of great subtlety.
items.exampleCN: 这把锁是一件极为精巧的装置。

items.meaning: made by human skill rather than occurring naturally
items.meaningCN: 由人的技艺制成而非自然生成
items.example: Artificial light changed the working day.
items.exampleCN: 人造光改变了工作日。

items.structure: facere (Latin verb, to make, to do)
items.example: Facere is the source of many English -fect and -fact words.
items.exampleCN: facere 是许多英语 -fect 与 -fact 词的来源。

items.structure: factum (Latin supine of facere, a thing made)
items.example: Factum gave English fact its earliest sense of a deed.
items.exampleCN: factum 给英语 fact 最早的「行为、事迹」义。

items.structure: fact (English, from Latin factum, a thing done)
items.meaning: something that is the case, originally a deed
items.example: The fact was recorded before any theory was proposed.
items.exampleCN: 事实在提出任何理论之前就已被记录。

items.structure: factory (Latin factorium, a place of making)
items.meaning: a building where goods are made
items.example: The factory produced pottery for the whole province.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂为全省生产陶器。

items.meaning: to make goods, originally by hand
items.meaningCN: 制造货物，原指用手制作
items.example: They manufacture the blades from local flint.
items.exampleCN: 他们用当地燧石制造石刃。

items.meaning: artificially produced, often in a false way
items.meaningCN: 人为制造的，常带虚假意味
items.example: A factitious glow came from the treated surface.
items.exampleCN: 处理过的表面发出一种人为的光。

latinEntries.structure: facere (Latin verb, to make, to do)

definition_zh: 理论上；按理说；从原理上讲；在假设情形下
definition_en: according to theory or principle, especially when practice may differ
core_image: 纸上算出的箭头与真实机器里实际走出的轨迹并排摆放，两者并不重合
scene: 这里指「理论上」。 Theoretically, the bridge can carry twice that load, but nobody has tested it.
sceneCN: 这里 theoretically 指「理论上」（第 2 个义项：按原理推算应当如此，实际未必）；句意：理论上这座桥能承受两倍的荷载，但没人测试过。图中可辨识物件：计算纸带、桥梁受力示意图、未启用的测试装置。

pos.zh: 理论上；按理说；从原理上（由 theoretical 加 -ly 构成，常用于「理应如此，实际未必」的对比）

senses.title: In Theory, Not in Practice
senses.definition: according to theory rather than practice
senses.definitionCN: 依据理论而非实践
senses.example: Theoretically the method is elegant; in the lab it fails.
senses.exampleCN: 理论上这个方法很优雅；在实验室里它却行不通。
senses.why: The adverb marks the side of the theory-practice pair. It says the statement is judged by principles, leaving open what happens when the method meets real conditions.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词标出「理论—实践」这一对里的理论一侧：它表示该陈述是按原理来评判的，至于方法遇到现实条件会怎样，则留着不说。

senses.title: In Principle
senses.definition: as reasoning says it should be
senses.definitionCN: 按推理所说应当如此
senses.example: Theoretically, the Bridge can carry twice that load.
senses.exampleCN: 按理说，这座桥能承受两倍的荷载。
senses.why: Here the word invites you to follow the calculation to its conclusion. It is a claim about what the numbers allow, not a report of what has been observed.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词邀请你顺着计算走到结论；它主张的是数字所容许的范围，而不是报告已经观察到的事实。

senses.title: Under a Supposition
senses.titleCN: 在假设情形下：假定前提成立
senses.definition: within a case that is assumed rather than actual
senses.definitionCN: 在被假定而非实际的情形之中
senses.example: Theoretically, with no friction, the puck would never stop.
senses.exampleCN: 在无摩擦的假设下，冰球理论上永远不会停下。
senses.why: A supposition sets the conditions. The adverb tells the listener that the conclusion holds inside those conditions only, so the missing friction is not an oversight but a premise.
senses.whyCN: 假设先设定条件；这个副词告诉听者，结论只在那些条件之内成立，因此被忽略的摩擦不是疏忽，而是前提。

senses.title: By Abstract Reasoning
senses.definition: by reasoning with abstractions rather than with observed cases
senses.definitionCN: 以抽象概念而非观察到的个案进行推理
senses.example: Theoretically, any language can express any idea.
senses.exampleCN: 从抽象推理上说，任何语言都能表达任何观念。
senses.why: The step here is from particular examples to a general claim. The adverb marks that move, which is legitimate in itself but must be defended on its own terms.
senses.whyCN: 这里的一步是从具体例子推向一般主张；这个副词标出的正是这一步——它本身是正当的，但必须按自身的规则来论证。

senses.title: As Predicted by a Model
senses.titleCN: 按模型推算：模型给出什么
senses.definition: as a model or calculation predicts
senses.definitionCN: 按照模型或计算所预测的
senses.example: Theoretically, the population should double in nine years.
senses.exampleCN: 按模型推算，该种群应在九年内翻倍。
senses.why: A model produces numbers whether or not the world cooperates. The adverb attributes the figure to the model, which protects the speaker if reality disagrees.
senses.whyCN: 模型无论现实是否配合都会给出数字；这个副词把数值归到模型名下，从而在现实不符时保护说话者。

senses.title: Expected but Not Guaranteed
senses.titleCN: 按理论推断：与实际常有落差
senses.definition: as one would expect from theory, often with the hint that reality differs
senses.definitionCN: 按理论推想应当如此，常暗示现实未必
senses.example: Theoretically it should work by Friday; last time it took a month.
senses.exampleCN: 按理论它周五前该能用了；上次却用了一个月。
senses.why: The contrast is supplied by the second clause. The adverb sets up an expectation that the speaker already suspects will not be met, a very common conversational use.
senses.whyCN: 对比由后半句提供；这个副词先立起一个期待，而说话者已怀疑它不会实现——这是口语里极常见的用法。

senses.title: On the Theory Side
senses.definition: with respect to the theoretical branch of a subject
senses.definitionCN: 就某一学科的理论分支而言
senses.example: The paper is theoretically strong but empirically thin.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文在理论方面很强，实证方面却很单薄。
senses.why: Here the adverb locates a work inside the theory branch and praises or criticizes it by that standard, not by the standard of data collection.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个副词把一项工作定位在理论分支之内，并按那一分支的标准来褒贬，而不是按数据收集的标准。

senses.title: In Idealized Terms
senses.titleCN: 以理想化的方式：删繁就简
senses.definition: in idealized terms that omit complicating detail
senses.definitionCN: 以省略复杂细节的理想化方式
senses.example: Theoretically, the two species never compete; in the field they do.
senses.exampleCN: 理想化地说，这两个物种从不竞争；在野外它们却竞争。
senses.why: Idealization removes friction, weather and history. The adverb flags that the clean result belongs to the simplified picture, which is useful precisely because it can then be tested against the messy one.
senses.whyCN: 理想化删去摩擦、天气与历史；这个副词提示干净的结果属于简化后的图景——它的用处恰恰在于随后可以用杂乱的现实来检验它。

intro.en: Theoretically is theoretical plus -ly, and theoretical descends from Greek theōria 'a looking, contemplation' through Latin theoreticus. The first English use is dated only approximately.
intro.cn: theoretically 由 theoretical 加 -ly 构成，而 theoretical 经拉丁 theoreticus 上溯希腊 theōria「观看、沉思」。英语首见年代仅为约数。

items.en: Theoros is generally explained as 'one who looks on', from thea 'a view' and horan 'to see'. It named a spectator and also an envoy sent to consult an oracle and report what he had seen.
items.cn: theoros 一般解释为「观看的人」，由 thea「景象」与 horan「看见」构成；它既指观众，也指被派去求神谕并回报所见之事的使者。

items.en: The abstract noun theōria meant 'the act of viewing, contemplation'. Philosophy gave it a technical sense: the mind's quiet inspection of eternal truths, in contrast with action.
items.cn: 抽象名词 theōria 意为「观看的行为、沉思」。哲学赋予它专门含义：心灵对永恒真理的安静审视，与行动形成对照。

items.en: Latin theoreticus gave English theoretic in the sixteenth century and theoretical in the seventeenth. Adding -ly produced theoretically. The exact first citation of the adverb is not firmly dated.
items.cn: 拉丁 theoreticus 在十六世纪给出英语 theoretic，十七世纪给出 theoretical；加 -ly 产生 theoretically。副词的确切首见书证没有可靠年代。

items.en: Modern English often uses theoretically at the front of a sentence as a comment adverb, meaning 'judging by theory'. The habit grew with scientific and academic writing.
items.cn: 现代英语常把 theoretically 放在句首作评注副词，意思是「按理论判断」。这一习惯随科学与学术写作而发展。

items.en: The Greek pair theōria and praxis still shapes the English pair theoretical and practical. The adverb therefore always implies a counterpart: some practice against which the reasoning could be checked.
items.cn: 希腊语 theōria 与 praxis 这对概念至今仍塑造英语 theoretical 与 practical 这对词。因此这个副词总暗含一个对应项：某种可以用来检验推理的实践。

note.en: The first group separates the adverb from its adjective and from a different adverb of whole systems. The second holds near-synonyms that hedge in different ways.
note.cn: 第一组区分该副词与其形容词，以及与「整体系统」有关的另一个副词；第二组是不同程度留有余地的近义词。

entries.definition: The adjective describing knowledge based on principles. It modifies a noun, while the adverb modifies the act of judging or speaking.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述以原理为基础的知识；它修饰名词，而副词修饰判断或陈述的动作。

entries.definition: In practice, or almost. It occupies the other half of the theory-practice pair and can also mean 'almost'.
entries.definitionCN: 在实践中，或「几乎」；它占据理论—实践这一对的另一半，也可表示「几乎」。

entries.definition: In a way that affects the whole system or body. It is unrelated in meaning to the theory-practice contrast.
entries.definitionCN: 以影响整个系统或全身的方式；与理论—实践这一对立在意义上无关。

entries.definition: As far as the basic rule goes. It is the plain-English equivalent of the second sense and carries the same unspoken 'but'.
entries.definitionCN: 就基本原则而言；它是第 2 个义项的平实英语说法，并且带着同样未说出口的「但是」。

entries.definition: At the level of ideas or definitions. It is about how concepts are formed, not about whether a result can be realized.
entries.definitionCN: 在观念或定义的层面上；它讲概念如何构成，而不讲结果能否实现。

entries.definition: Under an assumed condition. It is more openly fictional than theoretically and invites a conditional sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 在假定条件下；比 theoretically 更坦率地表示虚构，常引出条件句。

entries.definition: According to what something is called, not what it is. It is close to sense 6 but stresses labels rather than reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 按照名称上所说，而非实际如何；接近第 6 个义项，但强调的是名义标签而非推理。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: theoretical + -ly: judging a thing by principle rather than by trial.
normal.cn: theoretical + -ly：按原理而不是靠试验来评判一件事。

normal.en: The family runs theory, theoretical, theoretically, theorist, theorize, theorem.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 theory、theoretical、theoretically、theorist、theorize、theorem。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: theoretically possible, theoretically speaking, theoretically infinite.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：理论上可能、从理论上说、理论上无限。

normal.en: The natural partner is practically: theory says yes, practice says wait.
normal.cn: 天然搭档是 practically：理论说可以，实践说再等等。

normal.en: Sentence-initial Theoretically, ... is a comment on the whole claim that follows.
normal.cn: 句首的 Theoretically, ... 是对后面整个主张的评注。

abstract.en: Picture a straight line drawn with a ruler beside a path that curves around every stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一条用尺画出的直线，旁边是一条绕过每块石头的弯曲小路。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe that works perfectly until the kitchen runs out of one ingredient.
abstract.cn: 想象一份配方完美可行，直到厨房少了一样原料。

abstract.en: Picture a sign that reads 'should be fine' in a building where nothing has been switched on yet.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋还没通电的楼里挂着「应该没问题」的牌子。

examples.en: Theoretically, the reaction needs only a trace of catalyst.
examples.cn: 理论上，这个反应只需要极少量催化剂。

examples.en: Theoretically speaking, no ecosystem can grow without a limit.
examples.cn: 从理论上说，没有哪个生态系统能无限制地增长。

examples.en: The plan is theoretically justified, yet its cost makes it unusable.
examples.cn: 该计划在理论上说得通，但成本使它无法实施。

dict_mnemonic.text: theoretical（理论的）+ ly（以……方式）→ 以理论的方式 → 理论上

root: 希腊 thea「景象」+ horan「看见」→ theoros「观看者」→ theōria「观看、沉思」→ 拉丁 theoreticus → 英语 theoretical → theoretically。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all judge by principle rather than by trial, but the source of the principle varies: theory itself, a calculation, a supposition, abstract reasoning, a model, an expectation, a branch of study or an idealized picture.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都以原理而非试验来评判，但原理的来源各不相同：理论本身、计算、假设、抽象推理、模型、期待、学科分支或理想化图景。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a computed arrow beside the path a real machine actually takes.
core.cn: 核心意象：计算出的箭头与真实机器实际走出的轨迹并排摆放。

branches.en: THE THEORY SIDE: the adverb either contrasts with practice or locates a work inside the theoretical branch.
branches.cn: 理论一侧：该副词或与实践相对，或把一项工作定位在理论分支之内。

branches.en: WHAT THE RULE ALLOWS: a calculation or a model states what follows from its own assumptions.
branches.cn: 规则容许什么：计算或模型陈述的是从其自身假定推出的结果。

branches.en: CONDITIONS AND IDEALIZATION: a supposition or a simplified picture sets the boundary inside which the claim holds.
branches.cn: 条件与理想化：假设或简化图景设定了主张成立的边界。

branches.en: THE ABSTRACT STEP: moving from examples to a general claim, which must be argued in its own terms.
branches.cn: 抽象的一步：从例子推向一般主张，而这一步必须按自身规则论证。

branches.en: THE GAP: the adverb often raises an expectation the speaker already expects reality to break.
branches.cn: 落差：这个副词常立起一个期待，而说话者已料到现实会打破它。

intro.en: Theoretically is a Greek-derived adjective with an English adverb ending: a sight-root, a noun of contemplation, an adjective suffix and -ly.
intro.cn: theoretically 是希腊来源的形容词加英语副词词尾：一个「观看」词根、一个表示沉思的名词、一个形容词后缀，以及 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Greek theōria gave Latin theoreticus and English theory, theoretical, theoretic, theoretically, theorist and theorem. The sight-root also appears in theater, which arrived by another route.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 theōria 给出拉丁 theoreticus，以及英语 theory、theoretical、theoretic、theoretically、theorist、theorem。同一个「观看」词根也见于 theater，但那个词走的是另一条路径。

items.example: Theoretically, the tank holds a thousand litres.
items.exampleCN: 理论上，这个罐子能装一千升。

items.example: The theoretical gain was never measured.
items.exampleCN: 理论上的增益从未被测量。

items.example: The theory explains why the two curves cross.
items.exampleCN: 该理论解释了这两条曲线为何相交。

items.example: The theorist works mostly with pencil and paper.
items.exampleCN: 这位理论家主要用纸笔工作。

items.meaning: to reason in terms of theory
items.example: They theorized long before any data arrived.
items.exampleCN: 他们早在任何数据到来之前就做了理论推想。

items.example: The theorem follows from two simple axioms.
items.exampleCN: 该定理由两条简单公理推出。

items.example: Theoretic debate filled the early journals.
items.exampleCN: 早期的期刊充满理论争论。

items.example: The lighting gave the hall a theatrical air.
items.exampleCN: 灯光给大厅带来一种舞台气氛。

latinEntries.structure: theōria, -ae (f., first declension, Greek loan in Latin)

latinEntries.meaning: a thing viewed; a proved proposition
latinEntries.meaningCN: 所见之物；已证明的命题

definition_zh: 互动的；交互式的；相互作用的；（设备或软件）可双向操作的
definition_en: acting on or responding to one another; involving two-way communication between people, or between a user and a machine that reacts to input
core_image: 手指点向屏幕，屏幕随即亮起并改变画面：一方动作，另一方马上回应
scene: 博物馆里，孩子伸手触碰展项屏幕，讲解员说这是交互式展项。 This exhibit is interactive, so the picture changes when you touch the screen.
sceneCN: 这里 interactive 是「交互式的」（第 3 个义项：设备对用户操作作出回应）；句意：这个展项是交互式的，触摸屏幕画面就会改变。

pos.zh: 互动的；交互式的（指双方来回回应，尤指人机之间）
相互作用的；相互影响的（用于描述过程、关系或系统）

collocations.zh: 互动展项；交互式显示屏

senses.title: Mutually acting
senses.definition: describing two or more things that act on each other and produce effects on both sides
senses.definitionCN: 描述两个或更多事物彼此施力、双方都受影响
senses.example: The study models interactive forces inside the cell.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究对细胞内部相互作用的力进行建模。
senses.why: Interactive is interaction turned into an adjective: inter- 'between' + act, from Latin agere 'to do'. The -ive suffix makes it a property, so the word says that a relationship has two active ends rather than one.
senses.whyCN: interactive 是 interaction 转成的形容词：inter-“在……之间”+ act，源自拉丁语 agere“做”。-ive 后缀把它变成一种属性，因此这个词表示一种关系有两个活动的端点，而不是一个。

senses.title: Involving people in exchange
senses.definition: describing communication in which people speak, listen, and respond to one another
senses.definitionCN: 描述人们彼此说、听、回应的交流
senses.example: The workshop was interactive, with every participant speaking twice.
senses.exampleCN: 这场工作坊是互动式的，每位参与者都发言了两次。
senses.why: Applied to people, the adjective describes a pattern rather than a device: turns alternate, and each turn depends on the last. It contrasts with 'lecture-style', where information flows one way.
senses.whyCN: 用在人身上时，这个形容词描述一种模式而非设备：轮次交替，每一轮都取决于上一轮。它与“讲座式”相对，后者信息只朝一个方向流。

senses.title: Responding to user input
senses.titleCN: （设备）对用户操作作出回应的
senses.definition: describing a device, screen, or program that reacts immediately to what a user does
senses.definitionCN: 描述对用户操作立即作出反应的设备、屏幕或程序
senses.example: The new kiosk is fully interactive and works without a keyboard.
senses.exampleCN: 新的自助终端完全交互式，无需键盘即可使用。
senses.why: This is the computing sense recorded in the 1960s: a program is interactive when it waits for input and answers it. The machine is cast as a partner in the loop, not as a one-way display.
senses.whyCN: 这是 1960 年代记录的计算机义：程序等待输入并回应输入，就是交互式的。机器被设定为回路中的伙伴，而不是单向的显示器。

senses.title: Open to audience participation
senses.definition: describing an exhibition, performance, or broadcast that invites the audience to take part
senses.definitionCN: 描述邀请观众参与其中的展览、演出或节目
senses.example: The gallery's interactive installation lets visitors draw on the walls.
senses.exampleCN: 美术馆的互动装置让观众可以在墙上作画。
senses.why: Museums and media borrowed the computing sense and shifted the partner from a machine to an audience. What stays constant is the invitation: the work is unfinished until someone acts.
senses.whyCN: 博物馆与媒体借用了计算机义，把伙伴从机器换成了观众。不变的是那份邀请：作品在有人行动之前尚未完成。

senses.title: Two-way in teaching
senses.definition: describing teaching in which students ask, answer, and act rather than only listen
senses.definitionCN: 描述学生提问、回答、行动而不只是听讲的教学
senses.example: Interactive teaching raised the number of questions students asked.
senses.exampleCN: 互动教学提高了学生提问的数量。
senses.why: Education reform used the adjective as a slogan against passive instruction. The word measures the number of directions in which information travels, so a lecture with questions counts as interactive.
senses.whyCN: 教育改革把这个形容词当作反对被动灌输的口号。这个词衡量信息传播的方向数，所以带提问的讲授也算 interactive。

senses.title: Interactive mode in computing
senses.definition: describing a program or session that accepts commands and returns results immediately instead of running a fixed batch
senses.definitionCN: 描述立即接受命令并返回结果、而非按固定批处理运行的程序或会话
senses.example: Switch to interactive mode to test each query as you type it.
senses.exampleCN: 切换到交互模式，就可以边输入边测试每条查询。
senses.why: In computing, 'interactive' contrasts with 'batch': a batch job runs alone, while an interactive one waits and answers. The technical difference is where the human sits inside the loop.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域里 interactive 与 batch（批处理）相对：批处理任务独自运行，交互式任务则等待并回答。技术差别就在于人坐在回路的哪个位置。

senses.title: Mutually influencing in a process
senses.definition: describing a process or relationship in which each change produces a further change in the other party
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种过程或关系，其中一方的变化又引起另一方变化
senses.example: The report describes an interactive cycle of warming and melting.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了一个变暖与融化的相互影响循环。
senses.why: Here the adjective describes feedback rather than interface: warming melts ice, melting darkens the surface, darkening speeds warming. The word names the circle, not any single step.
senses.whyCN: 这里的形容词描述反馈而非界面：变暖融冰，融冰使地表变暗，变暗又加速变暖。这个词命名的是圆圈，而不是任何单一步骤。

senses.title: Playable in games and media
senses.definition: describing entertainment in which the player's choices change what happens next
senses.definitionCN: 描述玩家的选择会改变后续情节的娱乐形式
senses.example: The novel became an interactive story in which readers choose the ending.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说变成了互动故事，读者可以选择结局。
senses.why: Games and digital fiction extend the computing sense to narrative: the work branches according to input. 'Interactive' here means that the audience has authority over the outcome, however small.
senses.whyCN: 游戏与数字小说把计算机义扩展到叙事：作品随输入分岔。这里的 interactive 意味着观众对结局拥有决定权，无论这权力多小。

intro.en: Interactive is the adjective of interact, itself a back-formation from interaction. The parts are still visible: inter- 'between' plus act, from Latin agere 'to do'. Its computing sense is a twentieth-century specialization of a nineteenth-century word.
intro.cn: interactive 是 interact 的形容词，而 interact 又是 interaction 的逆构词。成分仍清晰可见：inter-“在……之间”加 act，源自拉丁语 agere“做”。它的计算机义是 19 世纪旧词在 20 世纪的专业化延伸。

items.en: Latin agere 'to do, drive' supplied actus and actio. The preposition inter 'between' could combine with almost any verb, giving the pattern 'do something between two parties'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 agere“做、驱动”提供了 actus 与 actio。介词 inter“在……之间”几乎能与任何动词组合，形成“在两方之间做某事”的模式。

items.en: Interaction appeared in English natural philosophy, and the adjective interactive followed in the same decade with the sense 'mutually acting'. Early uses described forces, not people or machines.
items.cn: interaction 出现在英语自然哲学中，形容词 interactive 在同一时期跟进，义为“相互作用的”。早期用法描述的是力，而不是人或机器。

items.en: The adjective extended to human relations and to systems, often in the phrase 'interactive effects'. It remained a learned word, commoner in science than in daily speech.
items.cn: 这个形容词扩展到人际关系与系统，常出现在 interactive effects 这一说法中。它长期是学术词，在科学文本中比在日常口语中常见。

items.en: Computer science gave the word its decisive modern sense: a program is interactive if it accepts input and answers during the session. The term separated real-time work from batch processing.
items.cn: 计算机科学赋予这个词决定性的现代义：程序在会话中接受输入并回答，就是交互式的。这个术语把实时工作与批处理区分开来。

items.en: Museums, schools, and broadcasters adopted 'interactive' as a label for audience participation, extending the computer model of input and response to culture and education.
items.cn: 博物馆、学校与广播机构把 interactive 用作观众参与的标签，把输入与回应的计算机模型扩展到文化与教育。

items.en: Modern usage ranges from particle physics to touch screens. In every case the test is the same: does the other side answer, and does the answer change what happens next?
items.cn: 现代用法从粒子物理一直延伸到触摸屏。无论哪种情况，检验标准都一样：另一方是否回应，而回应是否改变接下来的发展？

note.en: The look-alike group separates adjectival forms built on agere with different prefixes; the near-meaning group separates words for responsiveness and participation.
note.cn: 形近组区分以 agere 为词根但前缀不同的形容词；近义组区分表示“有回应”与“可参与”的词。

entries.definition: responding to a stimulus, often chemically. The re- means 'back', so the word stresses reaction after an event rather than exchange between equals.
entries.definitionCN: 对刺激作出反应，常用于化学。re- 意为“回”，因此这个词强调事件之后的反应，而不是对等双方的交流。

entries.definition: not active. Here in- is a negating prefix attached to active; there is no second party and no exchange at all.
entries.definitionCN: 不活跃的。这里的 in- 是否定前缀，加在 active 上；不存在第二方，也完全没有交流。

entries.definition: relating to interaction as a process. It describes the study or structure of exchanges, not a device or person that responds.
entries.definitionCN: 与互动过程有关的。它描述交流的研究或结构，而不是会回应的设备或人。

entries.definition: quick to react to something. It stresses speed and attentiveness on one side; interactive stresses that both sides act.
entries.definitionCN: 反应迅速的。它强调一方的速度与关注；interactive 强调双方都在行动。

entries.definition: allowing movement or communication in both directions. It names the channel, while interactive names the responding behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 允许双向移动或通信的。它命名通道，而 interactive 命名回应行为。

entries.definition: involving people as active participants. It stresses membership and taking part, not the back-and-forth of response.
entries.definitionCN: 让人作为积极参与者的。它强调加入与参与，而不是来回的回应。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: the inter- + act pattern, the computing contrast with batch mode, and the everyday phrase interactive display.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：inter- + act 的构词模式、与批处理模式相对的计算机用法，以及日常说法 interactive display。

normal.en: inter- 'between' + act 'do' + -ive: something that keeps doing between two sides.
normal.cn: inter-“在……之间”+ act“做”+ -ive：一直在两方之间做的东西。

normal.en: If the screen answers your finger, it is interactive; if it only shows, it is not.
normal.cn: 屏幕回应你的手指，就是 interactive；只显示不回应，就不是。

normal.en: Batch mode runs alone; interactive mode waits for you — that is the difference the word marks.
normal.cn: 批处理模式独自运行；交互模式等你输入——这个词标记的正是这个差别。

normal.en: An interactive class is measured by how many directions talk travels, not by how loud the teacher is.
normal.cn: 互动课堂按话语传播的方向数来衡量，而不是按老师嗓门大小。

normal.en: An interactive exhibition is unfinished until a visitor touches it.
normal.cn: 互动展览在观众触碰之前都算未完成。

abstract.en: The word describes a loop with two live ends; remove either end and the adjective no longer applies.
abstract.cn: 这个词描述一个两端都活着的回路；去掉任一端，这个形容词就不再适用。

abstract.en: Response is the test: a thing is interactive only if what you do changes what it does next.
abstract.cn: 回应是检验标准：只有你的作为改变了它接下来的作为，它才算 interactive。

abstract.en: From particles to novels, the same shape recurs — action, answer, altered next action.
abstract.cn: 从粒子到小说，同一个形状反复出现——行动、回应、被改变的下一个行动。

examples.en: The museum added interactive exhibits that respond to visitors' movements.
examples.cn: 博物馆增设了能对观众动作作出反应的互动展项。

examples.en: Interactive learning produces more questions than a straight lecture.
examples.cn: 互动式学习比纯讲授产生更多提问。

examples.en: The software runs in interactive mode so users see results at once.
examples.cn: 这款软件以交互模式运行，用户可以立刻看到结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: “因它来爱克提舞”——它一来，两边就“克”着互动起来 → interactive 互动的、交互式的

root: inter-（在……之间）+ 拉丁语 agere/actum“做”+ -ive（形容词后缀）；字面义“在两者之间来回做的”，核心是“一方动作、另一方回应”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of interactive all describe a loop with two active ends: forces, people, devices, audiences, classes, programs, feedback cycles, and games. The word is a property, not an event — it says that answering is possible.
sensesIntro.cn: interactive 的八个义项都描述一个两端都在活动的回路：力、人、设备、观众、课堂、程序、反馈循环与游戏。这个词是一种属性，而不是一个事件——它说的是“回应是可能的”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger touches a screen and the screen changes at once; action and answer in one moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指触碰屏幕，屏幕立刻改变；动作与回应在同一瞬间。

branches.en: NATURAL PROCESS: forces and feedback cycles act on each other without any user.
branches.cn: 自然过程：力与反馈循环在没有任何使用者的情况下彼此作用。

branches.en: PEOPLE: conversation and two-way teaching depend on alternating turns.
branches.cn: 人：交谈与双向教学依赖轮次的交替。

branches.en: MACHINE: a device or program waits for input and answers it, in contrast with batch operation.
branches.cn: 机器：设备或程序等待输入并回应，与批处理运行相对。

branches.en: AUDIENCE: exhibitions and media invite the visitor to act and then answer that act.
branches.cn: 观众：展览与媒体邀请观众动手，再对这一动作作出回应。

branches.en: PLAY: choices branch the story, so the audience holds authority over the outcome.
branches.cn: 游戏：选择让故事分岔，观众因此对结局拥有决定权。

intro.en: Interactive is interact + -ive, and interact is a back-formation from interaction. The family therefore circles around Latin agere 'to do', with inter- 'between' added in English.
intro.cn: interactive 是 interact + -ive，而 interact 是 interaction 的逆构词。整个家族因此围绕拉丁语 agere“做”，并由英语加上 inter-“在……之间”。

latinIntro.en: Latin agere 'to do, drive' gives actus, actio, activus, and the frequentative agitare. The prefix inter- is a separate preposition; it was attached to English act, not inherited as a Latin compound.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 agere“做、驱动”给出 actus、actio、activus 与反复动词 agitare。前缀 inter- 是独立的介词，它是加在英语 act 上，而不是作为拉丁复合词继承下来的。

items.meaningCN: 互动的；交互式的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The exhibit is interactive.
items.exampleCN: 这个展项是互动式的。

items.example: Users interact with the map by dragging it.
items.exampleCN: 用户通过拖动地图与它互动。

items.meaningCN: 互动；相互作用（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: Interaction between the two systems is limited.
items.exampleCN: 这两个系统之间的交互很有限。

items.meaningCN: 以交互方式（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The data can be explored interactively.
items.exampleCN: 数据可以交互式地探索。

items.meaning: the degree to which something responds
items.meaningCN: 互动性；交互性（-ity 构成抽象名词）
items.example: Reviewers praised the app's interactivity.
items.exampleCN: 评论者称赞这款应用的互动性。

items.meaningCN: 互动程度（-ness 构成抽象名词）
items.example: The interactiveness of the lesson surprised the observers.
items.exampleCN: 这堂课的互动程度让观察者惊讶。

items.meaningCN: 非交互的；单向的（non- 表否定）
items.example: A noninteractive report cannot be filtered.
items.exampleCN: 非交互式报表无法筛选。

items.meaning: acting in response to a stimulus
items.example: The material is reactive to light.
items.exampleCN: 这种材料对光有反应。

items.meaning: a deed or the process of doing
items.example: Action followed the decision at once.
items.exampleCN: 决定之后立即付诸行动。

latinEntries.meaning: to do, drive, set in motion

definition_zh: 杂食动物；杂食者；兴趣广泛的人
definition_en: an animal that eats both plant and animal food, or a person with broadly varied tastes and interests
core_image: 一只熊一手扒开蚁巢、一手拽下浆果，嘴里既嚼昆虫也嚼果实
scene: 这里指「杂食动物」。 The bear is an omnivore that switches from berries in summer to salmon in autumn.
sceneCN: 这里 omnivore 指「杂食动物」（第 1 个义项：既吃植物也吃动物）；这只熊夏季吃浆果，秋季改吃鲑鱼。图中可辨识物件：熊、蚁巢、浆果、鲑鱼。

pos.zh: 杂食动物；杂食者；兴趣广泛的人（可数，复数 omnivores）

collocations.zh: 机会主义杂食者；遇到什么吃什么
文化杂食者；品味跨越高雅与通俗的人
数字杂食者；跨多种设备与平台使用内容的人

senses.title: Eating both plants and animals
senses.titleCN: 杂食动物：植物与动物通吃
senses.definition: an animal whose diet includes substantial amounts of both plant and animal material
senses.definitionCN: 指食物中植物与动物材料都占相当比重的动物
senses.example: The raccoon is an omnivore that takes fruit, insects and carrion.
senses.exampleCN: 浣熊是杂食动物，吃果实、昆虫与腐肉。
senses.why: The word fills the plus-plus dietary cell, defined by neither plant nor flesh alone but by both.
senses.whyCN: 这个词填补食性表格中「两者都吃」的格子，既不只靠植物也不只靠肉，而是两者兼有。

senses.title: The human omnivore
senses.titleCN: 人类杂食者：生理上适应混合饮食
senses.definition: a human considered as a species adapted to a mixed diet of plants and animal products
senses.definitionCN: 指从物种层面被看作适应植物与动物性混合饮食的人类
senses.example: As an omnivore, the human gut can use both grains and meat.
senses.exampleCN: 作为杂食者，人的肠道既能利用谷物也能利用肉类。
senses.why: The label is used in nutrition and anthropology to describe a species-level capacity, not an individual choice.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签在营养学与人类学中描述物种层面的能力，而非个人选择。

senses.title: Opportunistic omnivore
senses.titleCN: 机会主义杂食者：随资源变化切换
senses.definition: an omnivore whose diet shifts with whatever is available, rather than following a fixed preference
senses.definitionCN: 指食性随可得资源变化、而非遵循固定偏好的杂食动物
senses.example: The fox is an opportunistic omnivore that follows the fruit season.
senses.exampleCN: 狐狸是机会主义杂食者，跟着果实季节改变食物。
senses.why: Flexibility is the point: the same animal can live through seasons when one food source fails.
senses.whyCN: 灵活性是关键：当一种食物来源失败时，同一种动物仍能熬过季节。

senses.title: Member of a feeding guild
senses.titleCN: 取食集团成员：生态学分类单位
senses.definition: in community ecology, an omnivore as a member of a guild that feeds at several trophic levels
senses.definitionCN: 群落生态学中指作为在多个营养级取食的集团成员的杂食动物
senses.example: Omnivores link the plant and animal channels of the food web.
senses.exampleCN: 杂食动物连接食物网中的植物通道与动物通道。
senses.why: Omnivores complicate the tidy trophic pyramid, because one species occupies several levels at once.
senses.whyCN: 杂食动物让整齐的营养金字塔变复杂，因为一个物种同时占据多个层级。

senses.title: Gut generalist
senses.titleCN: 消化道泛化：酶与菌群兼顾两类食物
senses.definition: an omnivore defined by a digestive system able to handle both plant fibre and animal protein
senses.definitionCN: 指消化道能够同时处理植物纤维与动物蛋白的杂食动物
senses.example: The omnivore's midgut carries enzymes for starch as well as for protein.
senses.exampleCN: 杂食者的中肠既带淀粉酶也带蛋白酶。
senses.why: The class is physiological as well as behavioural: the gut must be a compromise between two diets.
senses.whyCN: 这一类既是行为类别也是生理类别：消化道必须是两种食性的折中。

senses.title: Cultural omnivore
senses.titleCN: 文化杂食者：品味跨越雅俗
senses.definition: in sociology, a person who consumes both highbrow and popular culture rather than sticking to one tier
senses.definitionCN: 社会学中指既消费高雅文化也消费通俗文化、不固守单一层级的人
senses.example: The survey found that cultural omnivores attended both opera and football.
senses.exampleCN: 调查发现文化杂食者既看歌剧也看足球。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the dietary word because taste is treated as a menu with many courses.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用饮食词汇，因为品味被当作有许多菜目的菜单。

senses.title: Digital omnivore
senses.titleCN: 数字杂食者：跨设备跨平台使用内容
senses.definition: in media research, a user who consumes content across several devices and platforms rather than one channel
senses.definitionCN: 媒介研究中指跨多种设备与平台、而非只用单一渠道消费内容的用户
senses.example: Digital omnivores move between phone, laptop and television in one evening.
senses.exampleCN: 数字杂食者一个晚上就在手机、笔记本与电视之间切换。
senses.why: Media studies extends the diet metaphor to attention, where the menu is platforms rather than plants and meat.
senses.whyCN: 媒介研究把饮食比喻扩展到注意力，菜单从植物与肉变成平台。

senses.title: A broadly curious person
senses.titleCN: 兴趣广泛者：什么都想读一点
senses.definition: an informal use for a person who reads, studies or tries many unrelated things
senses.definitionCN: 口语用法，指阅读、研究或尝试许多不相关事物的人
senses.example: He is an omnivore of ideas, equally at home in physics and poetry.
senses.exampleCN: 他是观念上的杂食者，在物理与诗歌中都自在。
senses.why: The dietary metaphor softens specialisation into appetite, which is why it is used approvingly.
senses.whyCN: 饮食比喻把专业化软化为胃口，因此这个说法常带赞许。

intro.en: Omnivore combines Latin omnis 'all' with vorare 'to devour'. The adjective omnivorous is older; the noun is generally treated as a later back-formation.
intro.cn: omnivore 由拉丁语 omnis「全部」与 vorare「吞食」构成。形容词 omnivorous 出现更早，名词一般认为是由它逆构而来。

items.en: Omnis meant all or every, and it also gives omnibus, omnipotent and omniscient.
items.cn: omnis 意为全部、每个，也是 omnibus、omnipotent、omniscient 的来源。

items.en: Vorare meant to devour, the same verb that closes herbivore and carnivore.
items.cn: vorare 意为吞食，与 herbivore、carnivore 结尾的动词相同。

items.en: Omnivorus was formed in scientific Latin as the adjective for a mixed diet. Its exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: omnivorus 在科学拉丁语中构成，作为混合食性的形容词；确切首用存疑。

items.en: English omnivorous is recorded in the seventeenth century. The exact first citation is uncertain, and the early uses may have been figurative.
items.cn: 英语 omnivorous 见于 17 世纪；确切首见书证存疑，早期用法可能已是比喻。

items.en: Omnivore as a noun is generally dated to the nineteenth century and treated as a back-formation from omnivorous, though the dating is not fixed.
items.cn: 名词 omnivore 一般认为出现在 19 世纪，被视为由 omnivorous 逆构而来，但年代并不确定。

items.en: Twentieth-century sociology and media studies formed cultural omnivore and digital omnivore, extending 'all' to tastes and platforms.
items.cn: 20 世纪的社会学与媒介研究造出文化杂食者与数字杂食者，把「全部」扩展到品味与平台。

note.en: The look-alike group is the three diet classes; the near-meaning group separates the broad eater from the flexible strategist.
note.cn: 形近组是三个食性类别；近义组区分广泛取食者与灵活策略者。

entries.definition: An animal that eats plants. It is the plant-only class, and the first element herba- marks the difference.
entries.definitionCN: 指以植物为食的动物。它是纯植食类别，前半 herba- 标出差别。

entries.definition: An animal that eats flesh. It is the flesh-only class, and omni- 'all' is what separates it from omnivore.
entries.definitionCN: 指以肉为食的动物。它是纯肉食类别，正是 omni-「全部」把它与杂食动物区分开。

entries.definition: The adjective form meaning mixed-diet. Omnivore is the noun, so a bear is an omnivore and has an omnivorous diet.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词形式，意为混合食性的。omnivore 是名词，因此熊是 omnivore，饮食是 omnivorous。

entries.definition: A species that uses many resources. It overlaps with omnivore but is broader, since a generalist may use many habitats without eating both plants and meat.
entries.definitionCN: 指利用多种资源的物种。它与杂食动物重叠但更宽，因为广适种可能利用多种生境却不吃植物与肉。

entries.definition: One that takes whatever chance offers. It describes behaviour, while omnivore describes diet.
entries.definitionCN: 指抓住任何机会者。它描述行为，而 omnivore 描述食性。

entries.definition: A technical adjective for feeding on many kinds of food, common in entomology. It is close to omnivorous but usually applied to invertebrates.
entries.definitionCN: 技术形容词，指取食多种食物，常见于昆虫学。它接近 omnivorous，但多用于无脊椎动物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: omni 'all' + vore 'eater': the eater of everything.
normal.cn: omni「全部」+ vore「吃……者」：什么都吃者。

normal.en: The family runs omnivorous, omnivory, omnibus, omnipotent and omniscient.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 omnivorous、omnivory、omnibus、omnipotent、omniscient。

normal.en: Typical phrases: opportunistic omnivore, omnivore diet, cultural omnivore, digital omnivore.
normal.cn: 典型搭配：机会主义杂食者、杂食食谱、文化杂食者、数字杂食者。

normal.en: The three classes share -vore; only the first element changes: herbi-, carni-, omni-.
normal.cn: 三个类别共享 -vore，只有前半变化：herbi-、carni-、omni-。

normal.en: The noun is generally a back-formation from the older adjective omnivorous.
normal.cn: 名词一般被视为由更早的形容词 omnivorous 逆构而来。

abstract.en: Picture a bear pulling berries with one paw and breaking into an anthill with the other.
abstract.cn: 想象熊一只爪摘浆果，另一只爪扒开蚁巢。

abstract.en: Picture a reader with opera tickets and a football scarf in the same bag.
abstract.cn: 想象一位读者的包里同时装着歌剧票与球迷围巾。

abstract.en: Picture one person switching between phone, laptop and television before dinner ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人在晚饭结束前就在手机、笔记本与电视之间切换。

examples.en: The raccoon is an omnivore that thrives beside human settlements.
examples.cn: 浣熊是杂食动物，在人类聚居地旁也能繁盛。

examples.en: As omnivores, humans can digest both starch and meat.
examples.cn: 作为杂食者，人类既能消化淀粉也能消化肉类。

examples.en: The survey described her as a cultural omnivore with wide tastes.
examples.cn: 调查把她描述为品味广泛的文化杂食者。

dict_mnemonic.text: omni（全部）+ vore（吃……者）→ 什么都吃 → omnivore 杂食动物

root: 拉丁 omnis「全部」+ vorare「吞食」→ 科学拉丁语 omnivorus；名词 omnivore 一般认为由形容词 omnivorous 逆构而来。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start with the mixed diet and extend 'all' to human physiology, opportunity, trophic levels, taste and platforms.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从混合食性出发，把「全部」扩展到人类生理、机会、营养级、品味与平台。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bear taking berries and ants with different paws.
core.cn: 核心意象：熊用两只不同的爪子取浆果与蚂蚁。

branches.en: DIET: the base sense is both plant and animal food.
branches.cn: 食性：基本义是植物与动物性食物兼有。

branches.en: PHYSIOLOGY: the human species and its gut are described as mixed-diet generalists.
branches.cn: 生理：人类物种及其肠道被描述为混合食性的泛化者。

branches.en: ECOLOGY: flexibility lets the animal follow seasons and link trophic levels.
branches.cn: 生态：灵活性让动物随季节变化，并连接不同营养级。

branches.en: MEDIA AND CURIOSITY: platforms and reading habits become menus with many courses.
branches.cn: 媒介与好奇心：平台使用与阅读习惯也成了多道菜的菜单。

branches.en: CULTURAL WIDENING: 'all' extends from food to a taste that crosses every level.
branches.cn: 文化扩展：「全部」从食物延伸到跨越各层级的口味。

intro.en: Omnivore is the 'all' branch of the -vore family, and the prefix omni- is productive far beyond diet.
intro.cn: omnivore 是 -vore 词族中的「全部」支，前缀 omni- 的能产性远超饮食领域。

latinIntro.en: Omnis is a Latin adjective meaning all; vorare is the eating verb; the noun ending was added in scientific Latin and later in English.
latinIntro.cn: omnis 是意为「全部」的拉丁形容词，vorare 是吃的动词，名词词尾先在科学拉丁语、后在英语中加上。

items.meaning: an animal eating both plants and flesh
items.meaningCN: 既吃植物也吃肉的动物
items.example: Every omnivore has a favourite food.
items.exampleCN: 每种杂食动物都有偏爱的食物。

items.example: The omnivorous reader takes any genre.
items.exampleCN: 这位杂食读者任何体裁都读。

items.meaning: the practice of eating both diets
items.example: Omnivory blurs the trophic pyramid.
items.exampleCN: 杂食性模糊了营养金字塔。

items.example: Omni- appears in omnibus and omnipotent.
items.exampleCN: omni- 出现在 omnibus 与 omnipotent 中。

items.meaning: for all; a collected volume; a bus
items.meaningCN: 为所有人的；汇编本；公共汽车
items.example: The publisher issued an omnibus of the trilogy.
items.exampleCN: 出版社推出了三部曲的合集。

items.example: Herbivores and omnivores share the meadow.
items.exampleCN: 植食动物与杂食动物共用这片草甸。

items.example: The carnivore takes only meat.
items.exampleCN: 这只食肉动物只吃肉。

items.meaning: a species or person using many resources
items.meaningCN: 利用多种资源的物种或人
items.example: The omnivore is a dietary generalist.
items.exampleCN: 杂食动物是食性上的泛化者。

items.example: Polyphagous insects damage many crops.
items.exampleCN: 多食性昆虫危害多种作物。

definition_zh: n. 钱箱，保险箱；（复数）资金，金库；天花板的凹格
definition_en: a strong box for money or valuables; funds; a sunken panel in a ceiling
core_image: 一只包铁的木箱，锁扣上落着铜绿
scene: 教堂里那只旧钱箱塞满了发黄的信件。 The old coffer in the church was full of yellowed letters.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：coffer 指钱箱；句意是教堂里那只旧钱箱塞满了发黄的信件。

pos.zh: 钱箱；保险箱
资金；金库（复数）

senses.title: A strong box for money
senses.definition: a strong box used to keep money or valuables
senses.definitionCN: 存放钱财或贵重物品的坚固箱子
senses.example: The coins were locked in a coffer.
senses.exampleCN: 硬币锁在钱箱里。
senses.why: Latin cophinus means a basket.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 cophinus 意为篮子。

senses.title: Funds or reserves
senses.definition: the money available to an organisation, in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 机构可支配的钱，常用复数
senses.example: The repairs drained the city coffers.
senses.exampleCN: 维修耗尽了市库。
senses.why: A box of money became the money itself.
senses.whyCN: 装钱的箱子成了钱本身。

senses.title: A sunken ceiling panel
senses.definition: a decorative recessed panel in a ceiling or vault
senses.definitionCN: 天花板或拱顶上的装饰性凹格
senses.example: The ceiling was decorated with stone coffers.
senses.exampleCN: 天花板装饰着石制凹格。
senses.why: The square recess looks like a small box.
senses.whyCN: 方形凹格像一个小箱子。

intro.en: Coffer comes from a Greek basket by way of a Latin and French chest.
intro.cn: coffer 从希腊语的篮子，经拉丁语与法语的箱子演变而来。

items.en: Kophinos means a basket.
items.cn: kophinos 意为篮子。

items.en: Cophinus keeps the basket sense.
items.cn: cophinus 保留篮子义。

items.en: Coffre means a chest or trunk.
items.cn: coffre 意为箱、柜。

items.en: Coffer names a strong chest for money.
items.cn: 十三世纪 coffer 指装钱的坚固箱子。

items.en: The plural means funds; the panel sense survives in architecture.
items.cn: 现代复数指资金，凹格义见于建筑。

note.en: The look-alike group is a near spelling; the near-meaning group names other money holders.
note.cn: 形近组是相近拼写；近义组列出其他钱箱与金库。

normalIntro.en: A coffer is a box that guards money, and the money inside it.
normalIntro.cn: coffer 是守钱的箱子，也指箱里的钱。

normal.en: Cophinus was a basket.
normal.cn: cophinus 曾是篮子。

normal.en: Coffre was a chest.
normal.cn: coffre 曾是箱子。

normal.en: A coffer locks coins away.
normal.cn: 钱箱把硬币锁起来。

normal.en: The plural means funds.
normal.cn: 复数指资金。

normal.en: Coffered ceilings have square hollows.
normal.cn: coffered 天花板有方形凹格。

abstract.en: A wooden mouth that keeps gold.

abstract.en: A city s savings in a box.

abstract.en: Squares of shadow on a ceiling.

examples.en: The treasure was kept in an iron coffer.
examples.cn: 财宝存放在铁箱里。

examples.en: Tax cuts emptied the public coffers.
examples.cn: 减税掏空了国库。

examples.en: The dome is decorated with painted coffers.
examples.cn: 穹顶装饰着彩绘凹格。

dict_mnemonic.text: 希腊 kophinos（篮子）→ 拉丁 cophinus → 法语 coffre（箱子）→ coffer 钱箱。

root: 希腊 kophinos（篮子）→ 拉丁 cophinus → 法语 coffre（箱子）→ 英语 coffer

sensesIntro.en: A basket became a chest, a chest became funds, a square recess looked like a box.
sensesIntro.cn: 篮子成了箱子，箱子成了资金，方凹格也像小箱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an iron-bound chest with a heavy lock

latinIntro.en: Latin cophinus is a basket, thesaurus is a treasure store, and capsa is a box.
